document.title: Washington State K-12 Science Standards

2B7A1B40DFE80131C26568A86D17958E.description: External features of animals and plants are used to classify them into groups.

2B79DB80DFE80131C26468A86D17958E.description: There are many different types of living things on Earth. Many of them are classified as plants or animals.

2B799B30DFE80131C26368A86D17958E.description: Some things are alive and others are not.

2B78C380DFE80131C26068A86D17958E.description: Humans can change natural habitats in ways that can be helpful or harmful for the plants and animals that live there.

2B7873D0DFE80131C25F68A86D17958E.description: A habitat supports the growth of many different plants and animals by meeting their basic needs of food, water, and shelter.

2B782AB0DFE80131C25E68A86D17958E.description: There are different kinds of natural areas, or habitats, where many different plants and animals live together.

2B7733A0DFE80131C25B68A86D17958E.description: Most plants have roots to get water and leaves to gather sunlight.

2B76B5D0DFE80131C25A68A86D17958E.description: Animals have various ways of obtaining food and water. Nearly all animals drink water or eat foods that contain water.

2B7663E0DFE80131C25968A86D17958E.description: Different animals use their body parts in different ways to see, hear, grasp objects, and move from place to place.

2B762370DFE80131C25868A86D17958E.description: The parts of a plant or animal appear different under a magnifier compared with the unaided eye.

2B75E1B0DFE80131C25768A86D17958E.description: All plants and animals have various external parts.

2B759C60DFE80131C25668A86D17958E.description: The human body is made up of various external parts.

2B750800DFE80131C25468A86D17958E.description: Structures and Functions of Living Organisms (LS1)

2B748900DFE80131C25268A86D17958E.description: Some Earth objects are made of more than one material.

2B7446F0DFE80131C25168A86D17958E.description: Earth materials include solid rocks, sand, soil, and water. These materials have different observable physical properties.

2B73FF30DFE80131C25068A86D17958E.description: Some objects occur in nature; others have been designed and processed by people.

2B7303F0DFE80131C24D68A86D17958E.description: The Moon can be seen sometimes during the day and sometimes during the night. The Moon appears to have different shapes on different days.

2B72B610DFE80131C24C68A86D17958E.description: The position of the Sun in the sky appears to change during the day.

2B727210DFE80131C24B68A86D17958E.description: Many things can be seen in the sky. Some change minute by minute, while others move in patterns that can be seen if they are observed day after day.

2B716370DFE80131C24768A86D17958E.description: Solids retain their shape regardless of the container they are in.

2B70EEC0DFE80131C24668A86D17958E.description: Liquids take the shape of the part of the container they occupy.

2B6FE450DFE80131C24368A86D17958E.description: Some forces act by touching and other forces can act without touching.

2B6F8240DFE80131C24268A86D17958E.description: A force is a push or a pull. Pushing or pulling can move an object. The speed an object moves is related to how strongly it is pushed or pulled.

2B6F1810DFE80131C24168A86D17958E.description: Motion is defined as a change in position over time.

2B6EB050DFE80131C24068A86D17958E.description: The position of an object can be described by locating it relative to another object or to the object's surroundings.

2B6D42A0DFE80131C23C68A86D17958E.description: Counting, classifying, and measuring can sometimes be helpful in solving a problem.

2B6D03C0DFE80131C23B68A86D17958E.description: A problem may have more than one acceptable solution.

2B6CC2C0DFE80131C23A68A86D17958E.description: Different materials are more suitable for some purposes than for other purposes.

2B6C8100DFE80131C23968A86D17958E.description: Common tools can be used to solve problems.

2B6B3540DFE80131C23568A86D17958E.description: All scientific observations must be reported honestly and accurately.

2B6AA660DFE80131C23368A86D17958E.description: Observations are more reliable if repeated, especially if repeated by different people.

2B6A67F0DFE80131C23268A86D17958E.description: Scientists report on their investigations to other scientists, using drawings and words.

2B69E160DFE80131C23068A86D17958E.description: Scientists develop explanations using recorded observations (evidence).

2B694D20DFE80131C22E68A86D17958E.description: Many children's toys are models that represent real things in some ways but not in other ways.

2B68C760DFE80131C22C68A86D17958E.description: Scientific investigations involve asking and trying to answer a question about the natural world by making and recording observations.

2B676850DFE80131C22768A86D17958E.description: Some objects can easily be taken apart and put back together again while other objects cannot be taken apart without damaging them (e.g., books, pencils, plants, and animals).

2B6719A0DFE80131C22668A86D17958E.description: Living and nonliving things are made of parts. People give names to the parts that are different from the name of the whole object, plant, or animal.

document.title: Washington Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

10B55340DFE8013191A668A86D17958E.description: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

10B50180DFE8013191A568A86D17958E.description: Express whole numbers as fractions, and recognize fractions that are equivalent to whole numbers.
comments: Example: express 3 in the form 3 = 3/1; recognize that 6/1 = 6.
Example: locate 4/4 and 1 at the same point of a number line diagram.

10B4BD70DFE8013191A468A86D17958E.description: Recognize and generate simple equivalent fractions, e.g., 1/2 = 2/4, 4/6 = 2/3). Explain why the fractions are equivalent, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

10B47540DFE8013191A368A86D17958E.description: Understand two fractions as equivalent (equal) if they are the same size, or the same point on a number line.

10B42570DFE8013191A268A86D17958E.description: Explain equivalence of fractions in special cases, and compare fractions by reasoning about their size.

10B3DDA0DFE8013191A168A86D17958E.description: Represent a fraction a/b on a number line diagram by marking off a lengths 1/b from 0. Recognize that the resulting interval has size a/b and that its endpoint locates the number a/b on the number line.

10B39110DFE8013191A068A86D17958E.description: Represent a fraction 1/b on a number line diagram by defining the interval from 0 to 1 as the whole and partitioning it into b equal parts. Recognize that each part has size 1/b and that the endpoint of the part based at 0 locates the number 1/b on the number line.

10B33FF0DFE80131919F68A86D17958E.description: Understand a fraction as a number on the number line; represent fractions on a number line diagram.

10B2FBE0DFE80131919E68A86D17958E.description: Understand a fraction 1/b as the quantity formed by 1 part when a whole is partitioned into b equal parts; understand a fraction a/b as the quantity formed by a parts of size 1/b.

10B2B460DFE80131919D68A86D17958E.description: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers.

comments: Grade 3 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8.
Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 100

10B21210DFE80131919B68A86D17958E.description: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas. Express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole.
comments: For example, partition a shape into 4 parts with equal area, and describe the area of each part as 1/4 of the area of the shape.

10B1C2C0DFE80131919A68A86D17958E.description: Understand that shapes in different categories (e.g., rhombuses, rectangles, and others) may share attributes (e.g., having four sides), and that the shared attributes can define a larger category (e.g., quadrilaterals). Recognize rhombuses, rectangles, and squares as examples of quadrilaterals, and draw examples of quadrilaterals that do not belong to any of these subcategories.

10B17000DFE80131919968A86D17958E.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

10B0DD90DFE80131919768A86D17958E.description: Solve real world and mathematical problems involving perimeters of polygons, including finding the perimeter given the side lengths, finding an unknown side length, and exhibiting rectangles with the same perimeter and different areas or with the same area and different perimeters.

10B09240DFE80131919668A86D17958E.description: Geometric measurement: recognize perimeter as an attribute of plane figures and distinguish between linear and area measures.

10B04D20DFE80131919568A86D17958E.description: Recognize area as additive. Find areas of rectilinear figures by decomposing them into non-overlapping rectangles and adding the areas of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real world problems.

10AFF900DFE80131919468A86D17958E.description: Use tiling to show in a concrete case that the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths a and b + c is the sum of a × b and a × c. Use area models to represent the distributive property in mathematical reasoning.

10AFB020DFE80131919368A86D17958E.description: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles with whole-number side lengths in the context of solving real world and mathematical problems, and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas in mathematical reasoning.

10AF6B70DFE80131919268A86D17958E.description: Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths by tiling it, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths.

10AF2180DFE80131919168A86D17958E.description: Relate area to the operations of multiplication and addition.

10AED300DFE80131919068A86D17958E.description: Measure areas by counting unit squares (square cm, square m, square in, square ft, and improvised units).

10AE9070DFE80131918F68A86D17958E.description: A plane figure which can be covered without gaps or overlaps by n unit squares is said to have an area of n square units.

10AE4A60DFE80131918E68A86D17958E.description: A square with side length 1 unit, called "a unit square," is said to have "one square unit" of area, and can be used to measure area.

10AE04F0DFE80131918D68A86D17958E.description: Recognize area as an attribute of plane figures and understand concepts of area measurement.

10ADBE30DFE80131918C68A86D17958E.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition.

10AC6A90DFE80131918868A86D17958E.description: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths using rulers marked with halves and fourths of an inch. Show the data by making a line plot, where the horizontal scale is marked off in appropriate units— whole numbers, halves, or quarters.

10AC1330DFE80131918768A86D17958E.description: Draw a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent a data set with several categories. Solve one- and two-step "how many more" and "how many less" problems using information presented in scaled bar graphs.
comments: For example, draw a bar graph in which each square in the bar graph might represent 5 pets.

10AD7080DFE80131918B68A86D17958E.description: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses of objects using standard units of grams (g), kilograms (kg), and liters (l). Add, subtract, multiply, or divide to solve one-step word problems involving masses or volumes that are given in the same units, e.g., by using drawings (such as a beaker with a measurement scale) to represent the problem.
comments: Excludes multiplicative comparison problems (problems involving notions of "times as much";
Excludes compound units such as cm³ and finding the geometric volume of a container.

10AD1810DFE80131918A68A86D17958E.description: Tell and write time to the nearest minute and measure time intervals in minutes. Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals in minutes, e.g., by representing the problem on a number line diagram.

10ACC720DFE80131918968A86D17958E.description: Solve problems involving measurement and estimation of intervals of time, liquid volumes, and masses of objects.

10AB2C20DFE80131918468A86D17958E.description: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of 10 in the range 10—90 (e.g., 9 × 80, 5 × 60) using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.

10AAE5C0DFE80131918368A86D17958E.description: Fluently add and subtract within 1000 using strategies and algorithms based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.

10AA9E00DFE80131918268A86D17958E.description: Use place value understanding to round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100.

comments: A range of algorithms may be used.
10AA4480DFE80131918168A86D17958E.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

10A9DDE0DFE80131918068A86D17958E.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten
comments: Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to whole numbers less than or equal to 1,000,000.

10A987B0DFE80131917F68A86D17958E.description: Identify arithmetic patterns (including patterns in the addition table or multiplication table), and explain them using properties of operations.
comments: For example, observe that 4 times a number is always even, and explain why 4 times a number can be decomposed into two equal addends.

10A93AB0DFE80131917E68A86D17958E.description: Solve two-step word problems using the four operations. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.
comments: This standard is limited to problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers; students should know how to perform operations in the conventional order when there are no parentheses to specify a particular order (Order of Operations).

10A8FA20DFE80131917D68A86D17958E.description: Solve problems involving the four operations, and identify and explain patterns in arithmetic.

10A8B6B0DFE80131917C68A86D17958E.description: Fluently multiply and divide within 100, using strategies such as the relationship between multiplication and division (e.g., knowing that 8 × 5 = 40, one knows 40 ÷ 5 = 8) or properties of operations. By the end of Grade 3, know from memory all products of two one-digit numbers.

10A83070DFE80131917A68A86D17958E.description: Understand division as an unknown-factor problem.
comments: For example, find 32 ÷ 8 by finding the number that makes 32 when multiplied by 8.

10A7E040DFE80131917968A86D17958E.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide.
comments: Students need not use formal terms for these properties.
Example: Knowing that 8 × 5 = 40 and 8 × 2 = 16, one can find 8 × 7 as 8 × (5 + 2) = (8 × 5) + (8 × 2) = 40 + 16 = 56. (Distributive property.)

Example: If 6 × 4 = 24 is known, then 4 × 6 = 24 is also known (Commutative property of multiplication.) 3 × 5 × 2 can be found by 3 × 5 = 15, then 15 × 2 = 30, or by 5 × 2 = 10, then 3 × 10 = 30. (Associative property of multiplication.)

10A78FC0DFE80131917868A86D17958E.description: Understand properties of multiplication and the relationship between multiplication and division.

10A74C70DFE80131917768A86D17958E.description: Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation relating three whole numbers.
comments: For example, determine the unknown number that makes the equation true in each of the equations 8 × ? = 48, 5 = ÷ 3, 6 × 6 = ?.

10A70800DFE80131917668A86D17958E.description: Use multiplication and division within 100 to solve word problems in situations involving equal groups, arrays, and measurement quantities, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

comments: For example, describe a context in which a number of shares or a number of groups can be expressed as 56 ÷ 8.
10A6BF80DFE80131917568A86D17958E.description: Interpret whole-number quotients of whole numbers, e.g., interpret 56 ÷ 8 as the number of objects in each share when 56 objects are partitioned equally into 8 shares, or as a number of shares when 56 objects are partitioned into equal shares of 8 objects each.

10A67A60DFE80131917468A86D17958E.description: Interpret products of whole numbers, e.g., interpret 5 × 7 as the total number of objects in 5 groups of 7 objects each.
comments: For example, describe a context in which a total number of objects can be expressed as 5 × 7.

10A632A0DFE80131917368A86D17958E.description: Represent and solve problems involving multiplication and division.

10A59320DFE80131917168A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.

Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.
10A53AC0DFE80131917068A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.

comments: Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.
10A3AD50DFE80131916C68A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

comments: Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

10A31370DFE80131916A68A86D17958E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

1E2923D0DFE80131A93668A86D17958E.description: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and responding to texts, including using frequently occurring conjunctions to signal simple relationships (e.g., because).

1E248120DFE80131A92868A86D17958E.description: Use conventional spelling for words with common spelling patterns and for frequently occurring irregular words.

1E2424D0DFE80131A92768A86D17958E.description: Use commas in dates and to separate single words in a series.

1E237EC0DFE80131A92568A86D17958E.description: Capitalize dates and names of people.

1E232AC0DFE80131A92468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

1E226700DFE80131A92268A86D17958E.description: Use frequently occurring prepositions (e.g., during, beyond, toward).

1E21D050DFE80131A92068A86D17958E.description: Use frequently occurring conjunctions (e.g., and, but, or, so, because).

1E209C00DFE80131A91C68A86D17958E.description: Use singular and plural nouns with matching verbs in basic sentences (e.g., He hops; We hop).

1E204F50DFE80131A91B68A86D17958E.description: Use common, proper, and possessive nouns.

1E200120DFE80131A91A68A86D17958E.description: Print all upper- and lowercase letters.

1E1C4C00DFE80131A90F68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

1E1B24C0DFE80131A90B68A86D17958E.description: Add drawings or other visual displays to descriptions when appropriate to clarify ideas, thoughts, and feelings.

1E1ADC90DFE80131A90A68A86D17958E.description: Describe people, places, things, and events with relevant details, expressing ideas and feelings clearly.

1E19A250DFE80131A90668A86D17958E.description: Ask questions to clear up any confusion about the topics and texts under discussion.

1E195100DFE80131A90568A86D17958E.description: Build on others' talk in conversations by responding to the comments of others through multiple exchanges.

1E18FAE0DFE80131A90468A86D17958E.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., listening to others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).

1E17A090DFE80131A90068A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

1E174F00DFE80131A8FF68A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

1E16D5D0DFE80131A8FE68A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

1E163A10DFE80131A8FC68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

1E15EB70DFE80131A8FB68A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

1E1596B0DFE80131A8FA68A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

1E0F36A0DFE80131A8E668A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

1E0EE970DFE80131A8E568A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

1E0E8A40DFE80131A8E468A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

1E0E3130DFE80131A8E368A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

1E0D30D0DFE80131A8E068A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

1E0C9BC0DFE80131A8DE68A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

1E0C5130DFE80131A8DD68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

1E0BFCD0DFE80131A8DC68A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

1E04A140DFE80131A8C568A86D17958E.description: Recognize the distinguishing features of a sentence (e.g., first word, capitalization, ending punctuation).

1E044910DFE80131A8C468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print.

1E026AD0DFE80131A8BE68A86D17958E.description: Identify the reasons an author gives to support points in a text.

1E002380DFE80131A8B768A86D17958E.description: Describe the connection between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text.

1DFFD640DFE80131A8B668A86D17958E.description: Identify the main topic and retell key details of a text.

1DFF8C30DFE80131A8B568A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text.

1DFEA5F0DFE80131A8B268A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, read prose and poetry of appropriate complexity for grade 1.

218ADAF0DFE80131AF9768A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence, conveying a clear and distinct perspective, such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning, alternative or opposing perspectives are addressed, and the organization, development, substance, and style are appropriate to purpose, audience, and a range of formal and informal tasks.

218A1CC0DFE80131AF9568A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric, assessing the stance, premises, links among ideas, word choice, points of emphasis, and tone used.

2189BDE0DFE80131AF9468A86D17958E.description: Integrate multiple sources of information presented in diverse formats and media (e.g., visually, quantitatively, orally) in order to make informed decisions and solve problems, evaluating the credibility and accuracy of each source and noting any discrepancies among the data.

10E11B10DFE8013191E668A86D17958E.description: Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual model.

comments: For example, rewrite 0.62 as 62/100; describe a length as 0.62 meters; locate 0.62 on a number line diagram.

10E05D30DFE8013191E468A86D17958E.description: Express a fraction with denominator 10 as an equivalent fraction with denominator 100, and use this technique to add two fractions with respective denominators 10 and 100.
comments: Students who can generate equivalent fractions can develop strategies for adding fractions with unlike denominators in general. But addition and subtraction with unlike denominators in general is not a requirement at this grade.
For example, express 3/10 as 30/100, and add 3/10 + 4/100 = 34/100.

10DFC3C0DFE8013191E268A86D17958E.description: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

10D162B0DFE8013191B268A86D17958E.description: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems.

comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.
10D0CDE0DFE8013191B068A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.
10D07720DFE8013191AF68A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.

comments: Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

10CEE790DFE8013191AB68A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

10CE4AC0DFE8013191A968A86D17958E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

200EBE00DFE80131AC8768A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases; gather vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

200E6EE0DFE80131AC8668A86D17958E.description: Distinguish among the connotations (associations) of words with similar denotations (definitions) (e.g., stingy, scrimping, economical, unwasteful, thrifty).

200E1CB0DFE80131AC8568A86D17958E.description: Use the relationship between particular words (e.g., cause/effect, part/whole, item/category) to better understand each of the words.

200DC410DFE80131AC8468A86D17958E.description: Interpret figures of speech (e.g., personification) in context.

200D73C0DFE80131AC8368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

200D1BF0DFE80131AC8268A86D17958E.description: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

200CBC50DFE80131AC8168A86D17958E.description: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning or its part of speech.

200C5020DFE80131AC8068A86D17958E.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek or Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., audience, auditory, audible).

200BF640DFE80131AC7F68A86D17958E.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence or paragraph; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

200BA760DFE80131AC7E68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 6 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

200AFEE0DFE80131AC7C68A86D17958E.description: Maintain consistency in style and tone.

200A9A70DFE80131AC7B68A86D17958E.description: Vary sentence patterns for meaning, reader/listener interest, and style.

200A4950DFE80131AC7A68A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

200954F0DFE80131AC7768A86D17958E.description: Use punctuation (commas, parentheses, dashes) to set off nonrestrictive/parenthetical elements.

2008FF60DFE80131AC7668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

20089E30DFE80131AC7568A86D17958E.description: Recognize variations from standard English in their own and others' writing and speaking, and identify and use strategies to improve expression in conventional language.

20084690DFE80131AC7468A86D17958E.description: Recognize and correct vague pronouns (i.e., ones with unclear or ambiguous antecedents).

2007E740DFE80131AC7368A86D17958E.description: Recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in pronoun number and person.

20072960DFE80131AC7168A86D17958E.description: Ensure that pronouns are in the proper case (subjective, objective, possessive).

2006C660DFE80131AC7068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

2005DEA0DFE80131AC6D68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

200526E0DFE80131AC6B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

2004BF00DFE80131AC6A68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

20042540DFE80131AC6868A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

200381A0DFE80131AC6668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

20032360DFE80131AC6568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

20027270DFE80131AC6368A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

200214C0DFE80131AC6268A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

2001C380DFE80131AC6168A86D17958E.description: Include multimedia components (e.g., graphics, images, music, sound) and visual displays in presentations to clarify information.

20016A20DFE80131AC6068A86D17958E.description: Present claims and findings, sequencing ideas logically and using pertinent descriptions, facts, and details to accentuate main ideas or themes; use appropriate eye contact, adequate volume, and clear pronunciation.

2000C500DFE80131AC5E68A86D17958E.description: Delineate a speaker's argument and specific claims, distinguishing claims that are supported by reasons and evidence from claims that are not.

20007720DFE80131AC5D68A86D17958E.description: Interpret information presented in diverse media and formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively, orally) and explain how it contributes to a topic, text, or issue under study.

20002670DFE80131AC5C68A86D17958E.description: Review the key ideas expressed and demonstrate understanding of multiple perspectives through reflection and paraphrasing.

1FFFBDD0DFE80131AC5B68A86D17958E.description: Pose and respond to specific questions with elaboration and detail by making comments that contribute to the topic, text, or issue under discussion.

1FFF50A0DFE80131AC5A68A86D17958E.description: Follow rules for collegial discussions, set specific goals and deadlines, and define individual roles as needed.

1FFF0430DFE80131AC5968A86D17958E.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence on the topic, text, or issue to probe and reflect on ideas under discussion.

1FFEB680DFE80131AC5868A86D17958E.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 6 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

1FFDA8D0DFE80131AC5568A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

1FFD53E0DFE80131AC5468A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

1FFCF2C0DFE80131AC5368A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

1FFC53D0DFE80131AC5168A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

1FFBFA20DFE80131AC5068A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

1FFBA940DFE80131AC4F68A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

1FFAF640DFE80131AC4D68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

1FFA8B00DFE80131AC4C68A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for reflection and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

1FF9C920DFE80131AC4A68A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

1FF97460DFE80131AC4968A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, using search terms effectively; assess the credibility and accuracy of each source; and quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others while avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation.

1FF926A0DFE80131AC4868A86D17958E.description: Conduct short research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question), drawing on several sources and generating additional related, focused questions that allow for multiple avenues of exploration.

1FF8D090DFE80131AC4768A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

1FF87F90DFE80131AC4668A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and present the relationships between information and ideas clearly and efficiently.

1FF83260DFE80131AC4568A86D17958E.description: With some guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on how well purpose and audience have been addressed.

1FF7E400DFE80131AC4468A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

1FF73FE0DFE80131AC4268A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented.

1FF6E4B0DFE80131AC4168A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone.

1FF69400DFE80131AC4068A86D17958E.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

1FF63A00DFE80131AC3F68A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.

1FF5D960DFE80131AC3E68A86D17958E.description: Develop the topic with relevant, well-chosen facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples.

1FF56890DFE80131AC3D68A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic clearly, previewing what is to follow; organize ideas, concepts, and information into broader categories as appropriate to achieving purpose; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., charts, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

1FF50A30DFE80131AC3C68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts, including the narration of historical events, scientific procedures/experiments, or technical processes.

1FF4B7B0DFE80131AC3B68A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from or supports the argument presented.

1FF461A0DFE80131AC3A68A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

1FF3E430DFE80131AC3968A86D17958E.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

1FF37ED0DFE80131AC3868A86D17958E.description: Support claim(s) with logical reasoning and relevant, accurate data and evidence that demonstrate an understanding of the topic or text, using credible sources.

1FF32730DFE80131AC3768A86D17958E.description: Introduce claim(s) about a topic or issue, acknowledge and distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and organize the reasons and evidence logically.

1FF2D690DFE80131AC3668A86D17958E.description: Write arguments focused on discipline-specific content.

1FF23600DFE80131AC3468A86D17958E.description: Writing Standards for Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects 6—12

1FF1E030DFE80131AC3368A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

1FF13320DFE80131AC3168A86D17958E.description: Apply grade 6 Reading standards to literary nonfiction (e.g., "Trace and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, distinguishing claims that are supported by reasons and evidence from claims that are not").

1FF0CF10DFE80131AC3068A86D17958E.description: Apply grade 6 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Compare and contrast texts in different forms or genres [e.g., stories and poems; historical novels and fantasy stories] in terms of their approaches to similar themes and topics").

1FF066D0DFE80131AC2F68A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

1FF008A0DFE80131AC2E68A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources; assess the credibility of each source; and quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others while avoiding plagiarism and providing basic bibliographic information for sources.

1FEFAEA0DFE80131AC2D68A86D17958E.description: Conduct short research projects to answer a question, drawing on several sources and refocusing the inquiry when appropriate.

1FEF61C0DFE80131AC2C68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

1FEF1110DFE80131AC2B68A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing as well as to interact and collaborate with others; demonstrate sufficient command of keyboarding skills to type a minimum of three pages in a single sitting.

1FEEBD00DFE80131AC2A68A86D17958E.description: With some guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

1FEE44F0DFE80131AC2968A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

1FED83F0DFE80131AC2768A86D17958E.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from the narrated experiences or events.

1FED35A0DFE80131AC2668A86D17958E.description: Use precise words and phrases, relevant descriptive details, and sensory language to convey experiences and events.

1FECE670DFE80131AC2568A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of transition words, phrases, and clauses to convey sequence and signal shifts from one time frame or setting to another.

1FEC9580DFE80131AC2468A86D17958E.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, and description, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.

1FEC3D40DFE80131AC2368A86D17958E.description: Engage and orient the reader by establishing a context and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally and logically.

1FEBD870DFE80131AC2268A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, relevant descriptive details, and well-structured event sequences.

1FEB5ED0DFE80131AC2168A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from the information or explanation presented.

1FEB0110DFE80131AC2068A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

1FEAB2E0DFE80131AC1F68A86D17958E.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

1FEA60F0DFE80131AC1E68A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate transitions to clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.

1FEA0650DFE80131AC1D68A86D17958E.description: Develop the topic with relevant facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples.

1FE9B2C0DFE80131AC1C68A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic; organize ideas, concepts, and information, using strategies such as definition, classification, comparison/contrast, and cause/effect; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., charts, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

1FE95B40DFE80131AC1B68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas, concepts, and information through the selection, organization, and analysis of relevant content

1FE90390DFE80131AC1A68A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from the argument presented.

1FE88400DFE80131AC1968A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

1FE824D0DFE80131AC1868A86D17958E.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses to clarify the relationships among claim(s) and reasons.

1FE7D600DFE80131AC1768A86D17958E.description: Support claim(s) with clear reasons and relevant evidence, using credible sources and demonstrating an understanding of the topic or text.

1FE78700DFE80131AC1668A86D17958E.description: Introduce claim(s) and organize the reasons and evidence clearly.

1FE735E0DFE80131AC1568A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence.

1FE62980DFE80131AC1268A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

1FE58A40DFE80131AC1068A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

1FE53580DFE80131AC0F68A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

1FE4D9C0DFE80131AC0E68A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

1FE485F0DFE80131AC0D68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

1FE42CC0DFE80131AC0C68A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

1FE3CC40DFE80131AC0B68A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

1FE35EC0DFE80131AC0A68A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

1FE28CC0DFE80131AC0868A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

1FE23330DFE80131AC0768A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

1FE1E0C0DFE80131AC0668A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

1FE12FB0DFE80131AC0468A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

1FE0D880DFE80131AC0368A86D17958E.description: By the end of grade 8, read and comprehend science/technical texts in the grades 6—8 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

1FE086B0DFE80131AC0268A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

1FE033C0DFE80131AC0168A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the information gained from experiments, simulations, video, or multimedia sources with that gained from reading a text on the same topic.

1FDFDED0DFE80131AC0068A86D17958E.description: Distinguish among facts, reasoned judgment based on research findings, and speculation in a text.

1FDF7080DFE80131ABFF68A86D17958E.description: Integrate quantitative or technical information expressed in words in a text with a version of that information expressed visually (e.g., in a flowchart, diagram, model, graph, or table).

1FDE9890DFE80131ABFD68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the author's purpose in providing an explanation, describing a procedure, or discussing an experiment in a text.

1FDE4450DFE80131ABFC68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure an author uses to organize a text, including how the major sections contribute to the whole and to an understanding of the topic.

1FDDEDD0DFE80131ABFB68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of symbols, key terms, and other domain-specific words and phrases as they are used in a specific scientific or technical context relevant to grades 6—8 texts and topics.

1FDD3AC0DFE80131ABF968A86D17958E.description: Follow precisely a multistep procedure when carrying out experiments, taking measurements, or performing technical tasks.

1FDCE6F0DFE80131ABF868A86D17958E.description: Determine the central ideas or conclusions of a text; provide an accurate summary of the text distinct from prior knowledge or opinions.

1FDC9730DFE80131ABF768A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of science and technical texts.

1FDBE960DFE80131ABF568A86D17958E.description: Reading Standards for Literacy in Science and Technical Subjects 6—12

1FDB95D0DFE80131ABF468A86D17958E.description: By the end of grade 8, read and comprehend history/social studies texts in the grades 6—8 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

1FDB4790DFE80131ABF368A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

1FDAF610DFE80131ABF268A86D17958E.description: Analyze the relationship between a primary and secondary source on the same topic.

1FDAA030DFE80131ABF168A86D17958E.description: Distinguish among fact, opinion, and reasoned judgment in a text.

1FDA4190DFE80131ABF068A86D17958E.description: Integrate visual information (e.g., in charts, graphs, photographs, videos, or maps) with other information in print and digital texts.

1FD97AC0DFE80131ABEE68A86D17958E.description: Identify aspects of a text that reveal an author's point of view or purpose (e.g., loaded language, inclusion or avoidance of particular facts).

1FD92700DFE80131ABED68A86D17958E.description: Describe how a text presents information (e.g., sequentially, comparatively, causally).

1FD8D3F0DFE80131ABEC68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including vocabulary specific to domains related to history/social studies.

1FD82B20DFE80131ABEA68A86D17958E.description: Identify key steps in a text's description of a process related to history/social studies (e.g., how a bill becomes law, how interest rates are raised or lowered).

1FD7D4E0DFE80131ABE968A86D17958E.description: Determine the central ideas or information of a primary or secondary source; provide an accurate summary of the source distinct from prior knowledge or opinions.

1FD77AD0DFE80131ABE868A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of primary and secondary sources.

1FD6C390DFE80131ABE668A86D17958E.description: Reading Standards for Literacy in History/Social Studies 6—12

1FD67430DFE80131ABE568A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literary nonfiction in the grades 6—8 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

1FD62690DFE80131ABE468A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

1FD5D6D0DFE80131ABE368A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast one author's presentation of events with that of another (e.g., a memoir written by and a biography on the same person).

1FD58120DFE80131ABE268A86D17958E.description: Trace and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, distinguishing claims that are supported by reasons and evidence from claims that are not.

1FD51F40DFE80131ABE168A86D17958E.description: Integrate information presented in different media or formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively) as well as in words to develop a coherent understanding of a topic or issue.

1FD42970DFE80131ABDF68A86D17958E.description: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text and explain how it is conveyed in the text.

1FD3DB20DFE80131ABDE68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how a particular sentence, paragraph, chapter, or section fits into the overall structure of a text and contributes to the development of the ideas.

1FD389C0DFE80131ABDD68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings.

1FD2D9A0DFE80131ABDB68A86D17958E.description: Analyze in detail how a key individual, event, or idea is introduced, illustrated, and elaborated in a text (e.g., through examples or anecdotes).

1FD285B0DFE80131ABDA68A86D17958E.description: Determine a central idea of a text and how it is conveyed through particular details; provide a summary of the text distinct from personal opinions or judgments.

1FD22D10DFE80131ABD968A86D17958E.description: Cite textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

1FD112C0DFE80131ABD668A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, in the grades 6—8 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

1FD0C520DFE80131ABD568A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

1FD01C70DFE80131ABD368A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast texts in different forms or genres (e.g., stories and poems; historical novels and fantasy stories) in terms of their approaches to similar themes and topics.

1FCFB8C0DFE80131ABD268A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the experience of reading a story, drama, or poem to listening to or viewing an audio, video, or live version of the text, including contrasting what they "see" and "hear" when reading the text to what they perceive when they listen or watch.

1FCEF050DFE80131ABD068A86D17958E.description: Explain how an author develops the point of view of the narrator or speaker in a text.

1FCE9CD0DFE80131ABCF68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how a particular sentence, chapter, scene, or stanza fits into the overall structure of a text and contributes to the development of the theme, setting, or plot.

1FCE4D90DFE80131ABCE68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of a specific word choice on meaning and tone.

1FCDA010DFE80131ABCC68A86D17958E.description: Describe how a particular story's or drama's plot unfolds in a series of episodes as well as how the characters respond or change as the plot moves toward a resolution.

1FCD4FE0DFE80131ABCB68A86D17958E.description: Determine a theme or central idea of a text and how it is conveyed through particular details; provide a summary of the text distinct from personal opinions or judgments.

1FCCFB10DFE80131ABCA68A86D17958E.description: Cite textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

1FCBC1A0DFE80131ABC768A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

1FCB7260DFE80131ABC668A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

1FCB1E80DFE80131ABC568A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

1FCAC630DFE80131ABC468A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

1FCA6D50DFE80131ABC368A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.
comments: Please see "Research to Build and Present Knowledge" in Writing and "Comprehension and Collaboration" in Speaking and Listening for additional standards relevant to gathering, assessing, and applying information from print and digital sources.

1FC9C480DFE80131ABC168A86D17958E.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

1FC97400DFE80131ABC068A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

1FC92600DFE80131ABBF68A86D17958E.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

1FC87100DFE80131ABBD68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

1FC80F80DFE80131ABBC68A86D17958E.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

1FC7A750DFE80131ABBB68A86D17958E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

1FC6EEC0DFE80131ABB968A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Reading

document.title: Washington Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts

1E704A40DFE80131A9CC68A86D17958E.description: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and responding to texts, including using adjectives and adverbs to describe (e.g., When other kids are happy that makes me happy).

1E700270DFE80131A9CB68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish shades of meaning among closely related verbs (e.g., toss, throw, hurl) and closely related adjectives (e.g., thin, slender, skinny, scrawny).

1E682140DFE80131A9B268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

1E669890DFE80131A9AD68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

1E64FF80DFE80131A9A868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

1E63B2A0DFE80131A9A468A86D17958E.description: Create audio recordings of stories or poems; add drawings or other visual displays to stories or recounts of experiences when appropriate to clarify ideas, thoughts, and feelings.

1E6363D0DFE80131A9A368A86D17958E.description: Tell a story or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking audibly in coherent sentences.

1E62D190DFE80131A9A168A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says in order to clarify comprehension, gather additional information, or deepen understanding of a topic or issue.

1E6275E0DFE80131A9A068A86D17958E.description: Recount or describe key ideas or details from a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.

1E622940DFE80131A99F68A86D17958E.description: Ask for clarification and further explanation as needed about the topics and texts under discussion.

1E61DF60DFE80131A99E68A86D17958E.description: Build on others' talk in conversations by linking their comments to the remarks of others.

1E6042E0DFE80131A99968A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

1E5FF020DFE80131A99868A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

1E5F96E0DFE80131A99768A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

1E5EFA50DFE80131A99568A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

1E5E9D30DFE80131A99468A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

1E5E5080DFE80131A99368A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

1E5DB7C0DFE80131A99168A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

1E5C8D10DFE80131A98D68A86D17958E.description: Recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.

1E5C4780DFE80131A98C68A86D17958E.description: Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., read a number of books on a single topic to produce a report; record science observations).

1E5C0250DFE80131A98B68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge
