1E5B6F00DFE80131A98968A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults and peers, focus on a topic and strengthen writing as needed by revising and editing.

1E5A6E20DFE80131A98668A86D17958E.description: Write narratives in which they recount a well-elaborated event or short sequence of events, include details to describe actions, thoughts, and feelings, use temporal words to signal event order, and provide a sense of closure.

1E5A1F60DFE80131A98568A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts in which they introduce a topic, use facts and definitions to develop points, and provide a concluding statement or section.

1E59C7C0DFE80131A98468A86D17958E.description: Write opinion pieces in which they introduce the topic or book they are writing about, state an opinion, supply reasons that support the opinion, use linking words (e.g., because, and, also) to connect opinion and reasons, and provide a concluding statement or section.

1E58DA70DFE80131A98168A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

1E5827C0DFE80131A97F68A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

1E57C8C0DFE80131A97E68A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

1E578310DFE80131A97D68A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

1E573C00DFE80131A97C68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

1E56F460DFE80131A97B68A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

1E56AAF0DFE80131A97A68A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

1E565810DFE80131A97968A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

1E559CA0DFE80131A97768A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

1E5545C0DFE80131A97668A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

1E54FD80DFE80131A97568A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

1E5466A0DFE80131A97368A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

1E540C00DFE80131A97268A86D17958E.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

1E53C2E0DFE80131A97168A86D17958E.description: Read on-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.

1E537880DFE80131A97068A86D17958E.description: Read on-level text with purpose and understanding.

1E532BB0DFE80131A96F68A86D17958E.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

1E528AB0DFE80131A96D68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and read grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words.

1E521B50DFE80131A96C68A86D17958E.description: Identify words with inconsistent but common spelling-sound correspondences.

1E51C610DFE80131A96B68A86D17958E.description: Decode words with common prefixes and suffixes.

1E517DA0DFE80131A96A68A86D17958E.description: Decode regularly spelled two-syllable words with long vowels.

1E5134E0DFE80131A96968A86D17958E.description: Know spelling-sound correspondences for additional common vowel teams.

1E50EA90DFE80131A96868A86D17958E.description: Distinguish long and short vowels when reading regularly spelled one-syllable words.

1E509EE0DFE80131A96768A86D17958E.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

1E4FB570DFE80131A96468A86D17958E.description: By the end of year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, and technical texts, in the grades 2—3 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

1E4F6930DFE80131A96368A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

1E4F1F00DFE80131A96268A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the most important points presented by two texts on the same topic.

1E4ECC10DFE80131A96168A86D17958E.description: Describe how reasons support specific points the author makes in a text.

1E4E7660DFE80131A96068A86D17958E.description: Explain how specific images (e.g., a diagram showing how a machine works) contribute to and clarify a text.

1E4DC620DFE80131A95E68A86D17958E.description: Identify the main purpose of a text, including what the author wants to answer, explain, or describe.

1E4D7890DFE80131A95D68A86D17958E.description: Know and use various text features (e.g., captions, bold print, subheadings, glossaries, indexes, electronic menus, icons) to locate key facts or information in a text efficiently.

1E4D26D0DFE80131A95C68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 2 topic or subject area.

1E4C6E30DFE80131A95A68A86D17958E.description: Describe the connection between a series of historical events, scientific ideas or concepts, or steps in technical procedures in a text.

1E4C24D0DFE80131A95968A86D17958E.description: Identify the main topic of a multiparagraph text as well as the focus of specific paragraphs within the text.

1E4BDB50DFE80131A95868A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer such questions as who, what, where, when, why, and how to demonstrate understanding of key details in a text.

1E4AEEC0DFE80131A95568A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories and poetry, in the grades 2—3 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

1E4AA5F0DFE80131A95468A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

1E4A1200DFE80131A95268A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast two or more versions of the same story (e.g., Cinderella stories) by different authors or from different cultures.

1E49C7A0DFE80131A95168A86D17958E.description: Use information gained from the illustrations and words in a print or digital text to demonstrate understanding of its characters, setting, or plot.

1E4916B0DFE80131A94F68A86D17958E.description: Acknowledge differences in the points of view of characters, including by speaking in a different voice for each character when reading dialogue aloud.

1E48B9D0DFE80131A94E68A86D17958E.description: Describe the overall structure of a story, including describing how the beginning introduces the story and the ending concludes the action.

1E485E20DFE80131A94D68A86D17958E.description: Describe how words and phrases (e.g., regular beats, alliteration, rhymes, repeated lines) supply rhythm and meaning in a story, poem, or song.

1E47C890DFE80131A94B68A86D17958E.description: Describe how characters in a story respond to major events and challenges.

1E477930DFE80131A94A68A86D17958E.description: Recount stories, including fables and folktales from diverse cultures, and determine their central message, lesson, or moral.

1E4715A0DFE80131A94968A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer such questions as who, what, where, when, why, and how to demonstrate understanding of key details in a text.

1E4634C0DFE80131A94668A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

1E45DB30DFE80131A94568A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

1E4592D0DFE80131A94468A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

1E453B40DFE80131A94368A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

1E44EF60DFE80131A94268A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.

1E445620DFE80131A94068A86D17958E.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

1E440100DFE80131A93F68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

1E43AE90DFE80131A93E68A86D17958E.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

1E42FBC0DFE80131A93C68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

1E42AA80DFE80131A93B68A86D17958E.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

1E425B20DFE80131A93A68A86D17958E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

document.title: Washington State K-12 Social Studies Grade Level Expectations

2B562600DFE80131C22068A86D17958E.description: Evaluates positions and evidence to make one's own decisions in a paper or presentation.
comments: Weighs positions and evidence to determine how the Kurdish people have fared in different parts of the world.
Weighs positions and evidence to determine one's own political affiliation.
Weighs positions and evidence to determine one's own stance on the war in Iraq.

2B559FC0DFE80131C21E68A86D17958E.description: Creates a product that uses social studies content to support a thesis and presents the product in an appropriate manner to a meaningful audience.

2B555A60DFE80131C21D68A86D17958E.description: Evaluates how the discussion and the proposed alternative resolutions changed or solidified one's own position on public issues.

2B5473C0DFE80131C21A68A86D17958E.description: Evaluates the breadth of research to determine the need for new or additional investigation when researching an issue or event.

Upon concluding a research paper on the fairness of the government's farm subsidies, critiques the ways in which the research could be enhanced with additional investigation.

2B530230DFE80131C21668A86D17958E.description: Evaluates the plausibility of an analysis of decisions affecting the global community.

Critiques whether an analysis of the long-term implications of individual's career choices for their local community is realistic.

2B526580DFE80131C21468A86D17958E.description: Analyzes the short-term and long-term implications of decisions affecting the global community.

Examines the short-term and long-term implications that individual's career choices have for their local community and the world.

2B51E360DFE80131C21268A86D17958E.description: Uses critical reasoning skills to analyze and evaluate positions.

2B519EC0DFE80131C21168A86D17958E.description: Social Studies Skills - The student understands and applies reasoning skills to conduct research, deliberate, form, and evaluate positions through the processes of reading, writing, and communicating.

2B515510DFE80131C21068A86D17958E.description: Evaluates positions on a current issue based on an analysis of history.

2B50B520DFE80131C20E68A86D17958E.description: Uses history to understand the present and plan for the future.

comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.
11A08A60DFE8013192FA68A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.
11A02740DFE8013192F968A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.

comments: Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

119E88A0DFE8013192F568A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

0FFD2F10DFE8013190DB68A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. document.title: Washington State K-12 Social Studies Grade Level Expectations

2A5870C0DFE80131C01068A86D17958E.description: Prepares a list of resources, including the title, author, type of source, date published, and publisher for each source, and arranges the sources alphabetically.
comments: Using an online program, completes an alphabetical list of resources on the American Revolution, including the title, author, type of source, date published, and publisher for each source.

2A57CC40DFE80131C00E68A86D17958E.description: Researches multiple perspectives to take a position on a public or historical issue in a paper or presentation.
comments: Researches multiple perspectives on the public issue of mandating school uniforms.
Researches multiple perspectives on the public issue of banning cell phones in school.
Researches multiple perspectives on the public issue of removing dams to save salmon
Researches multiple perspectives on the public issue of mandating recycling.

2A572CB0DFE80131C00C68A86D17958E.description: Creates a product that uses social studies content to support a thesis and presents the product in an appropriate manner to a meaningful audience.

2A56DEB0DFE80131C00B68A86D17958E.description: Engages others in discussions that attempt to clarify and address multiple viewpoints on public issues based on key ideals.
comments: Engages classmates in a discussion to clarify the multiple viewpoints surrounding censorship based on the key ideal of individual rights.
Engages classmates in a discussion to clarify the multiple viewpoints surrounding the inclusion of "under God" in the Pledge of Allegiance based on the key ideal of freedom.

2A55A6B0DFE80131C00768A86D17958E.description: Understands how essential questions define the significance of researching an issue or event.
comments: Explains how the essential question "Why do people want to be free?" reminds us why we study the American Revolution.
Explains how the essential question "How can we be heard by our government?" reminds us why we study the writing of the Declaration of Independence.

2A54DC80DFE80131C00468A86D17958E.description: Evaluates the relevance of facts used in forming a position on an issue or event.
comments: Determines which facts are relevant in supporting a position on whether there should be a ban on smoking in public places.
Determines which facts are relevant in supporting a position on whether students should say the Pledge of Allegiance.

2A543700DFE80131C00268A86D17958E.description: Understands the purpose of documents and the concepts used in them.
comments: Explains the purposes of the Declaration of Independence and how Thomas Jefferson used the concept of rights in this document.
Explains how the concept of rights outlined in the Declaration of Independence relates to a particular public issue.
Explains the purposes of the Constitution and how the framers of the Constitution expressed the concept of government responsibilities.
Explains how the concept of government responsibilities in the Constitution relates to a particular public issue.
Explains how the founders expressed the concept of individual rights in the Bill of Rights.

2A539C30DFE80131C00068A86D17958E.description: Uses critical reasoning skills to analyze and evaluate positions.

2A5354D0DFE80131BFFF68A86D17958E.description: Social Studies Skills - The student understands and applies reasoning skills to conduct research, deliberate, form, and evaluate positions through the processes of reading, writing, and communicating.

2A530AD0DFE80131BFFE68A86D17958E.description: Understands that significant historical events in the United States have implications for current decisions and influence the future.
comments: Explains how the slogan of "no taxation without representation" has influenced initiative processes in states across the United States.
Explains how the principles and ideals set forth in the Constitution affect current government and citizen decisions.

2A525990DFE80131BFFC68A86D17958E.description: Uses history to understand the present and plan for the future.

2A5207F0DFE80131BFFB68A86D17958E.description: Analyzes the multiple causes of change and conflict in U.S. history.
comments: Analyzes the historical, economic, civic, and geographical causes of the Revolution.
Analyzes the historical, economic, civic, and geographical causes of the Boston Tea Party.
Explains how the distance between England and the thirteen colonies was a factor in the Revolutionary War.

2A517FA0DFE80131BFF968A86D17958E.description: Analyzes the multiple perspectives and interpretations of historical events in U.S. history.
comments: Examines different accounts of the colonization era, including colonists' perspective of settlement and indigenous people's perspective of genocide.
Examines different accounts of colonists and indentured servants.
Differentiates between historical facts, evidence, and historical interpretations of the Boston Massacre as a turning point igniting the Revolutionary War.

2A50EF10DFE80131BFF768A86D17958E.description: Understands that there are multiple perspectives and interpretations of historical events.

2A508B70DFE80131BFF668A86D17958E.description: Understands how technology and ideas have affected the way people live and change their values, beliefs, and attitudes.
comments: Explains how the idea of individual rights led to the creation of the Bill of Rights.
Explains how the printing press was used to print the Declaration of Independence in newspapers throughout the thirteen colonies, which led to an interest in democratic movements.
Explains how the idea of democracy led the colonists to seek change by fighting Great Britain in the Revolutionary War.

2A4FE6A0DFE80131BFF468A86D17958E.description: Analyzes how people from various cultural groups have shaped U.S. history.
comments: Examines how African slaves and free people of color contributed to the establishment and growth of agriculture in the thirteen colonies.
Examines how Germans and Swiss contributed to the development of Pennsylvania.
Examines how native peoples helped the colonists establish survival skills in their new environment.

2A4F58A0DFE80131BFF268A86D17958E.description: Understands and analyzes how individuals caused change in U.S. history.
comments: Examines the impact Crispus Attucks had on the colonists' desire to fight for freedom from Great Britain.
Explains how George Washington led troops to victory over Great Britain in the Revolutionary War.

2A4EBB70DFE80131BFF068A86D17958E.description: Understands and analyzes causal factors that have shaped major events in history.

comments: Explains how the rise of the Anasazi civilization helps to define the history of North America prior to European settlement as a time when indigenous societies were developing.
Explains how the interaction between the Puritans and the Wampanoag defines the history of the Americans between 1492 and 1763 as a time of encounter.

Explains how the establishment of the colony of Virginia, the Massachusetts Bay Colony, and the Pennsylvania Colony helps to define the history of the Americas between 1492 and 1763 as a time of settlement and colonization.
Explains how the effects of disease on indigenous peoples in the Americas between 1492 and 1763 define this era as a time of devastation.
Explains how the Revolution and Constitution help to define U.S. history from 1763 to 1791.
2A4E6730DFE80131BFEF68A86D17958E.description:
Understands how the following themes and developments help to define eras in U.S. history from time immemorial to 1791:
  • Development of indigenous societies in North America (time immemorial to 1791).
  • Encounter, colonization, and devastation (1492—1763).
  • Revolution and the Constitution (1763—1791).

2A4DCE60DFE80131BFED68A86D17958E.description: Understands and creates timelines to show how historical events are caused by other important events.
comments: Constructs and explains a timeline that shows the major eras in U.S. history up to 1776.
Constructs a timeline that relates events involving historical, economic, geographic, and civic factors to the causes of the Revolutionary War.

2A4CBD10DFE80131BFEA68A86D17958E.description: History - The student understands and applies knowledge of historical thinking, chronology, eras, turning points, major ideas, individuals, and themes in local, Washington State, tribal, United States, and world history in order to evaluate how history shapes the present and future.

comments: Explains and analyzes how the movement of the colonists to the Americas forced the movement of native peoples from their land.
Explains how the triangular trade route between Africa, Britain, and the thirteen colonies forced the movement of African people as slave labor.
2A4BF870DFE80131BFE768A86D17958E.description: Understands and analyzes the impact of the European colonists' movement to the Americas on the land and the indigenous peoples.

2A4AD480DFE80131BFE368A86D17958E.description: Understands human interaction with the environment.

2A4A88C0DFE80131BFE268A86D17958E.description: Understands the physical and cultural characteristics of the thirteen colonies.
comments: Explains the differences in the physical characteristics, including landforms, climate, and natural resources, of the thirteen colonies.
Explains the cultural characteristics, including distribution of population and languages, of the people in the thirteen colonies.

2A4A4540DFE80131BFE168A86D17958E.description: Characteristics and Spatial Organiztion of Places and Regions

2A49FEC0DFE80131BFE068A86D17958E.description: Constructs and uses maps to show and analyze information about European settlement in the Americas.
comments: Constructs maps that show the location of the thirteen colonies, major landforms, climate, natural resources, and economic products.

2A496D10DFE80131BFDE68A86D17958E.description: Understands the physical characteristics, cultural characteristics, and location of places, regions, and spatial patterns on the Earth's surface.

2A491B50DFE80131BFDD68A86D17958E.description: Geography - The student uses a spatial perspective to make reasoned decisions by applying the concepts of location, region, and movement and demonstrating knowledge of how geographic features and human cultures impact environments.

2A483380DFE80131BFDA68A86D17958E.description: Understands the impact of the British government on the economy of the thirteen colonies.
comments: Explains how British taxes on tea and sugar affected the distribution of goods in the colonies.
Explains how the Stamp Act imposed by British Parliament affected the economy of the colonies by requiring the purchase of a tax stamp for all legal documents.
Examines the reasons why colonists chose to dump tea into the Boston Harbor on December 16, 1773.

Explains how the public issue of maintaining public parks is related to the responsibility of paying taxes.

2A42D7E0DFE80131BFC868A86D17958E.description: Understands the function of the United States government.

Explains how the judicial branch judges laws according to the U.S. Constitution.

2A424CE0DFE80131BFC668A86D17958E.description: Understands the organization of the United States government.

2A41BDD0DFE80131BFC468A86D17958E.description: Understands the purposes, organization, and function of governments, laws, and political systems.

2A4169A0DFE80131BFC368A86D17958E.description: Evaluates how a public issue is related to constitutional rights and the common good.

Explains how the First Amendment promotes liberty.
2A40DD70DFE80131BFC168A86D17958E.description: Understands the key ideals of liberty and patriotism as outlined in the Declaration of Independence, U.S. Constitution, and other fundamental documents.

2A4042C0DFE80131BFBF68A86D17958E.description: Understands key ideals and principles of the United States, including those in the Declaration of Independence, the Constitution, and other fundamental documents.

2A3FE940DFE80131BFBE68A86D17958E.description: Civics - The student understands and applies knowledge of government, law, politics, and the nation's fundamental documents to make decisions about local, national, and international issues and to demonstrate thoughtful, participatory citizenship.

document.title: Options for Implementing the Arts Standards through Visual Arts by Grade Level

16FE3F00DFE801319C3468A86D17958E.description:

  • Uses materials safely.
  • Uses tools safely.
  • Meets deadlines.
  • Completes work.
  • Cares for personal and studio space.
  • Acquires good craftsmanship.

16FD9A90DFE801319C3268A86D17958E.description: Applies his/her understanding of how the knowledge, skills, and work habits of visual arts are used in the world of work, including careers in visual arts.

16FD4960DFE801319C3168A86D17958E.description: Understands how arts knowledge and skills are used in the world of work, including careers in the arts.

16FCEEC0DFE801319C3068A86D17958E.description: Uses specific attributes in artworks to reflect a specific culture, place, or time.

16FCA0A0DFE801319C2F68A86D17958E.description:
Explores, describes and compares attributes of:
  • Artworks in the classroom.
  • Artworks in the school.

  • Artworks of a specific culture, place, or time.

  • By members of the community.

16F36210DFE801319C1168A86D17958E.description: Analyzes the ways that visual arts are used to express feelings and present ideas and applies his/her understanding when creating artworks.

16F318E0DFE801319C1068A86D17958E.description: Uses visual arts to express feelings and present ideas.

16F28A70DFE801319C0E68A86D17958E.description:
Demonstrates a responding process:

  • Describes and communicates what is perceived and experienced through the senses (seen, felt, smelled, tasted, and/or heard).
  • Uses developmentally appropriate elements and foundations of visual arts.
  • Determines personal meaning based on personal experiences and background knowledge.

16F23F90DFE801319C0D68A86D17958E.description: Applies a responding process to a presentation/exhibit of visual arts.

16F1E840DFE801319C0C68A86D17958E.description: Applies a responding process to a presentation/exhibit of visual arts. (Engages, describes, analyzes, interprets, and evaluates)

16F19B10DFE801319C0B68A86D17958E.description:

  • Creates, revises, and evaluates works of visual arts through exploration, reflection, and problem-solving.
  • Selects artistic resources and materials in order to create and present artworks.
  • Produces and presents an artwork that represents a personal experience.
  • Communicates the process used to make a visual artwork and/or presentation.
  • Identifies the audience and purpose of the artwork and presentation.
  • Reflects upon the process used to create artworks and selfevaluates.
  • Interprets meaning through personal understanding of the work and/or presentation.

16F15080DFE801319C0A68A86D17958E.description: Applies a performance and/or presentation process to visual arts.

16F0F4F0DFE801319C0968A86D17958E.description: Applies a performance and/or presentation process to visual arts. (Identifies, selects, analyzes, interprets, practices, revises, adjusts, refines, presents, exhibits, produces, reflects, self-evaluates)

16F089F0DFE801319C0868A86D17958E.description:
Demonstrates a creative process:
  • Explores the purpose of a visual arts composition.
  • Gathers and uses information from diverse sources to create works of art.
  • Uses ideas, skills, foundations, and techniques to create works of arts.
  • Implements choices of the elements and techniques of visual arts and principles of design to create works of art.
  • Reflects for the purposes of self-evaluation and improvement.
  • Refines works of visual arts through feedback and selfreflection.
  • Presents works of art to others in the school and community.

16F03FE0DFE801319C0768A86D17958E.description: Applies a creative process to visual arts.

16EFFAF0DFE801319C0668A86D17958E.description: Applies a creative process to visual arts. (Identifies, explores, gathers, interprets, uses, implements, reflects, refines, and presents)

16EFB580DFE801319C0568A86D17958E.description: The student uses the artistic processes of creating, performing/presenting, and responding to demonstrate thinking skills in dance, music, theatre, and visual arts.

16EF2900DFE801319C0368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates respect for artists and artworks in the community and in a variety of visual arts settings.

16EEDE30DFE801319C0268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates appropriate audience conventions in a variety of arts settings.

16EF6FD0DFE801319C0468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates active listening and appropriate viewing skills in visual arts settings.

16EE8BB0DFE801319C0168A86D17958E.description: Analyzes the conventions and responsibilities of the audience and applies the conventions that are appropriate given the setting and culture.

16EE4710DFE801319C0068A86D17958E.description: Understands and applies audience conventions in a variety of settings, performances, and presentations of visual arts.

16ECDA60DFE801319BFB68A86D17958E.description: Uses visual thinking strategies to discuss a variety of artworks.

16EE00A0DFE801319BFF68A86D17958E.description: Uses arts vocabulary to describe specific attributes of the artworks of various artists, cultures, and times.

16EDBC10DFE801319BFE68A86D17958E.description: Differentiates between a variety of arts styles and genres from Western and non-Western traditions.

16ED7550DFE801319BFD68A86D17958E.description: Examines, selects, and uses influences from a particular artist, style, culture, or time to create an original artwork.

16ED29E0DFE801319BFC68A86D17958E.description: Examines a variety of artworks for historical and cultural information.

16EC91D0DFE801319BFA68A86D17958E.description: Applies, analyzes, and creates artworks using visual arts styles and genres of various artists, cultures, places, and times.

16EBF700DFE801319BF868A86D17958E.description: Uses forming and stamping techniques to create functional clay vessels.

16EBA2A0DFE801319BF768A86D17958E.description: Uses perceptual skills to create imagery from observation and imagination.

16EAFD60DFE801319BF568A86D17958E.description: Uses a variety of types of line and/or textures in an artwork.

16EB5100DFE801319BF668A86D17958E.description: Uses perceptual and technical skills to create two- and three-dimensional works of art.

16EAB720DFE801319BF468A86D17958E.description: Develops and explores the skills, techniques, and processes of visual arts.

16EA71D0DFE801319BF368A86D17958E.description: Applies and analyzes the skills and techniques of visual arts to create original works of art in two and/or three dimensions.

16EA2C30DFE801319BF268A86D17958E.description: Develops visual arts skills and techniques.

16E903D0DFE801319BEE68A86D17958E.description:
Examines, develops, and creates works of art in a variety of two- and three-dimensional media by using and combining:
  • Repetition/pattern
  • Contrast
  • Variety
  • Balance (symmetrical, asymmetrical, and radial)
  • Movement and rhythm.
  • Proportion
  • Emphasis/dominance (developed through the use of contrast of color, size/placement, balance, proportion, and movement/rhythm)

16E9E3A0DFE801319BF168A86D17958E.description: Uses and discusses the use of principles of design in his/her work and the work of others.

16E99840DFE801319BF068A86D17958E.description: Identifies, examines, classifies, and uses the patterns and types of balance found in nature, in man-made environments, and in works of art.

16E8BF30DFE801319BED68A86D17958E.description: Uses patterns to enhance the surfaces of shapes and forms in a variety of two- and three-dimensional works of art.

16E94940DFE801319BEF68A86D17958E.description: Explores and creates patterns, movement, and rhythm by using the repetition of lines, shapes, and colors.

16E87AB0DFE801319BEC68A86D17958E.description: Applies, analyzes, and creates repetition/pattern, contrast, variety, balance, movement/rhythm, and proportion in a work of art.

16E83400DFE801319BEB68A86D17958E.description:
Differentiates between, produces, mixes, and uses—in various artworks and using a variety of media—the following:
  • Primary colors (yellow, red, blue).
  • Secondary colors (orange, green, purple/violet); created by mixing and using primary colors (yellow + red = orange).
  • Warm colors (yellow, orange, red) and cool colors (blue, green, violet).
  • Intermediate (tertiary) colors; created by mixing selected primary and secondary colors (yellow + green = yellow-green).
  • Tints and shades (to show color value).
  • Complementary color pairs.
  • Language of color.

16E7EDD0DFE801319BEA68A86D17958E.description: Applies, analyzes, and creates the elements of visual arts when producing a work of art.

16E79F40DFE801319BE968A86D17958E.description:
Plans, selects, and uses the element of space and spatial devices in various environments, in works of two- and three-dimensional art, and in a variety of media to demonstrate/portray:
  • Baseline
  • Over/under
  • Above/below
  • Beside
  • Behind/in front
  • Foreground
  • Middle ground
  • Background
  • Overlap
  • Size
  • Placement on a page
  • Detail/diminishing detail
  • Color/diminishing color
  • Positive and negative space/shape

16E75680DFE801319BE868A86D17958E.description: Applies, analyzes, and creates the elements of visual arts when producing a work of art.

16E6B5A0DFE801319BE668A86D17958E.description: Develops textures realistically and imaginatively in works of art in a variety of media, styles, and subject matter.

16E663C0DFE801319BE568A86D17958E.description: Differentiates between visual/implied and actual texture.

16E705A0DFE801319BE768A86D17958E.description:
Selects, examines, and produces a variety of textures in various environments, in various works of two- and three-dimensional art, and in a variety of media to demonstrate/portray:
  • Visual texture
  • Implied texture

16E605D0DFE801319BE468A86D17958E.description: Applies, analyzes, and creates the elements of visual arts when producing a work of art.

16E5BA90DFE801319BE368A86D17958E.description: Examines and discusses the use of value in a variety of artworks.

16E55C70DFE801319BE268A86D17958E.description:
Examines and produces a range of four values in two- and three-dimensional artworks in a variety of media to demonstrate/establish:
  • The illusion of form on a two-dimensional surface.
  • The illusion of depth/space (foreground, middle ground, and background).
  • Shadows and a source of illumination in artworks.

16E503A0DFE801319BE168A86D17958E.description:
Describes, selects, and produces a range of four values in various environments and works of art in a variety of media; demonstrates and produces:
  • A black-to-white value scale with three intermediate levels of gray (see the glossary for an example).
  • A one-color value scale, including a range of two intermediate color values (see the glossary for an example).
  • Two- and three-dimensional artworks that incorporate three levels of value.
  • A value scale in which repeating lines and shapes are used to generate three levels of value.

16E4BA30DFE801319BE068A86D17958E.description: Applies, analyzes, and creates the elements of visual arts when producing a work of art.

16E46EF0DFE801319BDF68A86D17958E.description:
Differentiates between, selects, and produces shapes and forms in a variety of styles, artworks, and media, including digital media, to demonstrate:
  • Geometric shapes and forms.
  • Organic shapes and forms.
  • Free-form shapes and forms.
  • Positive and negative shapes.
  • The illusion of three-dimensional form on a two-dimensional surface.
  • Realism.

16E41E50DFE801319BDE68A86D17958E.description: Applies, analyzes, and creates the elements of visual arts when producing a work of art.

16E3D420DFE801319BDD68A86D17958E.description: Selects, uses, and constructs a variety of types and qualities of line to create texture in a two- or three-dimensional work of art.

16E389F0DFE801319BDC68A86D17958E.description:
Selects, uses, and produces a variety of types and qualities of line for artistic purposes in two- and three-dimensional artworks and to demonstrate/portray the following features and functions of line:
  • Direction
  • Expression/emotion
  • Movement
  • Shape
  • Textures
  • Patterns
  • Imaginative drawing
  • Observational drawing
  • To indicate form
  • Detail
  • Contours
  • Design
  • Space
  • Value (light, medium, and dark)
  • Gesture

16E2FA60DFE801319BDA68A86D17958E.description: Understands and applies visual arts concepts and vocabulary.

comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.
F9C61E25A1B44CE39622459775C7B99A.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

46B07D3A94124977AA86D32DA55AEED0.description: Look for and make use of structure.
comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

E344687BE97E493195D2E3A3F219445A.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

3D666D0959BC446DBBDBB6584E9296BC.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

document.title: Washington Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts

1F07B130DFE80131AA7368A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate conversational, general academic, and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal spatial and temporal relationships (e.g., After dinner that night we went looking for them).

1F0764B0DFE80131AA7268A86D17958E.description: Distinguish shades of meaning among related words that describe states of mind or degrees of certainty (e.g., knew, believed, suspected, heard, wondered).

1F071800DFE80131AA7168A86D17958E.description: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., describe people who are friendly or helpful).

1F06C260DFE80131AA7068A86D17958E.description: Distinguish the literal and nonliteral meanings of words and phrases in context (e.g., take steps).

1F0675C0DFE80131AA6F68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

1F062830DFE80131AA6E68A86D17958E.description: Use glossaries or beginning dictionaries, both print and digital, to determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

1F05D9E0DFE80131AA6D68A86D17958E.description: Use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root (e.g., company, companion).

1F0587D0DFE80131AA6C68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of the new word formed when a known affix is added to a known word (e.g., agreeable/disagreeable, comfortable/uncomfortable, care/careless, heat/preheat).

1F0529D0DFE80131AA6B68A86D17958E.description: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

1F04AD80DFE80131AA6A68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning word and phrases based on grade 3 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

1F040F60DFE80131AA6868A86D17958E.description: Recognize and observe differences between the conventions of spoken and written standard English.

1F03C2D0DFE80131AA6768A86D17958E.description: Choose words and phrases for effect.

1F037460DFE80131AA6668A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

1F02CD10DFE80131AA6468A86D17958E.description: Consult reference materials, including beginning dictionaries, as needed to check and correct spellings.

1F027D40DFE80131AA6368A86D17958E.description: Use spelling patterns and generalizations (e.g., word families, position-based spellings, syllable patterns, ending rules, meaningful word parts) in writing words.

1F0221D0DFE80131AA6268A86D17958E.description: Use conventional spelling for high-frequency and other studied words and for adding suffixes to base words (e.g., sitting, smiled, cries, happiness).

1F018210DFE80131AA6068A86D17958E.description: Use commas and quotation marks in dialogue.

1F007610DFE80131AA5D68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

1F001E60DFE80131AA5C68A86D17958E.description: Produce simple, compound, and complex sentences.

1EF6B800DFE80131AA5A68A86D17958E.description: Form and use comparative and superlative adjectives and adverbs, and choose between them depending on what is to be modified.

1EF61520DFE80131AA5868A86D17958E.description: Form and use the simple (e.g., I walked; I walk; I will walk) verb tenses.

1EF5CB60DFE80131AA5768A86D17958E.description: Form and use regular and irregular verbs.

1EF52E80DFE80131AA5568A86D17958E.description: Form and use regular and irregular plural nouns.

1EF4D770DFE80131AA5468A86D17958E.description: Explain the function of nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs in general and their functions in particular sentences.

1EF48DA0DFE80131AA5368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

1EF3A6D0DFE80131AA5068A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

1EF35750DFE80131AA4F68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

1EF30180DFE80131AA4E68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

1EF25DE0DFE80131AA4C68A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

1EF1A740DFE80131AA4A68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

1EF14290DFE80131AA4968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

1EF07710DFE80131AA4768A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

1EEFFF00DFE80131AA4668A86D17958E.description: Speak in complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation in order to provide requested detail or clarification.

1EEFAFC0DFE80131AA4568A86D17958E.description: Create engaging audio recordings of stories or poems that demonstrate fluid reading at an understandable pace; add visual displays when appropriate to emphasize or enhance certain facts or details.

1EEF56D0DFE80131AA4468A86D17958E.description: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking clearly at an understandable pace.

1EEEB9E0DFE80131AA4268A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions about information from a speaker, offering appropriate elaboration and detail.

1EEE68D0DFE80131AA4168A86D17958E.description: Determine the main ideas and supporting details of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

1EEE1870DFE80131AA4068A86D17958E.description: Explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.

1EEDC300DFE80131AA3F68A86D17958E.description: Ask questions to check understanding of information presented, stay on topic, and link their comments to the remarks of others.

1EED68C0DFE80131AA3E68A86D17958E.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., gaining the floor in respectful ways, listening to others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).

1EED16E0DFE80131AA3D68A86D17958E.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.

1EECB720DFE80131AA3C68A86D17958E.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 3 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

1EEB89B0DFE80131AA3968A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

1EEB3640DFE80131AA3868A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

1EEAE110DFE80131AA3768A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

1EEA2450DFE80131AA3568A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

1EE9BDB0DFE80131AA3468A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

1EE96D70DFE80131AA3368A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

1EE8D070DFE80131AA3168A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

1EE88190DFE80131AA3068A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

1EE77B10DFE80131AA2D68A86D17958E.description: Recall information from experiences or gather information from print and digital sources; take brief notes on sources and sort evidence into provided categories.

1EE71520DFE80131AA2C68A86D17958E.description: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge about a topic.

1EE68B10DFE80131AA2B68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

1EE633A0DFE80131AA2A68A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, use technology to produce and publish writing (using keyboarding skills) as well as to interact and collaborate with others.

1EE5E3F0DFE80131AA2968A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing.

1EE58F70DFE80131AA2868A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, produce writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task and purpose.
comments: (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards 1—3 above.)

1EE45E00DFE80131AA2568A86D17958E.description: Use temporal words and phrases to signal event order.

1EE412F0DFE80131AA2468A86D17958E.description: Use dialogue and descriptions of actions, thoughts, and feelings to develop experiences and events or show the response of characters to situations.

1EE3C2F0DFE80131AA2368A86D17958E.description: Establish a situation and introduce a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.

1EE373C0DFE80131AA2268A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences.

1EE30220DFE80131AA2168A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section.

1EE29A30DFE80131AA2068A86D17958E.description: Use linking words and phrases (e.g., also, another, and, more, but) to connect ideas within categories of information.

1EE244C0DFE80131AA1F68A86D17958E.description: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, and details.

1EE1ED20DFE80131AA1E68A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic and group related information together; include illustrations when useful to aiding comprehension.

1EE18DE0DFE80131AA1D68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.

1EE13870DFE80131AA1C68A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section.

1EE0E240DFE80131AA1B68A86D17958E.description: Use linking words and phrases (e.g., because, therefore, since, for example) to connect opinion and reasons.

1EE09880DFE80131AA1A68A86D17958E.description: Provide reasons that support the opinion.

1EE04CC0DFE80131AA1968A86D17958E.description: Introduce the topic or text they are writing about, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure that lists reasons.

1EDFFEE0DFE80131AA1868A86D17958E.description: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons.

1EDEE470DFE80131AA1568A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

1EDE4B20DFE80131AA1368A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

1EDDFD60DFE80131AA1268A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

1EDDAF20DFE80131AA1168A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

1EDD58D0DFE80131AA1068A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

1EDCF510DFE80131AA0F68A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

1EDC9390DFE80131AA0E68A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

1EDC35E0DFE80131AA0D68A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

1EDB9300DFE80131AA0B68A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

1EDB30D0DFE80131AA0A68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

1EDAE5A0DFE80131AA0968A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

1EDA5010DFE80131AA0768A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

1EDA01C0DFE80131AA0668A86D17958E.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

1ED9ABF0DFE80131AA0568A86D17958E.description: Read on-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings

1ED94670DFE80131AA0468A86D17958E.description: Read on-level text with purpose and understanding.

1ED8FC10DFE80131AA0368A86D17958E.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

1ED7C460DFE80131A9FF68A86D17958E.description: Decode words with common Latin suffixes.

1ED76D50DFE80131A9FE68A86D17958E.description: Identify and know the meaning of the most common prefixes and derivational suffixes.

1ED71DD0DFE80131A9FD68A86D17958E.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

1ED61DD0DFE80131A9FA68A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, and technical texts, at the high end of the grades 2—3 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

1ED5BE10DFE80131A9F968A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

1ED56100DFE80131A9F868A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the most important points and key details presented in two texts on the same topic.

1ED50250DFE80131A9F768A86D17958E.description: Describe the logical connection between particular sentences and paragraphs in a text (e.g., comparison, cause/effect, first/second/third in a sequence).

1ED4A030DFE80131A9F668A86D17958E.description: Use information gained from illustrations (e.g., maps, photographs) and the words in a text to demonstrate understanding of the text (e.g., where, when, why, and how key events occur).

1ED3C330DFE80131A9F468A86D17958E.description: Distinguish their own point of view from that of the author of a text.

1ED360C0DFE80131A9F368A86D17958E.description: Use text features and search tools (e.g., key words, sidebars, hyperlinks) to locate information relevant to a given topic efficiently.

1ED31320DFE80131A9F268A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 3 topic or subject area.

1ED26F00DFE80131A9F068A86D17958E.description: Describe the relationship between a series of historical events, scientific ideas or concepts, or steps in technical procedures in a text, using language that pertains to time, sequence, and cause/effect.

1ED21230DFE80131A9EF68A86D17958E.description: Determine the main idea of a text; recount the key details and explain how they support the main idea.

1ED1C820DFE80131A9EE68A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of a text, referring explicitly to the text as the basis for the answers.

1ED0DF70DFE80131A9EB68A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, at the high end of the grades 2—3 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

1ED091E0DFE80131A9EA68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

1ECFDE60DFE80131A9E868A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the themes, settings, and plots of stories written by the same author about the same or similar characters (e.g., in books from a series).

1ECF8C00DFE80131A9E768A86D17958E.description: Explain how specific aspects of a text's illustrations contribute to what is conveyed by the words in a story (e.g., create mood, emphasize aspects of a character or setting).

1ECEE540DFE80131A9E568A86D17958E.description: Distinguish their own point of view from that of the narrator or those of the characters.

1ECE87F0DFE80131A9E468A86D17958E.description: Refer to parts of stories, dramas, and poems when writing or speaking about a text, using terms such as chapter, scene, and stanza; describe how each successive part builds on earlier sections.

1E9157E0DFE80131A9E368A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, distinguishing literal from nonliteral language.

1E90AC10DFE80131A9E168A86D17958E.description: Describe characters in a story (e.g., their traits, motivations, or feelings) and explain how their actions contribute to the sequence of events.

1E905070DFE80131A9E068A86D17958E.description: Recount stories, including fables, folktales, and myths from diverse cultures; determine the central message, lesson, or moral and explain how it is conveyed through key details in the text.

1E8FECD0DFE80131A9DF68A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of a text, referring explicitly to the text as the basis for the answers.

1E8EB6A0DFE80131A9DC68A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

1E8E6BA0DFE80131A9DB68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

1E8E1EB0DFE80131A9DA68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

1E8DCE70DFE80131A9D968A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

1E8D7510DFE80131A9D868A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.
comments: Please see "Research to Build and Present Knowledge" in Writing and "Comprehension and Collaboration" in Speaking and Listening for additional standards relevant to gathering, assessing, and applying information from print and digital sources.

1E8CDD40DFE80131A9D668A86D17958E.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

1E8C8E70DFE80131A9D568A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

1E8B8A00DFE80131A9D268A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

1E8B3340DFE80131A9D168A86D17958E.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

1E8ADC80DFE80131A9D068A86D17958E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.
