107F3670DFE80131913D68A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.

Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.
107EE2F0DFE80131913C68A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.

comments: Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

103FF9F0DFE80131913868A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

103F4DC0DFE80131913668A86D17958E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

document.title: Washington State K-12 Science Learning Standards

E391E820E37A4815941DB5EEB1C846DB.description: Plan and carry out fair tests in which variables are controlled and failure points are considered to identify aspects of a model or prototype that can be improved.

E831E8C84096415494CA471AF19CD239.description: Generate and compare multiple possible solutions to a problem based on how well each is likely to meet the criteria and constraints of the problem.

8F286F4274C94D49B9BA3E70C2729557.description: Define a simple design problem reflecting a need or a want that includes specified criteria for success and constraints on materials, time, or cost.

B84D1E5D3A9B46999CAF6B3AE1CDE049.description: Obtain and combine information about ways individual communities use science ideas to protect the Earth's resources and environment.

comments: Assessment Boundary: Assessment is limited to oceans, lakes, rivers, glaciers, ground water, and polar ice caps, and does not include the atmosphere.
A5BEB0F12549404CA2940ECC3C2AC5E8.description: Describe and graph the amounts and percentages of water and fresh water in various reservoirs to provide evidence about the distribution of water on Earth.

517BAD686B9547F8BBCFD40EE30802E2.description: Develop a model using an example to describe ways the geosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere, and/or atmosphere interact.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples could include the influence of the ocean on ecosystems, landform shape, and climate; the influence of the atmosphere on landforms and ecosystems through weather and climate; and the influence of mountain ranges on winds and clouds in the atmosphere. The geosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere, and biosphere are each a system.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment is limited to the interactions of two systems at a time.

163373616D2144E8B5BCF0F81715EF3A.description: Represent data in graphical displays to reveal patterns of daily changes in length and direction of shadows, day and night, and the seasonal appearance of some stars in the night sky.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of patterns could include the position and motion of Earth with respect to the sun and selected stars that are visible only in particular months.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include causes of seasons.

070DE5718A2C46BAA3E8D1E2DD0ABF74.description: Support an argument that differences in the apparent brightness of the sun compared to other stars is due to their relative distances from Earth.
comments: Assessment Boundary: Assessment is limited to relative distances, not sizes, of stars. Assessment does not include other factors that affect apparent brightness (such as stellar masses, age, stage).

B7115BFC374E48F3B988F56095451851.description: Develop a model to describe the movement of matter among plants, animals, decomposers, and the environment.
comments: Clarifcation Statement: Emphasis is on the idea that matter that is not food (air, water, decomposed materials in soil) is changed by plants into matter that is food. Examples of systems could include organisms, ecosystems, and the Earth.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include molecular explanations.

5A32F790064F4E83BB2D61B5C4406620.description: Support an argument that plants get the materials they need for growth chiefly from air and water.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on the idea that plant matter comes mostly from air and water, not from the soil.

C96528E41D5142BAB8AA0ED8D184E3F9.description: From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of models could include diagrams, and flow charts.
1C7AD9C481FA45A98C4C8BFA77F80378.description: Use models to describe that energy in animals' food (used for body repair, growth, motion, and to maintain body warmth) was once energy from the sun.

comments: Clarification Statement: "Down" is a local description of the direction that points toward the center of the spherical Earth.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include mathematical representation of gravitational force.
005702CCC3AE46898B70599785345DCB.description: Support an argument that the gravitational force exerted by Earth on objects is directed down.

8DF36B2402FC42F1B048E7F3B42B36E0.description: Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions

BC95AAE866FE4C56AF4E427582D71974.description: Conduct an investigation to determine whether the mixing of two or more substances results in new substances.

7012E35DB79C4607942FBF42BCA2DF18.description: Make observations and measurements to identify materials based on their properties.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of materials to be identified could include baking soda and other powders, metals, minerals, and liquids. Examples of properties could include color, hardness, reflectivity, electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, response to magnetic forces, and solubility; density is not intended as an identifiable property.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include density or distinguishing mass and weight.
Clarification Statement: Examples of reactions or changes could include phase changes, dissolving, and mixing that form new substances.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include distinguishing mass and weight.
BD54477305FB488995BC0D5874C943F2.description: Measure and graph quantities to provide evidence that regardless of the type of change that occurs when heating, cooling, or mixing substances, the total weight of matter is conserved.

36265C8A2F0E47F08A52CCDA29550230.description: Develop a model to describe that matter is made of particles too small to be seen.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of evidence could include adding air to expand a basketball, compressing air in a syringe, dissolving sugar in water, and evaporating salt water.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include the atomic-scale mechanism of evaporation and condensation or defining the unseen particles.

178D5E10DFE801319CC068A86D17958E.description: Applies, analyzes, and creates artworks using visual arts styles and genres of various artists, cultures, places, and times.

178D1630DFE801319CBF68A86D17958E.description: Understands and applies visual arts genres and styles of various artists, cultures, and times.

178BF4D0DFE801319CBB68A86D17958E.description: Uses technology to create two-dimensional artworks.

178C8C90DFE801319CBD68A86D17958E.description: Uses a variety of art media and techniques in two- and three-dimensions to achieve specific purposes.

178CD220DFE801319CBE68A86D17958E.description: Uses the skills of drawing, painting, and forming to achieve specific purposes.

178B55F0DFE801319CB968A86D17958E.description: Develops and implements the skills, techniques, and processes of visual arts.

178B0ED0DFE801319CB868A86D17958E.description: Applies color theory and techniques in a variety of media to produce artworks.

178C4430DFE801319CBC68A86D17958E.description: Uses perceptual skills to create imagery from observation and imagination.

178AC5D0DFE801319CB768A86D17958E.description: Analyzes and applies the skills and techniques of visual arts to create original works of art in two and/or three dimensions.

178A7930DFE801319CB668A86D17958E.description: Develops visual arts skills and techniques.

178A2760DFE801319CB568A86D17958E.description: Selects, uses, and produces artworks that combine the principles of design.

17893190DFE801319CB268A86D17958E.description: Examines and discusses how artists (including the student him/herself) use the principles of design to develop artistic compositions.

1788DB80DFE801319CB168A86D17958E.description:
Examines, develops, and creates works of art in a variety of two- and three-dimensional media by using and combining:
  • Repetition/pattern
  • Contrast
  • Variety
  • Balance (symmetrical, asymmetrical, and radial)
  • Movement and rhythm
  • Proportion
  • Emphasis/dominance (developed through the use of contrastof color, size/placement, balance, proportion, and movement/rhythm)
  • Harmony and unity (developed through the use of similarities in compositions)

1789D2C0DFE801319CB468A86D17958E.description: Identifies, examines, classifies, and uses the patterns and types of balance found in nature, in man-made environments, and in works of art.

17887BA0DFE801319CB068A86D17958E.description: Uses patterns to enhance the surfaces of shapes and forms in a variety of two- and three-dimensional works of art.

17898490DFE801319CB368A86D17958E.description: Explores and creates patterns, movement, and rhythm by using the repetition of lines, shapes, and colors.

174C4E20DFE801319CAF68A86D17958E.description: Applies, analyzes, and creates repetition/pattern, contrast, variety, balance, movement/rhythm, and proportion in a work of art.

174B58E0DFE801319CAC68A86D17958E.description:

  • Mood.
  • Energy of color.
  • Pigment versus light.
  • Subtractive versus additive color.

174BF380DFE801319CAE68A86D17958E.description:
Differentiates between, mixes, produces, and uses—in various artworks and using a variety media—the following:
  • Primary colors (yellow, red, blue).
  • Secondary colors (orange, green, purple/violet); created by mixing primary colors (yellow + red = orange).
  • Warm colors (yellow, orange, red) and cool colors (blue, green, violet).
  • Intermediate (tertiary) colors; created by mixing selected primary and secondary colors (yellow + green = yellow-green).
  • Tints and shades (to show color value, monochromatic color schemes).
  • Complementary color pairs.
  • Language of color.
  • Analogous colors.
  • Hue, value, and intensities of color.
  • Neutrals and semi-neutrals (such as red and green to produce browns; purple and yellow to produce earth tones and grays).
  • Advancing and receding color in space.

174B9EF0DFE801319CAD68A86D17958E.description: Uses the color wheel to examine relationships between color schemes, such as primary, secondary, tertiary/intermediate, and complementary color schemes.

174B12F0DFE801319CAB68A86D17958E.description: Applies, analyzes, and creates the elements of visual arts when producing a work of art.

174A2160DFE801319CA868A86D17958E.description: Develops space realistically and expressively in works of art in a variety of media.

174A6F90DFE801319CA968A86D17958E.description: Examines, practices, and uses the techniques of one-point perspective in various environments and works of two- and three-dimensional art to enhance the illusion of depth.

174AC4A0DFE801319CAA68A86D17958E.description:

  • Baseline
  • Over/under
  • Above/below
  • Beside
  • Behind/in front
  • Foreground
  • Middle ground
  • Background
  • Overlap
  • Size
  • Placement on a page
  • Detail/diminishing detail
  • Color/diminishing color
  • Positive and negative space/shape
  • One-point perspective
  • Advancing and receding colors

1749D010DFE801319CA768A86D17958E.description: Applies, analyzes, and creates the elements of visual arts when producing a work of art.

17496EF0DFE801319CA668A86D17958E.description: Develops textures realistically and imaginatively in works of art in a variety of media, styles, and subject matter.

17491680DFE801319CA568A86D17958E.description:
Differentiates between, selects, and produces a variety of textures in various environments, in works of two- and three-dimensional art, and in a variety of media to demonstrate and portray:
  • Visual/implied texture
  • Actual texture

1748C140DFE801319CA468A86D17958E.description: Applies, analyzes, and creates the elements of visual arts when producing a work of art.

17481BB0DFE801319CA268A86D17958E.description:
Examines and produces a range of five values in two- and three-dimensional artworks in a variety of media to demonstrate/establish:
  • The illusion of form on a two-dimensional surface.
  • The illusion of depth/space (foreground, middle ground, and background).
  • Shadows and a source of illumination in artworks.
  • Emphasis.
  • Focal point.
  • Values in neutrals.
  • Modeling techniques.

1747BF10DFE801319CA168A86D17958E.description:
Examines, selects, and produces a range of four or more values in various environments and works of art in a variety of media; demonstrates and produces:
  • A value scale of black and white and four levels of gray (see the glossary for an example).
  • A monochromatic value scale, including a range of four intermediate color values (see the glossary for an example).
  • Two- and three-dimensional artworks that incorporate five levels of value.
  • A value scale in which repeating lines and shapes are used to generate five levels of value.

17487690DFE801319CA368A86D17958E.description: Examines and discusses the use of value in a variety of artworks.

174762C0DFE801319CA068A86D17958E.description: Applies, analyzes, and creates the elements of visual arts when producing a work of art.

17467B60DFE801319C9D68A86D17958E.description: Examines and discusses shapes and forms in a variety of artworks.

17460C90DFE801319C9C68A86D17958E.description: Uses a variety of construction techniques and materials to create three-dimensional sculptures and functional forms for a specific purpose.

17471190DFE801319C9F68A86D17958E.description: Selects and produces shapes and/or forms expressively in a variety of two- and three-dimensional artworks.

1746CAD0DFE801319C9E68A86D17958E.description:
Differentiates between, selects, and produces shapes and forms in a variety of styles, artworks, and media, including digital media, to demonstrate:
  • Geometric shapes and forms.
  • Organic shapes and forms.
  • Free-form shapes and forms.
  • Positive and negative shapes.
  • The illusion of three-dimensional form on a two-dimensional surface.
  • Realism.

1745AFA0DFE801319C9B68A86D17958E.description: Applies, analyzes, and creates the elements of visual arts when producing a work of art.

17455FE0DFE801319C9A68A86D17958E.description: Examines and discusses how line personality impacts the expressive qualities of an artwork.

17451B50DFE801319C9968A86D17958E.description: Uses converging lines in one-point linear perspective to create the illusion of space.

1744D1F0DFE801319C9868A86D17958E.description:
Selects, uses, and produces a variety of types and qualities of line for artistic purposes in two- and three-dimensional artworks in a variety of media and to demonstrate and portray the following features and functions of line:
  • Direction
  • Expression/emotion
  • Movement/dynamic line
  • Shape
  • Textures
  • Patterns
  • Imaginative drawing
  • Observational/realistic drawing
  • Form
  • Detail
  • Outline
  • Contours/blind contours
  • Design
  • Space
  • Value (five levels)
  • Gesture
  • Sketch lines
  • Line personality
  • Converging lines in one-point perspective

17448B70DFE801319C9768A86D17958E.description: Applies, analyzes, and creates the elements of visual arts when producing a work of art.

17444230DFE801319C9668A86D17958E.description: Understands and applies visual arts concepts and vocabulary.

1743ED30DFE801319C9568A86D17958E.description: The student understands and applies arts knowledge and skills in dance, music, theatre, and visual arts.

document.title: Washington State K-12 Science Learning Standards

50C75AA20E634B839F2B40006F3E286B.description: Analyze data from tests of two objects designed to solve the same problem to compare the strengths and weaknesses of how each performs.

F83DEDD070144B66A74C4D9B87B5F837.description: Develop a simple sketch, drawing, or physical model to illustrate how the shape of an object helps it function as needed to solve a given problem.

2114E06AABC246099174F4B402129D42.description: Ask questions, make observations, and gather information about a situation people want to change to define a simple problem that can be solved through the development of a new or improved object or tool.

BDE3739465B54EC49986B8144236A6EB.description: Obtain information to identify where water is found on Earth and that it can be solid or liquid.

comments: Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include quantitative scaling in models.
4BDF90C3C9E64D2D80CC74BD53ED31B4.description: Develop a model to represent the shapes and kinds of land and bodies of water in an area.

32AFFA188CB6416284A040B9839C66B3.description: Compare multiple solutions designed to slow or prevent wind or water from changing the shape of the land.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of solutions could include different designs of dikes and windbreaks to hold back wind and water, and different designs for using shrubs, grass, and trees to hold back the land.

E119E91D27EC429D8A02C91D6DE5EC29.description: Use information from several sources to provide evidence that Earth events can occur quickly or slowly.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of events and timescales could include volcanic explosions and earthquakes, which happen quickly and erosion of rocks, which occurs slowly.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include quantitative measurements of timescales.

89AE7A51C6FC459DBB36DFE139B0002A.description: Make observations of plants and animals to compare the diversity of life in different habitats.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on the diversity of living things in each of a variety of different habitats.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include specific animal and plant names in specific habitats.

19D0A699024349E5B32523990339D905.description: Develop a simple model that mimics the function of an animal in dispersing seeds or pollinating plants.

comments: Assessment Boundary: Assessment is limited to testing one variable at a time.
59890716AFC14927893CDFB3C4DE4741.description: Plan and conduct an investigation to determine if plants need sunlight and water to grow.

4F38D8FB80CE4D499777F103F642CA64.description: Construct an argument with evidence that some changes caused by heating or cooling can be reversed and some cannot.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of reversible changes could include materials such as water and butter at different temperatures. Examples of irreversible changes could include cooking an egg, freezing a plant leaf, and heating paper.
Clarification Statement: Examples of pieces could include blocks, building bricks, or other assorted small objects.
E52BDA4280EE4BCB962800DAC8FD6ADE.description: Make observations to construct an evidence-based account of how an object made of a small set of pieces can be disassembled and made into a new object.

E46A6DA9D1B74AB68AD9B57C3BE368EC.description: Analyze data obtained from testing different materials to determine which materials have the properties that are best suited for an intended purpose.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of properties could include, strength, flexibility, hardness, texture, and absorbency.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment of quantitative measurements is limited to length.
Clarification Statement: Observations could include color, texture, hardness, and flexibility. Patterns could include the similar properties that different materials share.
6A06B346AF434927B4644928061726EA.description: Plan and conduct an investigation to describe and classify different kinds of materials by their observable properties.

C50FC20F85774FD4B1800CF97827F4FC.description: 9: (DPI) Deliberating Public Issues: I can engage in constructive civil dialogue characterized by listening respectfully and valuing diverse perspectives, responding with reasoned contributions, and building on others’ ideas to collectively deepen understanding or reach conclusions.

54D9E2F0D05C493989661A30A7501039.description: 8: (CER) Claim-Evidence-Reasoning: I can develop inquiry questions and identify sources that lead to accurate, sufficient, and complete answers by evaluating the reasoning behind claims; the credibility and validity of evidence; and considering multiple viewpoints.

65AC1F0B1D2C4FD395F6752C1C61FE65.description: 7: (I&E) Inquiry & Evaluation: I can develop inquiry questions and identify sources that lead to accurate, sufficient, and complete answers by evaluating the reasoning behind claims; the credibility and validity of evidence; and considering multiple viewpoints.

5FA1CC0BC15144C9B404381FBD06BBE8.description: 6: (E&I) Equity & Identity: I can explain the harmful impacts of bias, privilege, power, and injustice in the world and recognize diverse experiences in their social, political, economic, and historical contexts rather than in ways that are oversimplified. I am developing language and historical and cultural knowledge that recognize and accurately describe how people’s multiple identities interact and create unique and complex individuals.

3DBDAAC3F8014FF3853337DF986B0F99.description: 5: (PPP) Sustainability: I can explain how the health of social, ecological, and economic systems determines the sustainability of natural and human communities at local, regional, national, tribal, and global scales (the triple bottom line of people, planet, and prosperity). I consider the impact of personal and collective action on current and future generations.

3C219B2726CC49BB8789117CE45BBB01.description: 4: (SA) Spatial Analysis: I can interpret maps, tables, charts, graphs, and other sources to identify geographic patterns, relationships, trends, and outcomes across geographic scales (local, tribal, national, regional, global).

2A6B1B60BE2248529DAEC3D9E615F1C2.description: 3.3 (SPS) Population & Migration: I can explain how changes in population have long- and short-term effects on a place’s culture, politics, economy, environment, and demography. [Population Policies, Women and Demographic Change, & Aging Populations]

BBB999C3B25A4CD6A2D3CCEED2D1C133.description: 3.2 (SPS) Cultural Identity: Thinking Geographically: I can explain how and why cultural ideas, practices, and innovations change or disappear over time. [Historical and Contemporary Causes of Diffusion, Effects of Diffusion]

488C8C97C6954AC5A843C1BCB67226D2.description: 2.3 (IMP) Population & Migration: I can explain how changes in population are due to mortality, fertility, and migration, which are influenced by the interplay of social, political, economic, environmental, and demographic factors. 7C8C2B517D83491183A678AF5E7B56BB.description: 1.3 (PSO) Population & Migration: I can explain how global social, political, economic, environmental, and demographic patterns influence where and how people live. document.title: The Washington State K-12 Educational Technology Standards

8EF77B5A89BA4A73A7D7E499AC413EED.description: Students explore local and global issues and use collaborative technologies to work with others to investigate solutions.

F8084D938AC94E1C8654678496FE7C4D.description: Students contribute constructively to project teams, assuming various roles and responsibilities to work effectively toward a common goal.

18183DE5F5C64D0FB8D814F8CDFA5BAE.description: Students use collaborative technologies to work with others, including peers, experts or community members, to examine issues and problems from multiple viewpoints.

9F825143D73740599D4A6F6656FE828E.description: Students use digital tools to connect with learners from a variety of backgrounds and cultures, engaging with them in ways that broaden mutual understanding and learning.

6F324F4D77FC4351B033D1C99D6290F8.description: Global Collaborator - Students use digital tools to broaden their perspectives and enrich their learning by collaborating with others and working effectively in teams locally and globally.

C957C95E95C347109B0A13CB496CDBED.description: Students publish or present content that customizes the message and medium for their intended audiences.

EA7565447032436AB2165DAB146DBC0D.description: Students communicate complex ideas clearly and effectively by creating or using a variety of digital objects such as visualizations, models or simulations.

5B4052FB53AA45DCB9A2A316BC2D1D20.description: Students create original works or responsibly repurpose or remix digital resources into new creations.

B03BE037713B4EF7865FEC529EBDF8A9.description: Students choose the appropriate platforms and tools for meeting the desired objectives of their creation or communication.

4125C8F9B9FD4C1DA7D4D7EA94AE5D49.description: Creative Communicator - Students communicate clearly and express themselves creatively for a variety of purposes using the platforms, tools, styles, formats and digital media appropriate to their goals.

34719EB315E849F5B6A40400DB49C728.description: Students understand how automation works and use algorithmic thinking to develop a sequence of steps to create and test automated solutions.

0222BA78A5BC4871AE8969474B78FB24.description: Students break problems into component parts, extract key information, and develop descriptive models to understand complex systems or facilitate problem-solving.

8F974072442C4741AF2E0843129C0AE8.description: Students collect data or identify relevant data sets, use digital tools to analyze them, and represent data in various ways to facilitate problem-solving and decision-making.

C73A07F7CFBD4A4E8FE70154DDBAC18E.description: Students formulate problem definitions suited for technology-assisted methods such as data analysis, abstract models and algorithmic thinking in exploring and finding solutions.

A28E4831858A491A8869A0DA756D62A3.description: Computational Thinker - Students develop and employ strategies for understanding and solving problems in ways that leverage the power of technological methods to develop and test solutions.

CD2B5636BD334243AF4B6145963D46B2.description: Students exhibit a tolerance for ambiguity, perseverance and the capacity to work with open-ended problems.

46B64F34368F4A69A7B5EF9AC2796ACA.description: Students develop, test and refine prototypes as part of a cyclical design process.

CBE295462B4F443087ABDE277CB92480.description: Students select and use digital tools to plan and manage a design process that considers design constraints and calculated risks.

A36E26DB7B9D4D8B9952030F55F84B71.description: Students know and use a deliberate design process for generating ideas, testing theories, creating innovative artifacts or solving authentic problems.

43532AFC22264C2390C5A59EC0FB2811.description: Innovative Designer - Students use a variety of technologies within a design process to identify and solve problems by creating new, useful or imaginative solutions.

306A66C89D634E5FAD4849A091EBBA9A.description: Students build knowledge by actively exploring real-world issues and problems, developing ideas and theories and pursuing answers and solutions.

260C1CA73A384BBC902DD57F8668F55B.description: Students curate information from digital resources using a variety of tools and methods to create collections of artifacts that demonstrate meaningful connections or conclusions.

57ABBA9336C540D5960D369F25C33ECE.description: Students evaluate the accuracy, perspective, credibility and relevance of information, media, data or other resources.

557A712E8CF746F7A94537A2AED324A2.description: Students plan and employ effective research strategies to locate information and other resources for their intellectual or creative pursuits.

75925A0B2B4848BAAB7F8D18862A3D04.description: Knowledge Constructor - Students critically curate a variety of resources using digital tools to construct knowledge, produce creative artifacts and make meaningful learning experiences for themselves and others.

503B3D91A20C4997B9F3BC754345A56E.description: Students manage their personal data to maintain digital privacy and security and are aware of data-collection technology used to track their navigation online

22CD8735CF5A438794E6727C5D805E38.description: Students demonstrate an understanding of and respect for the rights and obligations of using and sharing intellectual property.

A8B683E7945F4AEA815B2DAC9B820416.description: Students engage in positive, safe, legal and ethical behavior when using technology, including social interactions online or when using networked devices.

0D2BFC496B384094833B1A47FED70482.description: Students cultivate and manage their digital identity and reputation and are aware of the permanence of their actions in the digital world.

29AA51CAB3E744DF9B421E90BE1BC96D.description: Digital Citizen - Students recognize the rights, responsibilities and opportunities of living, learning and working in an interconnected digital world, and they act and model in ways that are safe, legal and ethical.

48FEA6654A9E4ED08DD39EB74CD7B653.description: Students understand the fundamental concepts of technology operations, demonstrate the ability to choose, use and troubleshoot current technologies and are able to transfer their knowledge to explore emerging technologies.

9908705140C641FB8AA0E901AF7BFD28.description: Students use technology to seek feedback that informs and improves their practice and to demonstrate their learning in a variety of ways.

2813E5AC07F5473EAE684F14BF5507D1.description: Students builed networks and customize their learning environments in ways that support the learning process.

B93211E3D0DE4F39A02BFF56268C2EAE.description: Students articulate and set personal learning goals, develop strategies leveraging technology to achieve them and relfect on the learning process itself to improve learning outcomes.

9A8AC55A73214AF89D6F1E938FB5CF22.description: Empowered Learner - Students leverage technology to take an active role in choosing, achieving and demonstrating competency in their learning goals, informed by the learning sciences.

1EDC32F812354321B5F96A8F5460EA34.description:
Lifelong Learning: Learners set goals and reflect on their progress in using languages for enjoyment,
enrichment, and advancement.

School and Global Communities: Learners use the language both within and beyond the classroom
to interact and collaborate in their community and the globalized world.

Communities: Communicate and interact with cultural competence in order to participate in multilingual communities at home
and around the world

culture through comparisons of the cultures studied and their own.

Language Comparisons: Learners use the language to investigate, explain, and reflect on the nature
of language through comparisons of the language studied and their own.

diverse perspectives that are available through the language and its cultures.

89926E66E1174A11B7EB2FAAFA101D15.description:
Making Connections: Learners build, reinforce, and expand their
knowledge of other disciplines while using the language to develop critical
thinking and to solve problems creatively.

1E038098E5B1427F94273D85E1D80F04.description:
Connections: Connect with other disciplines and acquire information and diverse perspectives
in order to use the language to function in academic and career-related situations

explain, and reflect on the relationship between the products and perspectives of the cultures studied.

38259472CAC04B88A95BE8E12E498ED4.description:

explain, and reflect on the relationship between the practices and perspectives of the cultures
studied.

3780E00B18444C0DA4D51FE730E96A3A.description: Cultures: Interact with cultural competence and understanding

ideas to inform, explain, persuade, and narrate on a variety of topics using appropriate media and
adapting to various audiences of listeners, readers, or viewers.

78ACB14F0FA046DF850ED3BBC8F1601A.description:
Interpretive Communication: Learners understand, interpret, and analyze
what is heard, read, or viewed on a variety of topics.

9A81BE292A374093AD65BE53518F0172.description:
Interpersonal Communication: Learners interact and negotiate meaning
in spoken, signed, or written conversations to share information, reactions,
feelings, and opinions.

128AF443F9894B95B61C99F221144D90.description:
Communication: Communicate effectively in more than one language in order to function in a variety of situations and for multiple

variables are related to solve problems in context by fitting functions to the data and explaining
trends and relationships within the data.

DEA23003A79744F3B886B3B99A0FD076.description:
Summarize categorical data for two categories in two-way frequency tables. Interpret
relative frequencies in the context of the data (including joint, marginal, and conditional relative
frequencies). Recognize possible associations and trends in the data.

E397F836A79D444195D35DC2510C7FF1.description:
Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative
variables.

2DA6F5307022436C9B161B6978155A22.description:
Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets,
accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers).

64A5003F2ED549FFB059D3F3F65F7FED.description:
Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (median, mean)
and spread (interquartile range, standard deviation) of two or more different data sets.

5E70DF97E6784BB195BBB42DF6C44226.description: Represent data with plots on the real number line (dot plots, histograms, and box plots).

237D2A994C054096A80D1E3F5F5AA39E.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable.

E51F184F70A14B4BB797953C26823DAC.description: Interpret the parameters in a linear or exponential function in terms of a context.

382C0C5FEFE64E90BF923A46BC0BDAC1.description: Interpret expressions for functions in terms of the situation they model.

81FD88F831FF491AA51D41AEE1772925.description:
Observe using graphs and tables that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually
exceeds a quantity increasing linearly, quadratically.

703A33A029AF4457A404CE8D8BD57846.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately construct linear and exponential functions given a
graph, a description of a relationship, or two input-output pairs (include reading these from a
table).

4D183385E57C4A818C3812F15007B9CB.description:
Distinguish between situations that can be modeled with linear functions (equal differences over
equal intervals) and with exponential functions (equal factors over equal intervals), recognizing
constant rates per unit interval, and growth or decay by a constant percent rate per unit interval.

9A9ACEE5C4014AFE89B8F91000B30782.description:
Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve
problems.

07126D00731E41D1AB4FF130A15166AC.description:
Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, k f(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for
specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Using a
variety of strategies, experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph
using technology.

A8A58A1405564103AC4A9DA56CFBCD32.description: Build new functions from existing functions.

4538A2E107654C9DBA0DF060EFD3280F.description:
Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively and with an explicit formula,
use them to model linear and exponential situations, and translate between two forms.

9498DF7D639346CDB96CAC3BC11BF7C4.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately write a function that describes a relationship between two
quantities, including linear and exponential arithmetic and geometric sequences in context.

191B6CF9745C493C9C683502FEFDE388.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.

CF6CF8511DDA4FEF82BD8191879E2C4F.description:
Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically,
numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions). Functions could be linear, exponential, or
quadratic.

5D3812A246BC47379858EDE706007377.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately write a function defined by an expression in different but
equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties of the function including zeros and
symmetry, using factoring for quadratic functions and integer constants for time with exponential
growth and decay.

1A1200334F194DE08C2911D6CEFA78A6.description:
Graph linear, exponential, and quadratic functions expressed symbolically and show key features of
the graph, including intercepts, maximum, minimum, and interpreting end behavior for exponential
functions by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.

620E3C1B84444BA189C294182E630E23.description:
Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (represented symbolically or as a
table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.

A0EFD1CECC07415FAEE7E9671429BED7.description:
Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship
it describes in linear, exponential, or quadratic contexts.

DAAE67C8A4B14E5592C4E9341B62F573.description:
For a function that models a relationship between two quantities in context, interpret key features
of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a
verbal description of the relationship. Key features include intercepts; intervals where the function
is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries for
functions including linear, exponential, and quadratic.

F211CA019B024E9E8C844E3EF8D2F493.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context.

ACFACE6558774DD699F8245A29600C55.description:
Recognize that sequences are functions, sometimes defined recursively, whose domain is a subset
of the integers.

549AA162DCC74C7CBC62DFB6560D72BB.description:
Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret statements that
use function notation in terms of a context.

22097161CA9D422DACF2A5DC5F0741B4.description:
Understand that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range)
assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range. If 𝑓𝑓 is a function and x is
an element of its domain, then 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) denotes the output of f corresponding to the input 𝑥𝑥. The
graph of f is the graph of the equation 𝑦𝑦 = 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥).

93181C4E92634ED7A966E57C06E697DF.description: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation.

8B9FC82F33344353A5B9AFBB00CABC9E.description:
Graph the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half-plane (excluding the boundary
in the case of a strict inequality), and graph the solution set to a system of linear inequalities in two
variables as the intersection of the corresponding half-planes.

A521AD08C5CB4178AAD96A740E745818.description:
Using a variety of strategies explain the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the
equations 𝑦𝑦 = 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) and 𝑦𝑦 = 𝑔𝑔(𝑥𝑥) intersect are the solutions of the equation 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) = 𝑔𝑔(𝑥𝑥); find
the solutions approximately, e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make tables of values,
or find successive approximations. Include cases where 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) and/or 𝑔𝑔(𝑥𝑥) are linear, exponential,
and quadratic.

7FCF4E8011DA4C9792654721F76DCE4E.description:
Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in
the coordinate plane, often forming a curve (which could be a line).

3AA289DD0B624C5C8325EA4E976AA2AC.description: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically.

583DE572934B46B0AB53F32D67D7C967.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately solve a simple system consisting of a linear equation
and a quadratic equation in two variables algebraically and graphically.

5AE29F2A7DE3466D957D73DDA83A5960.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately solve systems of linear equations exactly and
approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.

70E421AF0A6F4BA5BE80C73D0AF4F4FA.description:
Demonstrate using a variety of strategies that, given a system of two equations in two
variables, replacing one equation by the sum of that equation and a multiple of the other produces
a system with the same solutions.

E32B32CB25834CB6B0A2EF575C856205.description:
Solve quadratic equations in one variable by inspection, taking square roots, and
factoring as appropriate to the initial form of the equation.

92A340DCB668436283FBC6C7F7EB0A79.description:
Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients
represented by letters.

5A01731A2AE94A69A6CF34732A3E73F5.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.

5F7C09EFDC534DC197D74BCB61DB59D8.description:
Explain each step in solving an equation as following from the equality of numbers asserted at the
previous step flexibly, efficiently, and accurately selecting and demonstrating use of strategies to
solve equations, starting from the assumption that the original equation has a solution. Construct a
viable argument to justify a solution method.

B12FF57072A24AB4BE15D0515A82B7AE.description: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning.

DA5EDD183EE645AB830936DA317B7DD4.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the
same reasoning as in solving equations within linear, quadratic, and exponential equations.

B35B2848A21C4522A5C283DD2D111202.description:
Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities,
and interpret solutions as viable or nonviable options in a modeling context within linear,
quadratic, and exponential equations.

E9E903715B574B1E91BB95E270D91017.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately create linear, quadratic, exponential equations to represent
relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.

75ECC9D7A1E04B4E916019531E12DC01.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them
to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear, quadratic, and exponential functions.

E7FC1B42C6D345948842BB7842D05528.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.

5B8A440567B64253BBF216EDD4864C79.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately demonstrate that polynomials form a system similar
to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and
multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials.

90A504D0CFF24EEEB75B1DA827B57D2B.description: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions

602283D67DC34625BA1F510B7463FB42.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately create an equivalent form of an expression to reveal and explain
properties of the quantity represented by the expression including factoring quadratic expressions
and using properties of exponents to create equivalent forms of exponential expressions to reveal
properties of interest in the function.

CBDBBDE9AEF74F84BD8D98BD0DE87E8C.description: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems.

D6163E41C1C44BB788C39993FCA3E3AB.description:
Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it within exponential and quadratic
functions.

B0E0508D54A24FFA834E8BF7283FF5F9.description:
Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context within linear, exponential, and
quadratic functions.

C6C3709F4B7D4E409158CD5354E39073.description: Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on measurement when reporting quantities.

6F452723063C4DEA88A0715867FD6EC1.description: Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive modeling.

1C91E256430C43568E444971321F1B77.description:
Use units as a way to understand problems and to guide the solution of multi-step problems;
choose and interpret units consistently in formulas; choose and interpret the scale and the origin in graphs and data displays.

436FF21C0C7A4EB7A94C32703CC4D6BB.description: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems.

189A7174AC4A4512B10DFAFB386854D7.description:
Explain why the sum or product of two rational numbers is rational; that the sum of a
rational number and an irrational number is irrational; and that the product of a nonzero rational
number and an irrational number is irrational.

2DF69CA22C464BAEB2F58E46A7AE05A7.description: Use properties of rational and irrational numbers.

56D02FE68E0646FFB86CC6F466766373.description:
Rewrite expressions involving radicals and rational exponents using the properties of exponents.
Use properties of rational and irrational numbers.

EC20B7ED55A845ACA90C9C984F49706A.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately explain how the definition of the meaning of rational exponents
follows from extending the properties of integer exponents to those values using a variety of
strategies, allowing for a notation for radicals in terms of rational exponents.

D630E80C07714DF8A3CDDE8ED1DFF748.description: Extend the properties of exponents to rational exponents.

1735E3205A4E45ABAB9704CAD4459712.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

95575F4533DB4F70A7F2345CC1FADDD8.description: Look for and make use of structure.

4CD678D4439049AB8951C59C5CBED04F.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

6A16A316238E46B8B0D96B28A4DBF965.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Public Draft WA Learning Standards Math

30887AA988EE4C178757418557535D44.description:
Acknowledge the presence of missing data values and understand how missing values may add bias to analysis and interpretation. Examine and discuss competing explanations for data
trends observed such as confounding variables. Respond to competing arguments or
interpretations of the data of different community groups, paying careful attention to what
conclusions the data supports, taking into account correlation versus causation.

770518DE8A744D03BF106B9B5A896ADC.description:
Create and analyze data sets and data displays, including but not limited to scatter plots,
regressions, histograms and boxplots using technology to sort or filter data, summarize, and
describe relationships between quantitative variables.

09311054E25E4B60B6A8CA863A7EE6BF.description:
Understand the issues of bias and confounding variables when collecting data and their
impact on interpretation. Understand practices for collecting and handling data, including sensitive
information and concerns for privacy and how that may affect data collection.

3DF58DA57E314DE997A5DB0FD671F51A.description:
Formulate multivariable statistical investigative questions and determine how data can be
collected and provide an answer, consider causality and prediction when posing the question.

4C67D4C3A3EE4D89AF816CE210BA082B.description:
Apply the Addition Rule, 𝑃𝑃(𝐴𝐴 𝑜𝑜𝑜𝑜 𝐵𝐵) = 𝑃𝑃(𝐴𝐴) + 𝑃𝑃(𝐵𝐵) − 𝑃𝑃(𝐴𝐴 𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎 𝐵𝐵), and interpret the
answer in terms of the model.

841A8BFD7B4C4AD38B099B4348AD2002.description:
Find the conditional probability of A given B as the fraction of B's outcomes that also
belong to A, and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

69D12156F0374225A3A78A2AFC7C4344.description: Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events.

0F9D9D5BAA524AA79E6F72649EB3C526.description:
Recognize and explain the concepts of conditional probability and independence in
everyday language and everyday situations.

327E44BF32EB4C3CBA3FA42357D53FC2.description:
Construct and interpret two-way frequency tables of data when two categories are
associated with each object being classified. Use the two-way table as a sample space to decide if
events are independent and to approximate conditional probabilities.

235E5A4E158C469FA7C73E3AFB8EC1BA.description:
Understand the conditional probability of 𝐴𝐴 given 𝐵𝐵 as
𝑃𝑃(𝐴𝐴 𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎 𝐵𝐵),
𝑃𝑃(𝐵𝐵) and interpret
independence of 𝐴𝐴 and 𝐵𝐵 as saying that the conditional probability of 𝐴𝐴 given 𝐵𝐵 is the same as the
probability of 𝐴𝐴, and the conditional probability of 𝐵𝐵 given 𝐴𝐴 is the same as the probability of 𝐵𝐵.

7DE3E8061BE943E69DB6F17DBE49C21E.description:
Understand that two events A and B are independent if the probability of A and B
occurring together is the product of their probabilities, and use this characterization to determine if
they are independent.

6145A7211D0646CD8ABADDB9E57F63AA.description:
Describe events as subsets of a sample space (the set of outcomes) using characteristics (or categories) of the outcomes, or as unions, intersections, or complements of other events ("or,"
"and," "not").

31785EFA142340769DFAC1D5392B37B4.description: Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data.

ABA13B42619E472FAF04B82FCF39B376.description: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability

9EFB19857EE04BBBB57BCE36A8027A81.description: Compute (using technology) and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit.

30BC948C068C46DDBDBD18921827BC36.description:
Interpret the slope (rate of change) and the intercept (constant term) of a linear model in the
context of the data.

97818527F20A434E95BD0DDE62C4BE6A.description:
Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the
variables are related to solve problems in context by fitting functions to the data and explaining
trends and relationships within the data.

A144A804A8CA4F66AAC3EA58BBC6FBF9.description:
Summarize categorical data for two categories in two-way frequency tables. Interpret
relative frequencies in the context of the data (including joint, marginal, and conditional relative
frequencies). Recognize possible associations and trends in the data.

0C69E0C8D16946F8835060BFD5FBEA92.description:
Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative
variables.

5DA7036EA2334FCC95E28BB44DCAD260.description:
Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets,
accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers).

202ED89908114908AE9B27CF16148875.description:
Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (median, mean)
and spread (interquartile range, standard deviation) of two or more different data sets.

4B599A08A5CC4EB7910900A67F9416AD.description: Represent data with plots on the real number line (dot plots, histograms, and box plots).

722C817C66FC492CAD0917FCA4D62773.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable.

EBBCB2A873AC4BCD9A84FB866A4A2E9C.description:
Apply geometric methods to solve design problems (e.g., designing an object or
structure to satisfy physical constraints or minimize cost; working with typographic grid systems
based on ratios).

D53299394CA44C11AEDD24BCA2533E6B.description:
Apply concepts of density based on area and volume in modeling situations (e.g.,
persons per square mile, BTUs per cubic foot).

3E3C04B7488E42D78496A5EFB074D78F.description:
Use geometric shapes, their measures, and their properties to describe objects (e.g.,
modeling a tree trunk or a human torso as a cylinder).

DDF2D8030915421B9484B746814849C6.description: Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations.

FC39A5530B3443458953B59CB03FC618.description:
Identify the shapes of two-dimensional cross-sections of three-dimensional objects,
and identify three-dimensional objects generated by rotations of two-dimensional objects.

A6E64CA0B69441BBA6872769684A8964.description:
Visualize relationships between two-dimensional and three-dimensional
objects.

67A3A98913C24B778E39B6E693CF8413.description: Use volume formulas for cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres to solve problems.

2C9C0F78FB1E444C97864475F98293C9.description:
Give an informal argument for the formulas for the circumference of a circle, area of a
circle, volume of a cylinder, pyramid, and cone.

00FBE4277079443184C053C71944902D.description: Explain volume formulas and use them to solve problems.

6028B95077C549FC820BF3946345A47F.description:
Use coordinates to compute perimeters of polygons and areas of triangles and
rectangles, e.g., using the distance formula.

D03E83C542AB44849E660B03B97504E5.description:
Find the point on a directed line segment between two given points that partitions the
segment in a given ratio.

9C5F8D11D91A425185A07637BA0E0B75.description:
Prove the slope criteria for parallel and perpendicular lines and use them to solve
geometric problems (e.g., find the equation of a line parallel or perpendicular to a given line that
passes through a given point).

1D021A10D8C243D0B4FF2ED6B286360C.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.

FC3DE2996D8A4FCE9B71BBEFF7CB2015.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.

2D5EE7F7F42546B1BB8BC6615CA32E56.description:
Derive the equation of a circle of given center and radius using the Pythagorean
Theorem.

7BD1172E7C3F4625A83DB7724C9FAE1A.description: Translate between the geometric description and the equation for a conic section.

B7681383F5A24A3F961AB8F569F80F73.description:
Derive using similarity the fact that the length of the arc intercepted by an angle is
proportional to the radius, and define the radian measure of the angle as the constant of proportionality; derive the formula for the area of a sector.

2325D4AF06E04998B220932969BA4E56.description: Find arc lengths and areas of sectors of circles.

1ECD17369B72409B85C8B96684F3BA6E.description:
Construct the inscribed and circumscribed circles of a triangle and flexibly, efficiently, and
accurately prove properties of angles for a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle.

3F4F7A9A51984B199B95BB45768BE01A.description:
Identify and describe relationships among inscribed angles, radii, and chords, including
how angles formed inside the circle, the circle's radius, and line segments within the circle are
related. Understand special cases including angles formed by diameters and how the circle's edge
interacts with its radius.

604FA2C912E44541931D511E2AB952D5.description: Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately prove that all circles are similar.

9848E7D97F924DB98D40F7B1671C689E.description: Understand and apply theorems about circles.

B213C3D408484BB0815B450BE6B7C5C6.description: Use trigonometric ratios and the Pythagorean Theorem to solve right triangles in applied problems.

81DC73854B594A20AE9C98FAE44B86EC.description: Explain and use the relationship between the sine and cosine of complementary angles.

7FD1D0DBE57045199DE71152A2C2F7C3.description:
Understand that by similarity, side ratios in right triangles are properties of the angles in the
triangle, leading to definitions of trigonometric ratios for acute angles.

134AAC2868C34FFF9BE82DA25CC8B9D3.description: Define trigonometric ratios and solve problems involving right triangles.

EFCF99472B11475787583DF2216B1358.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately use congruence and similarity criteria for triangles to solve
problems and to prove relationships in geometric figures.

7ED9966F568F4DDC85B57FB497910495.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately prove theorems about triangles: proportionality, triangle
similarity, and the Pythagorean Theorem.

DD3A1A01CBE24649B45D453D54D4EF02.description:
Use the properties of similarity transformations to establish the AA criterion for two
triangles to be similar.

564930780299450A8E4F3E1683496771.description:
Given two figures, use the definition of similarity in terms of similarity transformations to decide if they are similar; explain using similarity transformations the meaning of similarity for
triangles as the equality of all corresponding pairs of angles and the proportionality of all
corresponding pairs of sides.

51AEE7C2BBE84A4CA1AFA841B1C32645.description:
Verify experimentally the properties of dilations given by a center and a scale factor
by seeing what happens to lines affected by a center of dilation and how scale factor affects line
segments.

8BC897999BA84864865BE43DDE0B69BB.description: Understand similarity in terms of similarity transformations.

D41916072F05453BAF6FD6492FB7350C.description: Construct an equilateral triangle, a square, and a regular hexagon inscribed in a circle.

C805C3E072544330840C1F2DF4B9425F.description: Make formal geometric constructions with a variety of tools and methods.

89EDF71514EB4465995CC1BD56C2CD59.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately prove theorems about parallelograms: congruence of
opposite sides and opposite angles, properties of diagonals.

26653AF64BA1431A97349C4EEBEECB68.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately prove theorems about triangles: interior angles, base angles,
segments joining midpoint of two sides, and medians of a triangle.

7617E394C1304BAEBE83357008AC3442.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately prove theorems about lines and angles: vertical, transversals,
alternate interior and exterior, perpendicular bisectors, etc.

A3B18A7926B648239B77CBE1A7C4284F.description:
Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, surface area, and
volume.

AC4729B47219411AAA2C077E190569A0.description:
Explain how the criteria for triangle congruence (ASA, SAS, and SSS) follow from the definition of
congruence in terms of rigid motions.

49769F16E8C04248AB6FB7A840F1EEB3.description:
Use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to show that two triangles are
congruent if and only if corresponding pairs of sides and corresponding pairs of angles are
congruent.

550E7330A8E84D6BBAA0AE714789FD39.description:
Use geometric descriptions of rigid motions to transform figures and to predict the effect of a
given rigid motion on a given figure; given two figures, use the definition of congruence in terms of
rigid motions to decide if they are congruent.

EFA6AB19758F4B0285FFEDB432A6367C.description: Understand congruence in terms of rigid motions.

239FC9B4535D4FF68FD12093B832B5BB.description:
Given a geometric figure and a rotation, reflection, or translation, draw the transformed figure
using, e.g., graph paper, tracing paper, or geometry software. Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately specify a sequence of transformations that will carry a given figure onto another.

464D2B5A3ACA409EBD499310A0C35292.description:
Develop definitions of rotations, reflections, and translations in terms of angles, circles,
perpendicular lines, parallel lines, and line segments.

58F7DE065BBB450CB43A50FE9FF03E1B.description:
Given a rectangle, parallelogram, trapezoid, or regular polygon, describe the rotations and
reflections that carry it onto itself.

97C7715A93CE4F4D9F9CC9ED099ED300.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately represent transformations in the plane, e.g., transparencies and
geometry software; describe transformations as functions that take points in the plane as inputs
and give other points as outputs. Compare transformations that preserve distance and angle to
those that do not (e.g., translation versus horizontal stretch).

C83A1D9D94E049ECB57728AF31F2D3D2.description:
Know precise definitions of angle, circle, perpendicular line, parallel line, and line segment, based
on the undefined notions of point, line, distance along a line, and distance around a circular arc.

8C7B5B19813B49E9A003692654B7A084.description: Experiment with transformations in the plane.

64D4DC0550224050B61100D596C65F09.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

82287F150F824469889CC237E1CC07E6.description: Look for and make use of structure.

8AF2DE1EF934475F9B0F2308C1353641.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

093702D4DEC244D3BE42F8899AF72D27.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Public Draft WA Learning Standards Math

107AE6F0DE00460EB607C2E4D9E0DF60.description:
Acknowledge the presence of missing data values and understand how missing values may add bias to analysis and interpretation. Examine and discuss competing explanations for data
trends observed such as confounding variables. Respond to competing arguments or
interpretations of the data of different community groups, paying careful attention to what
conclusions the data supports, taking into account correlation versus causation.

50E7367813C0434CB2D768F3C03216E1.description:
Create and analyze data sets and data displays, including but not limited to scatter plots,
regressions, histograms and boxplots using technology to sort or filter data, summarize, and
describe relationships between quantitative variables.

C63E2B3E902345EA82D36BD3D047B464.description:
Understand the issues of bias and confounding variables when collecting data and their
impact on interpretation. Understand practices for collecting and handling data, including sensitive
information and concerns for privacy and how that may affect data collection.

7D8332A7EFC245F2BFD96E3F86A5560D.description:
Formulate multivariable statistical investigative questions and determine how data can be
collected and provide an answer, consider causality and prediction when posing the question.

F83A29EB89124D429083BA2A0E699808.description: Compute (using technology) and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit.

85991AD881C74E2C85546D9492930C2C.description:
Interpret the slope (rate of change) and the intercept (constant term) of a linear model in the
context of the data.

BBBB5B0414B94EF3A8A2DD5216854610.description:
Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the
variables are related to solve problems in context by fitting functions to the data and explaining
trends and relationships within the data.

3B968FF9A1834C538A6CE193DC29736D.description:
Summarize categorical data for two categories in two-way frequency tables. Interpret
relative frequencies in the context of the data (including joint, marginal, and conditional relative
frequencies). Recognize possible associations and trends in the data.

5E168FD0F97A4FEE86C17E38CBA8D8B3.description:
Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative
variables.

19C57155F3A347818370DD8D3F34821F.description:
Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets,
accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers).

C5E992907598438E991C0A494202E3CC.description:
Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (median, mean)
and spread (interquartile range, standard deviation) of two or more different data sets.

D0A7B94D7DA049EA8311D348B82E4F27.description: Represent data with plots on the real number line (dot plots, histograms, and box plots).

DB50FAB30D2E48D69647141EC5A29C30.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable.

AEE2ACE155A24041AEF910223E91E4C5.description:
Use coordinates to compute perimeters of polygons and areas of triangles and
rectangles, e.g., using the distance formula.

489CFDBF126D4D7582B40F2E0CCBC708.description:
Find the point on a directed line segment between two given points that partitions the
segment in a given ratio.

4BB6EF704A284770AFF83868F55FB804.description:
Prove the slope criteria for parallel and perpendicular lines and use them to solve
geometric problems (e.g., find the equation of a line parallel or perpendicular to a given line that
passes through a given point).

FB005CA9057A4C32BCC414B79B33F92F.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.

9EA042A3C87543FA90E379D402D55B6B.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.

6B3374581F78455BB4C02E373C9ED9CD.description: Construct an equilateral triangle, a square, and a regular hexagon inscribed in a circle.

B1AFCCF6A5D14D01A0250B8BC6DE2BB4.description: Make formal geometric constructions with a variety of tools and methods.

8FD7A1990CD5471F821FED86B6C7B67E.description:
Explain how the criteria for triangle congruence (ASA, SAS, and SSS) follow from the definition of
congruence in terms of rigid motions.

350D51793B0043849F9912BDCF553ED2.description:
Use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to show that two triangles are
congruent if and only if corresponding pairs of sides and corresponding pairs of angles are
congruent.

91DB7F56AEC74DE89DB0E17887BCAC7A.description:
Use geometric descriptions of rigid motions to transform figures and to predict the effect of a
given rigid motion on a given figure; given two figures, use the definition of congruence in terms of
rigid motions to decide if they are congruent.

8CD18C1D551A4F0C829D0A083B5C860F.description: Understand congruence in terms of rigid motions.

6B94C581CB4849F1B1FACF323AE25087.description:
Given a geometric figure and a rotation, reflection, or translation, draw the transformed figure
using, e.g., graph paper, tracing paper, or geometry software. Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately specify a sequence of transformations that will carry a given figure onto another.

9F2C9733E487406D85C83830DD48B8F0.description:
Develop definitions of rotations, reflections, and translations in terms of angles, circles,
perpendicular lines, parallel lines, and line segments.

6E5685788814400AABE414D3F8DA6BBB.description:
Given a rectangle, parallelogram, trapezoid, or regular polygon, describe the rotations and
reflections that carry it onto itself.

C44D4E49210E47A5893393105EE87082.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately represent transformations in the plane, e.g., transparencies and
geometry software; describe transformations as functions that take points in the plane as inputs
and give other points as outputs. Compare transformations that preserve distance and angle to
those that do not (e.g., translation versus horizontal stretch).

20966231F01C45A280E83DDFE022FE85.description:
Know precise definitions of angle, circle, perpendicular line, parallel line, and line segment, based
on the undefined notions of point, line, distance along a line, and distance around a circular arc.

D0FE61CEB6A24484B4CC109BA68EA82C.description: Experiment with transformations in the plane.

BDAD9CF1B11444E8BFB9976AE38DAA6D.description: Interpret the parameters in a linear or exponential function in terms of a context.

92FED4D62AD04A10A1A175E8FB9604E0.description: Interpret expressions for functions in terms of the situation they model.

3CDAB83ACA9544D186C301DD42BDF274.description:
Observe using graphs and tables that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually
exceeds a quantity increasing linearly, quadratically.

69E0C7FA6DC540CDA3174E0603133ACD.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately construct linear and exponential functions given a
graph, a description of a relationship, or two input-output pairs (include reading these from a
table).

CCB8049DFAE9441C8AA91BC6E3942C39.description:
Distinguish between situations that can be modeled with linear functions (equal differences over
equal intervals) and with exponential functions (equal factors over equal intervals), recognizing
constant rates per unit interval, and growth or decay by a constant percent rate per unit interval.

005F2A403CCA48D089590D70AFCCA757.description:
Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve
problems.

A05DE079C5C348C1BA236ED6F9D4F6D6.description:
Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, k f(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for
specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Using a
variety of strategies, experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph
using technology.

AC25C69BAD6F4EE197CF80E12EAC8ED8.description: Build new functions from existing functions.

CC25BB13CAB944E39ADF2FC64F71C8ED.description:
Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively and with an explicit formula,
use them to model linear and exponential situations, and translate between two forms.

D9BCBC01A57F475AA7B0C615CE7255CB.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately write a function that describes a relationship between two
quantities, including linear and exponential arithmetic and geometric sequences in context.

8C26E51FFAE347E080B028983F3CAEC5.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.

817BFF883DC04F0DB98E754DF73886EC.description:
Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically,
numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions). Functions could be linear, exponential, or
quadratic.

E8650371BBF74A48BC4BEF815AE18E45.description:
Graph linear, exponential, and quadratic functions expressed symbolically and show key features of
the graph, including intercepts, maximum, minimum, and interpreting end behavior for exponential
functions by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.

FF8430637D524E02A3EEF2EBF67379B7.description:
Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (represented symbolically or as a
table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.

46C4F38B4B63432EA31114D055671A8A.description:
Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship
it describes in linear, exponential, or quadratic contexts.

6DDAEF3F74CF4FFDAA714C0A6815C795.description:
For a function that models a relationship between two quantities in context, interpret key features
of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a
verbal description of the relationship. Key features include intercepts; intervals where the function
is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries for
functions including linear, exponential, and quadratic.

10EA72C64D21424D8ADE65E9ACD3C543.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context.

B0B2852B23494FC789AE90E922394F7A.description:
Recognize that sequences are functions, sometimes defined recursively, whose domain is a subset
of the integers.

7560C23BBDF34821B960A15417894987.description:
Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret statements that
use function notation in terms of a context.

FBF857BC662A4291994F62A2BED28786.description:
Understand that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range)
assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range. If 𝑓𝑓 is a function and x is
an element of its domain, then 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) denotes the output of f corresponding to the input 𝑥𝑥. The
graph of f is the graph of the equation 𝑦𝑦 = 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥).
