D0EBF8861D764869BCC434BAC852F921.description: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation.

4D6A23D68F0B4D8D883D02E3F3E77863.description:
Graph the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half-plane (excluding the boundary
in the case of a strict inequality), and graph the solution set to a system of linear inequalities in two
variables as the intersection of the corresponding half-planes.

8F783F48152049F48BC2CCF861A06E68.description:
Using a variety of strategies explain the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the
equations 𝑦𝑦 = 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) and 𝑦𝑦 = 𝑔𝑔(𝑥𝑥) intersect are the solutions of the equation 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) = 𝑔𝑔(𝑥𝑥); find
the solutions approximately, e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make tables of values,
or find successive approximations. Include cases where 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) and/or 𝑔𝑔(𝑥𝑥) are linear, exponential,
and quadratic.

F614A3537B20458DBD69F32004F63DB6.description:
Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in
the coordinate plane, often forming a curve (which could be a line).

7E0FC7EC5A4B4225A9221ECB1651846C.description: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically.

DAC8339772B3465DB490257ED5F15D7A.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately solve systems of linear equations exactly and
approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.

5924CF12F6294CA18DF96C42B4392FEF.description:
Demonstrate using a variety of strategies that, given a system of two equations in two
variables, replacing one equation by the sum of that equation and a multiple of the other produces
a system with the same solutions.

404BC17E42124C21A329BE218FEA537C.description:
Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients
represented by letters.

48C70AEAD7FC4CEA96835D9B05347C32.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.

0E60468D19294232B00CE918392C784E.description:
Explain each step in solving an equation as following from the equality of numbers asserted at the
previous step flexibly, efficiently, and accurately selecting and demonstrating use of strategies to
solve equations, starting from the assumption that the original equation has a solution. Construct a
viable argument to justify a solution method.

A3933CD54AE24C908F5C0CCE572C895C.description: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning.

CC9356366C074847894BDFA2152524BE.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the
same reasoning as in solving equations within linear, quadratic, and exponential equations.

B26FF598D1354A0D8EFA95993D5FC470.description:
Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities,
and interpret solutions as viable or nonviable options in a modeling context within linear,
quadratic, and exponential equations.

B5FF7566FA8C4DA6A24AF8F50DFB3419.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately create linear, quadratic, exponential equations to represent
relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.

4EAEC151895F4FCCB8E23F0F0865BAC9.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them
to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear, quadratic, and exponential functions.

E046D646DC284C8793B610E194B4D45B.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.

271D493F208A49DD866414AD0C52AF51.description:
Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context within linear, exponential, and
quadratic functions.

F12CCC22309F43FA9946F2C49BB6E942.description: Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on measurement when reporting quantities.

849C232B62BA487D8FBE8C2AD3B72229.description: Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive modeling.

D5CEE2C3FC7C4292A58A30785D0998C1.description:
Use units as a way to understand problems and to guide the solution of multi-step problems;
choose and interpret units consistently in formulas; choose and interpret the scale and the origin in graphs and data displays.

07BF6C98245040399579E247BDF31CDC.description: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems.

2FC932C567B94856B4A7674D2F68AF66.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

2BAF0C1CDD374201B3E4E4C16C1A2A96.description: Look for and make use of structure.

0FE3FBA7740546CBAFA11E2D12D486AC.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

2ABE9F83D4DC4A999F07FFC56ECFCEB9.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Public Draft WA Learning Standards Math

183156BBAA98467CBAB4A188F60520FD.description:
Acknowledge the presence of missing data values and understand how missing values may add bias to analysis and interpretation. Examine and discuss competing explanations for data
trends observed such as confounding variables. Respond to competing arguments or
interpretations of the data of different community groups, paying careful attention to what
conclusions the data supports, taking into account correlation versus causation.

7E08EAC759BF420593AAC629BA293CB7.description:
Create and analyze data sets and data displays, including but not limited to scatter plots,
regressions, histograms and boxplots using technology to sort or filter data, summarize, and
describe relationships between quantitative variables.

7306B5E057BB46EFBA7B761C9FF6098B.description:
Understand the issues of bias and confounding variables when collecting data and their
impact on interpretation. Understand practices for collecting and handling data, including sensitive
information and concerns for privacy and how that may affect data collection.

329D2AB0728E4376A05FC15B12115E11.description:
Formulate multivariable statistical investigative questions and determine how data can be
collected and provide an answer, consider causality and prediction when posing the question.

271FCAF70B8C448B9441A008E203511A.description:
Apply the Addition Rule, 𝑃𝑃(𝐴𝐴 𝑜𝑜𝑜𝑜 𝐵𝐵) = 𝑃𝑃(𝐴𝐴) + 𝑃𝑃(𝐵𝐵) − 𝑃𝑃(𝐴𝐴 𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎 𝐵𝐵), and interpret the
answer in terms of the model.

0A4E72F22198458589DD4553AA06EDBB.description:
Find the conditional probability of A given B as the fraction of B's outcomes that also
belong to A, and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

7BC2A96ADC4A48F88241DB4E638728E9.description: Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events.

5F45C7CBEEE14AA7AF4254EEC6F4800C.description:
Recognize and explain the concepts of conditional probability and independence in
everyday language and everyday situations.

C93BFE6CB8E8402387B724E437A66899.description:
Construct and interpret two-way frequency tables of data when two categories are
associated with each object being classified. Use the two-way table as a sample space to decide if
events are independent and to approximate conditional probabilities.

015FB9C8DFF6428C8E5ADDE166AA6F81.description:
Understand the conditional probability of 𝐴𝐴 given 𝐵𝐵 as
𝑃𝑃(𝐴𝐴 𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎 𝐵𝐵),
𝑃𝑃(𝐵𝐵) and interpret
independence of 𝐴𝐴 and 𝐵𝐵 as saying that the conditional probability of 𝐴𝐴 given 𝐵𝐵 is the same as the
probability of 𝐴𝐴, and the conditional probability of 𝐵𝐵 given 𝐴𝐴 is the same as the probability of 𝐵𝐵.

DB00B986190043F1A8FA1162E249830A.description:
Understand that two events A and B are independent if the probability of A and B
occurring together is the product of their probabilities, and use this characterization to determine if
they are independent.

77B338B508F445DA97CE74BBFA685DE7.description:
Describe events as subsets of a sample space (the set of outcomes) using characteristics (or categories) of the outcomes, or as unions, intersections, or complements of other events ("or,"
"and," "not").

1FF61931B1394360B95F2300873E3CB9.description: Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data.

D435C4AD3F304084A8448AE062BECF24.description: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability

F6E93A7202DE41258E0D20FB8463F0B4.description:
Apply geometric methods to solve design problems (e.g., designing an object or
structure to satisfy physical constraints or minimize cost; working with typographic grid systems
based on ratios).

77B959E72BDA4F5294AEDB462849917F.description:
Apply concepts of density based on area and volume in modeling situations (e.g.,
persons per square mile, BTUs per cubic foot).

8A7691FC92D0428CA21883D0F8E7D063.description:
Use geometric shapes, their measures, and their properties to describe objects (e.g.,
modeling a tree trunk or a human torso as a cylinder).

599BF62F9805459595F225EFACD0F954.description: Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations.

80B357A70F5E4766BE16E1A933BE2CFF.description:
Identify the shapes of two-dimensional cross-sections of three-dimensional objects,
and identify three-dimensional objects generated by rotations of two-dimensional objects.

035F93F9F83141378E827F2C7607777B.description:
Visualize relationships between two-dimensional and three-dimensional
objects.

89FC07A6C5574EB38C9C77D2DF874E0B.description: Use volume formulas for cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres to solve problems.

7CD90B44CF4946B79FA01BCE4EE04E41.description:
Give an informal argument for the formulas for the circumference of a circle, area of a
circle, volume of a cylinder, pyramid, and cone.

C1FBBC90BCB447B6A68FF1DC3233911D.description: Explain volume formulas and use them to solve problems.

0C83A448B13644DBBDBB52DD25517A30.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.

57E69364665743E7827BD8D9E2C6C531.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.

37E35A3B0F3A40EA9CEC318628A25F89.description:
Derive the equation of a circle of given center and radius using the Pythagorean
Theorem.

87BEED61005740B68591EF32F8475DD6.description: Translate between the geometric description and the equation for a conic section.

6A05DC8B9D5F4937996C75FEAEB517B5.description:
Derive using similarity the fact that the length of the arc intercepted by an angle is
proportional to the radius, and define the radian measure of the angle as the constant of proportionality; derive the formula for the area of a sector.

AC549576712F49E690E923DE099F4875.description: Find arc lengths and areas of sectors of circles.

DA8E8AD3B8BA446CA43B9385BFF739A4.description:
Construct the inscribed and circumscribed circles of a triangle and flexibly, efficiently, and
accurately prove properties of angles for a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle.

67648F9F9769474482FC2A0F003F6F04.description:
Identify and describe relationships among inscribed angles, radii, and chords, including
how angles formed inside the circle, the circle's radius, and line segments within the circle are
related. Understand special cases including angles formed by diameters and how the circle's edge
interacts with its radius.

1C7EEF79825C49B68B1A336C0AF997CA.description: Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately prove that all circles are similar.

27D2BAAB82FD44A5A1A9C5E7D47BF928.description: Understand and apply theorems about circles.

4F021970494A48619AEE2185C35B19A1.description: Use trigonometric ratios and the Pythagorean Theorem to solve right triangles in applied problems.

1DD34FC457E84A5C89538467E06E826E.description: Explain and use the relationship between the sine and cosine of complementary angles.

C8068794874E4D878142BA2381F273E8.description:
Understand that by similarity, side ratios in right triangles are properties of the angles in the
triangle, leading to definitions of trigonometric ratios for acute angles.

FE61D86347824E729CD54FBE23BBA370.description: Define trigonometric ratios and solve problems involving right triangles.

7E91E9072C45407DA8A8915EF6DF1338.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately use congruence and similarity criteria for triangles to solve
problems and to prove relationships in geometric figures.

B460D8AA8F9B4CF0BB09D45BEB4F3D16.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately prove theorems about triangles: proportionality, triangle
similarity, and the Pythagorean Theorem.

D1FF16056F8C41819F00670C08935350.description:
Use the properties of similarity transformations to establish the AA criterion for two
triangles to be similar.

C4A4DAB1DC35483CB3F1944D1136A944.description:
Given two figures, use the definition of similarity in terms of similarity transformations to decide if they are similar; explain using similarity transformations the meaning of similarity for
triangles as the equality of all corresponding pairs of angles and the proportionality of all
corresponding pairs of sides.

BEABABB8178549489A26EFE27A16E767.description:
Verify experimentally the properties of dilations given by a center and a scale factor
by seeing what happens to lines affected by a center of dilation and how scale factor affects line
segments.

D6014B4C0A0549059AA9A62D855D97EC.description: Understand similarity in terms of similarity transformations.

551F7AF263014145A4801CE5E0547B1C.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately prove theorems about parallelograms: congruence of
opposite sides and opposite angles, properties of diagonals.

6B8D475308F34627B9FD34BC11A018E7.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately prove theorems about triangles: interior angles, base angles,
segments joining midpoint of two sides, and medians of a triangle.

BE8D6AB4EB4D48A5920894415EDACF45.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately prove theorems about lines and angles: vertical, transversals,
alternate interior and exterior, perpendicular bisectors, etc.

5DDDA013AB204B0A998272475D3043C9.description:
Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, surface area, and
volume.

4017449C8C214CF4A018A0C6D789D942.description:
Observe using graphs and tables that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually
exceeds a quantity increasing linearly, quadratically.

7C76E7D08D8244399A00F80069330473.description:
Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve
problems.

BEF11BE70657495BB77F7D0EC22DAF5A.description:
Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, k f(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for
specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Using a
variety of strategies, experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph
using technology.

1BC55BE2B4DE4942A8439FF1D741C3DC.description: Build new functions from existing functions.

19FFC7CFC336412F8586771136607CA3.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately write a function that describes a relationship between two
quantities, including linear and exponential arithmetic and geometric sequences in context.

34E06566D2D94F35838E7D38D96C4D45.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.

150D2BCB5EC14B0B9B234A982B1940A5.description:
Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically,
numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions). Functions could be linear, exponential, or
quadratic.

0687E9835D5C49599EABAA45783DC6F5.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately write a function defined by an expression in different but
equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties of the function including zeros and
symmetry, using factoring for quadratic functions and integer constants for time with exponential
growth and decay.

EFE52F80C48048DDA4B5A01B90B98556.description:
Graph linear, exponential, and quadratic functions expressed symbolically and show key features of
the graph, including intercepts, maximum, minimum, and interpreting end behavior for exponential
functions by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.

EA8565139C524CAEB18788D57C827E2B.description:
Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (represented symbolically or as a
table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.

FBC5D779A3004588B53D14823FEFF46A.description:
Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship
it describes in linear, exponential, or quadratic contexts.

E71DC488585C419881DAB55EC093D6C0.description:
For a function that models a relationship between two quantities in context, interpret key features
of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a
verbal description of the relationship. Key features include intercepts; intervals where the function
is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries for
functions including linear, exponential, and quadratic.

CB53E546C6E742B5B31D3F30DE306CDF.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context.

F4254CFAA00F431686AFDF25209A8D28.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately solve a simple system consisting of a linear equation
and a quadratic equation in two variables algebraically and graphically.

A2E7355E0B834C3B9CEDD8A318F4F166.description:
Solve quadratic equations in one variable by inspection, taking square roots, and
factoring as appropriate to the initial form of the equation.

5C9B9ABD5C164EE9BA2CEA9D9EB00F98.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.

92410A9DC73A4208BB7B5DFA89FBE4E3.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the
same reasoning as in solving equations within linear, quadratic, and exponential equations.

9E144D0AC8124E7F8F22FC26F9884556.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately create linear, quadratic, exponential equations to represent
relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.

8293DEF6AF824CB58768F7BEC9B7E5B3.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them
to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear, quadratic, and exponential functions.

0BB0526173B14EE592CBA3B8F91AB114.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.

6BC6783B3B464FC88783EA18ED45484A.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately demonstrate that polynomials form a system similar
to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and
multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials.

FD51A34161C14A69BEA1B6AB21C87857.description: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions

021201CF9F3646C38715C5B1F98BBD0F.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately create an equivalent form of an expression to reveal and explain
properties of the quantity represented by the expression including factoring quadratic expressions
and using properties of exponents to create equivalent forms of exponential expressions to reveal
properties of interest in the function.

B6BAB94E725642A4B7DB792B0D65551F.description: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems.

38A05698295E47EDBBD7EC2DE6D47F64.description:
Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it within exponential and quadratic
functions.

14E8E874E97F46A3B12DB0B2C70F6E5E.description:
Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context within linear, exponential, and
quadratic functions.

A146C211CDAE4E5CBD1B6FF181D96880.description: Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on measurement when reporting quantities.

CAE0FBDDCD4040E089686DA5F96B1F0F.description: Use complex numbers in polynomial identities and equations.

81E0C2CAB5054A8D8551D8373E01D7C3.description:
Use the relation i2 = -1 and the commutative, associative, and distributive properties to
add, subtract, and multiply complex numbers.

457C2FD30C434C18B1BADEC786A35725.description:
Know there is a complex number i such that i2 = -1, and every complex number has the
form a + bi with a and b real.

0F31A1A4CE544E9982D151F406FB1F9D.description: Perform arithmetic operations with complex numbers.

E50F9284BAA349D5B42114CBDB5DD0D8.description:
Explain why the sum or product of two rational numbers is rational; that the sum of a
rational number and an irrational number is irrational; and that the product of a nonzero rational
number and an irrational number is irrational.

EA6E2EFB8248429491D82649B373289F.description: Use properties of rational and irrational numbers.

71B1639790CB4C629EFC806EC42795EA.description:
Rewrite expressions involving radicals and rational exponents using the properties of exponents.
Use properties of rational and irrational numbers.

6E58C28AC79A460990AFA09D6DB84174.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately explain how the definition of the meaning of rational exponents
follows from extending the properties of integer exponents to those values using a variety of
strategies, allowing for a notation for radicals in terms of rational exponents.

E42125FE184A4CCEBE9BFBE6D868B471.description: Extend the properties of exponents to rational exponents.

0D2D64D54D9145BE90A39E28FAFB578B.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

6E486589E1354FA2BD8331D0B89E8253.description: Look for and make use of structure.

643E38EB30BD4AB7AC860A9BF3DF75D4.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

C631CB3B39454D1681CBFF7D0885A20E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Public Draft WA Learning Standards Math

D8B1698B185248D0887913FA4A68E7BF.description:
Acknowledge the presence of missing data values and understand how missing values
may add bias to analysis and interpretation. Examine and discuss competing explanations for data
trends observed such as confounding variables. Respond to competing arguments or
interpretations of the data of different community groups, paying careful attention to what
conclusions the data supports, taking into account correlation versus causation.

47D042CC5419479CA8F2B0BC9EBF2322.description:
Create and analyze data sets and data displays, including but not limited to scatter plots,
regressions, histograms and boxplots using technology to sort or filter data, summarize, and
describe relationships between quantitative variables.

B073B9232CAE4582A7A825EF2DD9DAAD.description:
Understand the issues of bias and confounding variables when collecting data and their
impact on interpretation. Understand practices for collecting and handling data, including sensitive
information and concerns for privacy and how that may affect data collection.

A1AF363777054864A82B05A4855A1B70.description:
Formulate multivariable statistical investigative questions and determine how data can be
collected and provide an answer, consider causality and prediction when posing the question.

6B74B62B11954B48A01CEEB29D2464F3.description:
Apply the Addition Rule, 𝑃𝑃(𝐴𝐴 𝑜𝑜𝑜𝑜 𝐵𝐵) = 𝑃𝑃(𝐴𝐴) + 𝑃𝑃(𝐵𝐵) − 𝑃𝑃(𝐴𝐴 𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎 𝐵𝐵), and interpret the
answer in terms of the model.

7620083D631249B2BC6DB2BD47E3A4D9.description:
Find the conditional probability of A given B as the fraction of B's outcomes that also
belong to A, and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

20AAA7FAF8924E8193D6CC2D6D936FD5.description: Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events.

CA57D54699D142A693B166EBB0D20957.description:
Recognize and explain the concepts of conditional probability and independence in
everyday language and everyday situations.

32BDA0D6B7514B27ADE81A67D260040B.description:
Construct and interpret two-way frequency tables of data when two categories are
associated with each object being classified. Use the two-way table as a sample space to decide if
events are independent and to approximate conditional probabilities.

2418C59C1F564B269469F11EA7489650.description:
Understand the conditional probability of 𝐴𝐴 given 𝐵𝐵 as
𝑃𝑃(𝐴𝐴 𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎 𝐵𝐵),
𝑃𝑃(𝐵𝐵) and interpret  independence of 𝐴𝐴 and 𝐵𝐵 as saying that the conditional probability of 𝐴𝐴 given 𝐵𝐵 is the same as the
probability of 𝐴𝐴, and the conditional probability of 𝐵𝐵 given 𝐴𝐴 is the same as the probability of 𝐵𝐵.

CE339EDEB0554F8FA3E8564764B9BB62.description:
Understand that two events A and B are independent if the probability of A and B
occurring together is the product of their probabilities, and use this characterization to determine if
they are independent.

0F327BF5221B45CBAD0C1EFDCDA7E789.description:
Describe events as subsets of a sample space (the set of outcomes) using characteristics
(or categories) of the outcomes, or as unions, intersections, or complements of other events ("or,"
"and," "not").

EA2B40B7F96848C3BF6F156EF06A4860.description: Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data.

9981D6755203426ABED9BFFB10193638.description: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability

72C9680075484312BAD0038F30591A0D.description:
Use data from a randomized experiment to compare two treatments; use simulations to
decide if differences between parameters are significant.

E31DC122DF8E428597813E844CC0C08A.description:
Use data from a sample survey to estimate a population mean or proportion; develop a
margin of error through the use of simulation models for random sampling.

12B59EACD2FF445A9B438B70402636C1.description:
Recognize the purposes of and differences among sample surveys, experiments, and
observational studies; explain how randomization relates to each.

D5ADA4E351974EADA728AD3438FA1AE8.description:
Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiments, and
observational studies.

061774D28F9C43AEA224221C39949D03.description:
Decide if a specified model is consistent with results from a given data-generating
process, e.g., using simulation.

B4D34541A1BD4970A159588F7F04CBDC.description:
Understand statistics as a process for making inferences about population parameters
based on a random sample from that population.

E957A1B99EB24104B82E849C7129B259.description: Understand and evaluate random processes underlying statistical experiments.

6360F95C1E284A1AB0B0341A5EB79F83.description: Compute (using technology) and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit.

A35555963BEA4A6EBE14385C94F8B522.description:
Interpret the slope (rate of change) and the intercept (constant term) of a linear model in
the context of the data.

BF06383BBC6D49D5B52938E2E3CCBD38.description:
Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the
variables are related to solve problems in context by fitting functions to the data and explaining
trends and relationships within the data.

D2A1DF203BCB45B5A373DAFF5E8ADD6A.description:
Summarize categorical data for two categories in two-way frequency tables. Interpret
relative frequencies in the context of the data (including joint, marginal, and conditional relative
frequencies). Recognize possible associations and trends in the data.

6A559C6AF630494FB7A2BC73132FBAE7.description:
Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative
variables.

758716FDD09E42F2A9EA60548360B16A.description:
Use the mean and standard deviation of a data set to fit it to a normal distribution and to
estimate population percentages. Recognize that there are data sets for which such a procedure is
not appropriate. Use calculators, spreadsheets, and tables to estimate areas under the normal
curve.

FC3CA57DD1D0471BAF602152B5D37585.description:
Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets,
accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers).

34EF5BF7D0C94D778BF5C166926B21E4.description:
Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (median,
mean) and spread (interquartile range, standard deviation) of two or more different data sets.

FE09CB57EBAA462982EEF59AA3807E33.description: Represent data with plots on the real number line (dot plots, histograms, and box plots).

83FEC70111024A1194BC588BC23C4108.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable.

9C5AB56C501C4A84A6BADD43D9E22BF8.description:
Apply geometric methods to solve design problems (e.g., designing an object or
structure to satisfy physical constraints or minimize cost; working with typographic grid systems
based on ratios).

6572C1312AE94DE7974282CAC6C0E3F7.description:
Apply concepts of density based on area and volume in modeling situations (e.g.,
persons per square mile, BTUs per cubic foot).

BBBCF631DAF048A19B08E742F847985E.description:
Use geometric shapes, their measures, and their properties to describe objects (e.g.,
modeling a tree trunk or a human torso as a cylinder).

36021EDCAB6F48C8A6ABB82806CA086D.description: Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations.

8D1AE1B9A70847B6A28236822C2C114C.description:
Identify the shapes of two-dimensional cross-sections of three-dimensional objects,
and identify three-dimensional objects generated by rotations of two-dimensional objects.

4EFE15326AA141C8839FDBF861A1A2D6.description:
Visualize relationships between two-dimensional and three-dimensional
objects.

17D3D247632B4C42AA2D1232A892D48E.description: Use volume formulas for cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres to solve problems.

43E2D470B1804708BC65B13DCB0F41A2.description:
Give an informal argument for the formulas for the circumference of a circle, area of a
circle, volume of a cylinder, pyramid, and cone.

B6E12E68C33A43EC85F9C2A52FC08B6C.description: Explain volume formulas and use them to solve problems.

FBFCEABE2A1E4B4BA18E7780C9455DE9.description:
Use coordinates to compute perimeters of polygons and areas of triangles and
rectangles, e.g., using the distance formula.

89C20958D0D6468C87FB4384087EA905.description:
Find the point on a directed line segment between two given points that partitions the
segment in a given ratio.

222B6FE5991D47E994CF88081F33A934.description:
Prove the slope criteria for parallel and perpendicular lines and use them to solve
geometric problems (e.g., find the equation of a line parallel or perpendicular to a given line that
passes through a given point).

FC111B8A6D2D458081B2125F7F713217.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.

587F84CF585D4D4EB1BB302E20FE6CAA.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.

2AB05CEF006E4102BC3620E983D2E28E.description:
Derive the equation of a circle of given center and radius using the Pythagorean
Theorem; complete the square to find the center and radius of a circle given by an equation.

A0F89B5C233E477C911C3EB9FFB242A3.description: Translate between the geometric description and the equation for a conic section.

31BFAA62E68F4062AD1D65009928020A.description:
Derive using similarity the fact that the length of the arc intercepted by an angle is
proportional to the radius, and define the radian measure of the angle as the constant of
proportionality; derive the formula for the area of a sector.

5517FB9A9DFB4BF2AC97A88744854664.description: Find arc lengths and areas of sectors of circles.

9BF243402D254063813122CAF3719A40.description:
Construct the inscribed and circumscribed circles of a triangle and flexibly, efficiently, and
accurately prove properties of angles for a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle.

87808FCA9B514730AD78B74A36E58385.description:
Identify and describe relationships among inscribed angles, radii, and chords, including
how angles formed inside the circle, the circle's radius, and line segments within the circle are related. Understand special cases including angles formed by diameters and how the circle's edge
interacts with its radius.

1E44DF24CAF744819496A55854AAE9B4.description: Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately prove that all circles are similar.

33B1FF4B6AC647C4A8A206E8F1770B24.description: Understand and apply theorems about circles.

0485EDCF90BA46A3A746F228FDA15168.description:
Use trigonometric ratios and the Pythagorean Theorem to solve right triangles in
applied problems.

1198331F7B9D474D82B5AB4EB86EC399.description: Explain and use the relationship between the sine and cosine of complementary angles.

F6FB0DF542C942AE8DD181F5836CE364.description:
Understand that by similarity, side ratios in right triangles are properties of the angles in
the triangle, leading to definitions of trigonometric ratios for acute angles.

8006B130D03745A2AEE39C6F036C5D00.description: Define trigonometric ratios and solve problems involving right triangles.

439348A2C7E142D0B34C6489E9778B64.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately use congruence and similarity criteria for triangles to
solve problems and to prove relationships in geometric figures.

F822E2B362D74EDB8E277E241562A7DD.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately prove theorems about triangles: proportionality,
triangle similarity, and the Pythagorean Theorem.

F63BCB37309C4B69B50039547737A4B2.description:
Use the properties of similarity transformations to establish the AA criterion for two
triangles to be similar.

D030C1C9137D4731B40D3EE739544D6B.description:
Given two figures, use the definition of similarity in terms of similarity transformations to
decide if they are similar; explain using similarity transformations the meaning of similarity for
triangles as the equality of all corresponding pairs of angles and the proportionality of all
corresponding pairs of sides.

75172B2E65CF4ABBA502BB99A0D22AA6.description:
Verify experimentally the properties of dilations given by a center and a scale factor
by seeing what happens to lines affected by a center of dilation and how scale factor affects line
segments.

6F7C6B3D67CF4768AE95B6115B70B277.description: Understand similarity in terms of similarity transformations.

EE3EA29DF57743BBA163148EDF1E9F88.description: Construct an equilateral triangle, a square, and a regular hexagon inscribed in a circle.

DE188863942043C89D022C152EE137AD.description: Make formal geometric constructions with a variety of tools and methods.

C08C612E689C45488D6AAD5E05575347.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately prove theorems about parallelograms: congruence of
opposite sides and opposite angles, properties of diagonals.

7B77E4B450FC44C3875A88089D7C62B4.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately prove theorems about triangles: interior angles, base
angles, segments joining midpoint of two sides, and medians of a triangle.

E868C58D36974CC59A48AD5AE1C3BBC9.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately prove theorems about lines and angles: vertical,
transversals, alternate interior and exterior, perpendicular bisectors, etc.

C53E6FDD43A348A2BA8B03EF8AC7DF72.description:
Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, surface area, and
volume.

5409CBF0B4C74DEC93918D4F9992E310.description:
Explain how the criteria for triangle congruence (ASA, SAS, and SSS) follow from the
definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions.

53FE1357EA2F4F7ABAC7BBFEBB141C8D.description:
Use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to show that two triangles are
congruent if and only if corresponding pairs of sides and corresponding pairs of angles are
congruent.

E83ED6D012CE41C9813D5BFC4499FB6B.description:
Use geometric descriptions of rigid motions to transform figures and to predict the effect
of a given rigid motion on a given figure; given two figures, use the definition of congruence in
terms of rigid motions to decide if they are congruent.

92F33DF032EC4016883D6132DE6D8E6E.description: Understand congruence in terms of rigid motions.

96BB2F9926B148BBACE07BA65C9D243D.description:
Given a geometric figure and a rotation, reflection, or translation, draw the transformed
figure using, e.g., graph paper, tracing paper, or geometry software. Specify a sequence of
transformations that will carry a given figure onto another.

73618B9E67014541BC3C13F87E2AB22E.description:
Develop definitions of rotations, reflections, and translations in terms of angles, circles,
perpendicular lines, parallel lines, and line segments.

76FE7C14C13E410388350918564E2698.description:
Given a rectangle, parallelogram, trapezoid, or regular polygon, describe the rotations
and reflections that carry it onto itself.

CA0ADE51EE404032983BF0E9AC21135D.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately represent transformations in the plane, e.g.,
transparencies and geometry software; describe transformations as functions that take points in the
plane as inputs and give other points as outputs. Compare transformations that preserve distance
and angle to those that do not (e.g., translation versus horizontal stretch).

2727B62384FC43E98D834337CD5B40F6.description:
Know precise definitions of angle, circle, perpendicular line, parallel line, and line
segment, based on the undefined notions of point, line, distance along a line, and distance around
a circular arc.

E6A9528F73084BC5A45DCADB1DD2C10C.description: Experiment with transformations in the plane.

317761C04BF54CF29E872BF28CB1B04D.description:
Prove the Pythagorean identity sin2(θ) + cos2(θ) = 1 and use it to find sin(θ), cos(θ), or
tan(θ) given sin(θ), cos(θ), or tan(θ) and the quadrant of the angle.

4A8502DAFC5644E494483F1771109F9D.description:
Choose trigonometric functions to model periodic phenomena with specified amplitude,
frequency, and midline.

D5C59BCC3EFA4E97A7B11D54BD479AEC.description: Interpret expressions for functions in terms of the situation they model.

2D560C08426142A89F4A12483212D6CF.description:
Explain how the unit circle in the coordinate plane enables the extension of trigonometric
functions to all real numbers, interpreted as radian measures of angles traversed counterclockwise
around the unit circle.

CAE0537F62614FCD8235A0FB887071F3.description: Extend the domain of trigonometric functions using the unit circle.

88730D0D0B744198BE5041779B51D134.description: Interpret the parameters in a linear or exponential function in terms of a context.

5083DBA4FD1046F186601C46F609709A.description: Interpret expressions for functions in terms of the situation they model.

E3349E91A7CA40DF99441A7B50C98EC8.description:
For exponential models, express as a logarithm the solution to abct = d where a, c, and d
are numbers and the base b is 2, 10, or e; evaluate the logarithm using technology.

01055165662A42B8A2FF61585B2B909E.description:
Observe using graphs and tables that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually
exceeds a quantity increasing linearly, quadratically, or as a polynomial function.

B1F8D352D83B42DFB991D231513C6349.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately construct linear and exponential functions given a
graph, a description of a relationship, or two input-output pairs (include reading these from a
table).

7787D2D0FD014223BA9F361E39CAA07A.description:
Distinguish between situations that can be modeled with linear functions (equal
differences over equal intervals) and with exponential functions (equal factors over equal intervals),
recognizing constant rates per unit interval, and growth or decay by a constant percent rate per
unit interval.

3F7977893F2A4C0E8675C9F5C6D58ABF.description:
Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve
problems.

E43C1804B60B4CFCB4032451839465E4.description: Find inverse functions through focus on relationships between inputs and outputs.

AB81382ED5FD438AA63CFBCA772C164D.description:
Identify the effect on the graph of replacing 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) 𝑏𝑏𝑏𝑏 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) + 𝑘𝑘, 𝑘𝑘 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥), 𝑓𝑓(𝑘𝑘𝑘𝑘), 𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥 + 𝑘𝑘) for specific values of 𝑘𝑘 (both positive and negative); find the value of 𝑘𝑘 given the graphs.
Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph using technology.

0FA47DA05811441EB807B693AFFED629.description: Build new functions from existing functions.

EB4537B2AFF34CCD8745745D564856D6.description:
Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively and with an explicit formula,
use them to model situations, and translate between the two forms.

632AC4B7ED3E45668D909A874EC96ABE.description:
Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities including
determining an explicit expression, recursive process, or steps for calculation from a context, and
combining standard function types using arithmetic operations.

C768841580E4496295B774E66D805179.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.

0DBED561869D445D909B93D991C36BC4.description:
Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically,
graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions). Functions can include: polynomial,
radical, rational, logarithms, absolute value, piecewise, and trigonometric. Linear, exponential, and
quadratic relationships in increased complexity.

FF1229F6B36D484182975C1E0893F2E0.description:
Write a function defined by an expression in different but equivalent forms to reveal and
explain different properties of the function, including factoring and completing the square to reveal
zeros, symmetry, and extreme values of a quadratic functions and non-integer constants for time
with exponential growth and decay in context.

6EEDAEE426B34070A4DAC05A0CE66CF1.description:
Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by
hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases including linear, quadratic,
exponential, square root, cube root, and piecewise-defined functions, including step functions and
absolute value functions, polynomial functions, identifying zeros when suitable factorizations are
available, and showing end behavior, and exponential and logarithmic functions, showing
intercepts and end behavior, and trigonometric functions, showing period, midline, and amplitude.

1501A435922D46F699341D6650BEEB9E.description:
Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or
as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.

E0EB6557BC56481697B5581738840598.description:
Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative
relationship it describes in context. Functions can include: polynomial, radical, rational, logarithms,
absolute value, piecewise, and trigonometric. Linear, exponential, and quadratic relationships in
increased complexity.

FCDC3AD5C74A46AE94713542FD5E679E.description:
For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal
description of the relationship. Key features include intercepts; intervals where the function is
increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries.
Functions can include: polynomial, radical, rational, logarithms, absolute value, piecewise, and
trigonometric. Linear, exponential, and quadratic relationships in increased complexity.

7E23252A913C4EA4BF465146F489C5A8.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context.

D6F31FE9A3EB4373BB8E9159A3BED874.description:
Recognize that sequences are functions, sometimes defined recursively, whose domain is a
subset of the integers.

A102D6ED4D5A44FF89152E05EBB90D27.description:
Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret
statements that use function notation in terms of a context.

ECB0E3143E984D82863F0900BF34DD03.description:
Understand that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the
range) assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range. If 𝑓𝑓 is a function
and x is an element of its domain, then 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) denotes the output of f corresponding to the input 𝑥𝑥.
The graph of f is the graph of the equation 𝑦𝑦 = 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥).

EA7669DEA8CD479BB2C1537C5691E5C9.description: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation.

FE269B4FF1094B1C9F5072CC342CF6FD.description:
Graph the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half-plane (excluding the
boundary in the case of a strict inequality), and graph the solution set to a system of linear
inequalities in two variables as the intersection of the corresponding half-planes.

924D1875D56941BFAACE4EE9681E8E98.description:
Using a variety of strategies explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the
graphs of the equations 𝑦𝑦 = 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) and 𝑦𝑦 = 𝑔𝑔(𝑥𝑥) intersect are the solutions of the equation
𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) = 𝑔𝑔(𝑥𝑥) find the solutions approximately, e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make
tables of values, or find successive approximations. Include cases where 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) and/or 𝑔𝑔(𝑥𝑥) are linear,
polynomial, rational, absolute value, exponential, and logarithmic functions.

05559FCF789243F5B5FD81D3D5957DD7.description:
Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions
plotted in the coordinate plane, often forming a curve (which could be a line).

1C8408424D424D91836581651C634EB1.description: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically.

2E188C5AC5F9457084A52FD2BE205B1E.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately solve a simple system consisting of a linear equation
and a quadratic equation in two variables algebraically and graphically.

A8E74563EF3046C3AF9E95B0D7ED1544.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately solve systems of linear equations exactly and
approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.

BF77965E3E0E4FEB9D84EEB6653BDCB5.description:
Demonstrate using a variety of strategies that, given a system of two equations in two
variables, replacing one equation by the sum of that equation and a multiple of the other produces
a system with the same solutions.

017582A88D01466E8840A51936C35095.description:
Solve quadratic equations in one variable by inspection, factoring, completing the
square and derive the quadratic formula from this form. Recognize when the quadratic formula
give complex solutions and write them as a ± bi for real numbers a and b.

759DF1DC6152407593DAD99587B03FF1.description:
Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with
coefficients represented by letters.

AE11E51DB2CA4FFFB794FD411B2612B1.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.

00F6DA857D08414490613954D333E5E5.description:
Solve rational and radical equations in one variable, and give examples showing how
extraneous solutions may arise.

B55E5A9DC91343A28AB38D90A45F7E70.description:
Explain each step in solving a simple equation as following from the equality of numbers
asserted at the previous step, starting from the assumption that the original equation has a
solution. Construct a viable argument to justify a solution method.

BBD6A59333AC45A68003604237FFA4A2.description: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning.

F6D5EE4B7C8A4EC09895FA2E4884C3B2.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest,
using the same reasoning as in solving equations.

C45B9334F0904BF0A8D00FBE7A1F4F33.description:
Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or
inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or nonviable options in a modeling context.

3163B6C669494B0289B2A904FBF53897.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately create equations in two or more variables to
represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and
scales.

E600A22FB1B9497E9FA6217213A6E7E3.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately create equations and inequalities in one variable and
use them to solve problems.

49E25688ACA145FEA26EC5FB1AF00103.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.

ED0E41C71F2E464EBCC4D9B017EF94DE.description:
Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms; write a(x)/b(x) in the form q(x) +
r(x)/b(x), where a(x), b(x), q(x), and r(x) are polynomials with the degree of r(x) less than the degree
of b(x), using inspection, long division, or, for the more complicated examples, a computer algebra
system.

8FDB01E5C777406F9B541C1AB5A7BA70.description: Prove polynomial identities and use them to describe numerical relationships.

7E966A1388C846D9BAE75675F6BA3F50.description: Identify zeros of polynomials when suitable factorizations are available, and use the zeros to construct a rough graph of the function defined by the polynomial.

33966648D2854C708CBF97C844F3AAFB.description:
Know and apply the Remainder Theorem: For a polynomial p(x) and a number a, the
remainder on division by x - a is p(a), so p(a) = 0 if and only if (x - a) is a factor of p(x).

F242E40C8F964E7B8CD07FFF490772AD.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately demonstrate that polynomials form a system similar
to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and
multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials.

9E31E02683234C7AB05A2A65137BA5C6.description: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions

54032977FC9B4B81B4811365BCE9C915.description:
Derive the formula for the sum of a finite geometric series (when the common ratio is
not 1), and use the formula to solve problems.

CD0287B367724FA5B1ADC3F9C092552F.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately create an equivalent form of an expression to reveal
and explain properties of the quantity represented by the expression including factoring quadratic
expressions, completing the square in a quadratic expression to reveal maximums or minimums,
and using properties of exponents to create equivalent forms of exponential expressions to reveal
properties of interest in the function.

BFC96B5753444729992DCC7B326E12B1.description: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems.

A9C740A34B314C34B94FF4923236E4AF.description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it.

079A5B2305B14DEA83C98F2347DD17D8.description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

1D9A595F71C8499FAE186D63CA4F33FF.description: Solve quadratic equations with real coefficients that have complex solutions.

79277E23448646B0851974F432B0561A.description: Use complex numbers in polynomial identities and equations.

6BFF910B3E954488899F8F49D12063A8.description:
Use the relation i2 = -1 and the commutative, associative, and distributive properties to
add, subtract, and multiply complex numbers.

ED675AC599C845AC8D942E4DB30E8BC3.description:
Know there is a complex number i such that i2 = -1, and every complex number has the
form a + bi with a and b real.

0D3020B069074E6EA11AD1CF684230B9.description: Perform arithmetic operations with complex numbers.

18C3751F59744B71AE98746208B2B322.description: Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on measurement when reporting quantities.

58A62FA8C75841C5A81647229208F4C5.description: Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive modeling.

EB1D35F53C4F499C850BC600A68EC945.description:
Use units as a way to understand problems and to guide the solution of multi-step
problems; choose and interpret units consistently in formulas; choose and interpret the scale and
the origin in graphs and data displays.

3F913FCACC9B482D9215A0ED5A3AFF82.description: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems.

AFD761AB2C924F0BA554D4562BA83BBD.description:
Explain why the sum or product of two rational numbers is rational; that the sum of a
rational number and an irrational number is irrational; and that the product of a nonzero rational
number and an irrational number is irrational.

466901016F1E4ECB8D3F32AE18338C2F.description: Use properties of rational and irrational numbers.

6F60C64AB1474E36AA0E59B50B45D1D5.description:
Rewrite expressions involving radicals and rational exponents using the properties of
exponents. Use properties of rational and irrational numbers.

6A8323D7A7A04D6A92D6715F2692521A.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately explain how the definition of the meaning of rational
exponents follows from extending the properties of integer exponents to those values using a
variety of strategies, allowing for a notation for radicals in terms of rational exponents.

9532751E41EF46ABBEEA4EB6E9884A3B.description: Extend the properties of exponents to rational exponents.

DB3114900550418E86C442D562D5CAA1.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

64259EFB31744A2B9A9582F725752A68.description: Look for and make use of structure.

BA8A2F573D51456CADD99F36082C641C.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

75A86323D9CD4885A54395D52E3AEDEB.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Public Draft WA Learning Standards Math

90AC6E23D2C14D9886702AA26BDD7E68.description:
Acknowledge the presence of missing data values and understand how missing values
may add bias to analysis and interpretation. Examine and discuss competing explanations for data
trends observed such as confounding variables. Respond to competing arguments or
interpretations of the data of different community groups, paying careful attention to what
conclusions the data supports, taking into account correlation versus causation.

9A12E5ABC86140EBBDD3D176FC5FEFC6.description:
Create and analyze data sets and data displays, including but not limited to scatter plots,
regressions, histograms and boxplots using technology to sort or filter data, summarize, and
describe relationships between quantitative variables.

CED0C44E216D41C3AD4F2B03A463B870.description:
Understand the issues of bias and confounding variables when collecting data and their
impact on interpretation. Understand practices for collecting and handling data, including sensitive
information and concerns for privacy and how that may affect data collection.

E3610DA95C954CA4BF00C223B784442E.description:
Formulate multivariable statistical investigative questions and determine how data can be
collected and provide an answer, consider causality and prediction when posing the question.

EB75F0121B3341A987BC47D60122931D.description:
Use data from a randomized experiment to compare two treatments; use simulations to
decide if differences between parameters are significant.

6B823967F3C14592809CA5F85BF02AC4.description:
Use data from a sample survey to estimate a population mean or proportion; develop a
margin of error through the use of simulation models for random sampling.

A1DB9B0601E44D54B76324390675A358.description:
Recognize the purposes of and differences among sample surveys, experiments, and
observational studies; explain how randomization relates to each.

EDCF5B375C9E4BD5A4F89A25BEFC9E5C.description:
Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiments, and
observational studies.

F4592549400B42619CBFB45F16D5875D.description:
Decide if a specified model is consistent with results from a given data-generating
process, e.g., using simulation.

5002E0D9F44043BAAF2EC51840DED7F4.description:
Understand statistics as a process for making inferences about population parameters
based on a random sample from that population.

62052975C4454406B98A4DE1409EC8A9.description: Understand and evaluate random processes underlying statistical experiments.

EDA3F65240134DB3A314A8443A25AE42.description:
Use the mean and standard deviation of a data set to fit it to a normal distribution and to
estimate population percentages. Recognize that there are data sets for which such a procedure is
not appropriate. Use calculators, spreadsheets, and tables to estimate areas under the normal
curve.

B43D1E3DF253491D9D731FB5AF968694.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable.

5D7F3BC6E02C46FF9FB8ACC5FD4F69CB.description:
Prove the Pythagorean identity sin2(θ) + cos2(θ) = 1 and use it to find sin(θ), cos(θ), or
tan(θ) given sin(θ), cos(θ), or tan(θ) and the quadrant of the angle.

8AA892A511274B5493A51D5A72DC11C1.description:
Choose trigonometric functions to model periodic phenomena with specified amplitude,
frequency, and midline.

1FBA8CBB1B6548839C83A2BEB49C512F.description: Interpret expressions for functions in terms of the situation they model.

9DAF15FABD6C4885BDC1E6DCBC509829.description:
Explain how the unit circle in the coordinate plane enables the extension of trigonometric
functions to all real numbers, interpreted as radian measures of angles traversed counterclockwise
around the unit circle.

FA8EF31992AB47FDB61B71CFE273EBA3.description: Extend the domain of trigonometric functions using the unit circle.

2FCB94698659483A974BC5F5256D9FE3.description:
For exponential models, express as a logarithm the solution to abct = d where a, c, and d
are numbers and the base b is 2, 10, or e; evaluate the logarithm using technology.

CF24C5C9DDEF49BAA2002F57D649C18A.description:
Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve
problems.

026ABDC4578040F88CC36243E32761C8.description: Find inverse functions through focus on relationships between inputs and outputs.

ABDA7FB48AAE496490FB51D685C58DF7.description:
Identify the effect on the graph of replacing 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) 𝑏𝑏𝑏𝑏 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) + 𝑘𝑘, 𝑘𝑘 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥), 𝑓𝑓(𝑘𝑘𝑘𝑘), 𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥 + 𝑘𝑘) for specific values of 𝑘𝑘 (both positive and negative); find the value of 𝑘𝑘 given the graphs.
Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph using technology.

63D37A71B1464C8FB09BCBA1E18BD2DE.description: Build new functions from existing functions.

56E524C2F41E4CD7B783063CB8937BC0.description:
Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively and with an explicit formula,
use them to model situations, and translate between the two forms.

D79CEF12AA60432DBDA88AC2D062DA63.description:
Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities including determining an
explicit expression, recursive process, or steps for calculation from a context, and combining
standard function types using arithmetic operations.

F396E16ECFFF4AE2A5A0BB2FCEAEF023.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.

B8232BC8956845D5932D11252C50224B.description:
Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically,
numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions). Functions can include: polynomial, radical, rational,
logarithms, absolute value, piecewise, and trigonometric. Linear, exponential, and quadratic
relationships in increased complexity.

71A9CBB589E547669025762EDF34EF2F.description:
Write a function defined by an expression in different but equivalent forms to reveal and explain
different properties of the function, including factoring and completing the square to reveal zeros,
symmetry, and extreme values of a quadratic functions and non-integer constants for time with
exponential growth and decay in context.

EA3A28765471495298ABE4B959DBFB44.description:
Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple
cases and using technology for more complicated cases including square root, cube root, and
piecewise-defined functions, including step functions and absolute value functions, polynomial
functions, identifying zeros when suitable factorizations are available, and showing end behavior,
and exponential and logarithmic functions, showing intercepts and end behavior, and
trigonometric functions, showing period, midline, and amplitude.

D051AA2DBACE4E8E854625C4D2567BC0.description:
Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or
as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.

FE7AC384045C4A3D97B05809430C70A8.description:
Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative
relationship it describes in context. Functions can include: polynomial, radical, rational, logarithms,
absolute value, piecewise, and trigonometric. Linear, exponential, and quadratic relationships in
increased complexity.

9E26235F433741C3A2E5BADE11C6187F.description:
For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal
description of the relationship. Key features include intercepts; intervals where the function is
increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries.
Functions can include: polynomial, radical, rational, logarithms, absolute value, piecewise, and
trigonometric. Linear, exponential, and quadratic relationships in increased complexity.

2025C3DECC0D49559C9B717D78C578AC.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context.

D7A494120C1B4FB3A7310E4DA98CDF97.description:
Using a variety of strategies explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the
graphs of the equations 𝑦𝑦 = 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) and 𝑦𝑦 = 𝑔𝑔(𝑥𝑥) intersect are the solutions of the equation
𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) = 𝑔𝑔(𝑥𝑥) find the solutions approximately, e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make
tables of values, or find successive approximations. Include cases where 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) and/or 𝑔𝑔(𝑥𝑥) are linear,
polynomial, rational, absolute value, exponential, and logarithmic functions.

C5438191C64E44D49DCAB45B2E9B7517.description: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically.

B67580E7CACB43859E29BD2BA276A405.description:
Solve quadratic equations in one variable by inspection, factoring, completing the
square and derive the quadratic formula from this form. Recognize when the quadratic formula
give complex solutions and write them as a ± bi for real numbers a and b.

4B27E217C182457F837366C574DFE414.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.

0A27C3BC001E469782DA1F3FF6DC3AFF.description:
Solve rational and radical equations in one variable, and give examples showing how
extraneous solutions may arise.

E470AB27309B4C479C25121176B1A630.description: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning.

4AB9696B56E74F4FA80374E57BFA88F7.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest,
using the same reasoning as in solving equations.

7F9134EC8C184B9696EB7BFA5E79B936.description:
Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or
inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or nonviable options in a modeling context.

E68DC611AEBD4672AFF029185802E8FB.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately create equations in two or more variables to
represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and
scales.

56221AA50F494C84BE59FCDBD3ACA846.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately create equations and inequalities in one variable and
use them to solve problems.

D1CB9C5174FB4D4984506F13B0486928.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.

72FED17767314B86832C7427CE4C45B7.description:
Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms; write a(x)/b(x) in the form q(x) +
r(x)/b(x), where a(x), b(x), q(x), and r(x) are polynomials with the degree of r(x) less than the degree
of b(x), using inspection, long division, or, for the more complicated examples, a computer algebra
system.

832760D72B3E4CE9847D71FBCC8C0140.description: Prove polynomial identities and use them to describe numerical relationships.

07860BFC007441EA934E5DE6102D6623.description: Identify zeros of polynomials when suitable factorizations are available, and use the zeros to construct a rough graph of the function defined by the polynomial.

29E14E1DCDA14A0988A4CEF18751269E.description:
Know and apply the Remainder Theorem: For a polynomial p(x) and a number a, the
remainder on division by x - a is p(a), so p(a) = 0 if and only if (x - a) is a factor of p(x).

906E45DC75934A488F7BA73ED1C9018E.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately demonstrate that polynomials form a system similar
to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and
multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials.

97E6490FB062444F8F4D886E5DD8C690.description: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions

16763DEEE5B14ED0BCE6E111C68E0EBB.description:
Derive the formula for the sum of a finite geometric series (when the common ratio is
not 1), and use the formula to solve problems.

4203504329EE433691110D71EBC67A96.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately create an equivalent form of an expression to reveal and explain
properties of the quantity represented by the expression including factoring quadratic expressions,
completing the square in a quadratic expression to reveal maximums or minimums, and using properties of exponents to create equivalent forms of exponential expressions to reveal properties
of interest in the function.

86D8DD3FCC184190A36AB2375C25A819.description: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems.

BEC545D33E0D4C9FA1C2C9A253254903.description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it.

4F3A69CDAE9C4E1E9A8AC1BB2F28986C.description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

E6FAD409888849B38CC7531195A1ABB5.description: Solve quadratic equations with real coefficients that have complex solutions.

BA52FF1B28804242AE1D9D307E6042AD.description: Use complex numbers in polynomial identities and equations.

5F7C0E3035AA4F50A669DEAAD2D6DE9A.description:
Use the relation i2 = -1 and the commutative, associative, and distributive properties to
add, subtract, and multiply complex numbers.

2C5A69882F444D9FAAF63AC967BEF70D.description:
Know there is a complex number i such that i2 = -1, and every complex number has the
form a + bi with a and b real.

A25121617F0B4952B2796146319CCFFD.description: Perform arithmetic operations with complex numbers.

8C6FAFE03F7D45E1AF25511ECF06F761.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

473C96F0BC394BD4B4A59B2AF756D7A7.description: Look for and make use of structure.

34D5CA1A488E495E9791FC1C4A05CFD3.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

67D4ED7DDD8041CABC571609FDB476A8.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

Identify the shapes of two-dimensional cross-sections of three-dimensional objects,
and identify three-dimensional objects generated by rotations of two-dimensional objects.

8C05222A8C5D4CFC89D387B000B39184.description:
Visualize relationships between two-dimensional and three-dimensional
objects.

Understand radian measure of an angle as the length of the arc on the unit circle
subtended by the angle.

FDC4354BD4FB4B3CB431505483DE22F1.description: Extend the domain of trigonometric functions using the unit circle.

EE4F50F1AECD46B2A819914648D30AB5.description:
For exponential models, express as a logarithm the solution to abct = d where a, c, and d
are numbers and the base b is 2, 10, or e; evaluate the logarithm using technology.

C4673A857276471B9818FD16E788596C.description:
Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve
problems.

D3F91C6D00B442D68A56587E0930CD6F.description: Find inverse functions through focus on relationships between inputs and outputs.

6590ECFFE0884846A7EE146CC5978744.description:
Identify the effect on the graph of replacing 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) 𝑏𝑏𝑏𝑏 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) + 𝑘𝑘, 𝑘𝑘 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥), 𝑓𝑓(𝑘𝑘𝑘𝑘), 𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥 + 𝑘𝑘) for specific values of 𝑘𝑘 (both positive and negative); find the value of 𝑘𝑘 given the graphs.
Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph using technology.

6CA77F6B2ADE4F349B359C45FC05AF08.description: Build new functions from existing functions.

3CB6D8EB106C4404B2FEB7CBFC9E650A.description:
Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively and with an explicit formula,
use them to model situations, and translate between the two forms.

F23F2FADA2364F92A6E04D9419DC2A76.description:
Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities including
determining an explicit expression, recursive process, or steps for calculation from a context, and
combining standard function types using arithmetic operations.

0C299EBDEC534A90910DBF31F9531BD8.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.

17CFADC152C14C7BB490D64CD2070DC7.description:
Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically,
graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions). Functions can include: polynomial,
radical, rational, logarithms, absolute value, piecewise, and trigonometric. Linear, exponential, and
quadratic relationships in increased complexity.

00179EA557FE4DC69BFAE0DE88270191.description:
Write a function defined by an expression in different but equivalent forms to reveal and
explain different properties of the function, including factoring and completing the square to reveal
zeros, symmetry, and extreme values of a quadratic functions and non-integer constants for time
with exponential growth and decay in context.

44FC1B33EE684A1592BA4A7428ED930C.description:
Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by
hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases including linear, quadratic,
exponential, square root, cube root, and piecewise-defined functions, including step functions and
absolute value functions, polynomial functions, identifying zeros when suitable factorizations are
available, and showing end behavior, and exponential and logarithmic functions, showing
intercepts and end behavior, and trigonometric functions, showing period, midline, and amplitude.

0C03EA0672E848D4A43900C85933776D.description:
Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or
as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.

93228782BE2C4C2BB6C1006EBDAA1999.description:
Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative
relationship it describes in context. Functions can include: polynomial, radical, rational, logarithms,
absolute value, piecewise, and trigonometric. Linear, exponential, and quadratic relationships in
increased complexity.

09D7926CBBB84171A30392B174F42063.description:
For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal
description of the relationship. Key features include intercepts; intervals where the function is
increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries.
Functions can include: polynomial, radical, rational, logarithms, absolute value, piecewise, and
trigonometric. Linear, exponential, and quadratic relationships in increased complexity.

0CFC055A77364560AB58DE8E57078C36.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context.

CD188A60BE1C4057B3F37F6FA98318F7.description:
Using a variety of strategies explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the
graphs of the equations 𝑦𝑦 = 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) and 𝑦𝑦 = 𝑔𝑔(𝑥𝑥) intersect are the solutions of the equation
𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) = 𝑔𝑔(𝑥𝑥) find the solutions approximately, e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make
tables of values, or find successive approximations. Include cases where 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) and/or 𝑔𝑔(𝑥𝑥) are linear,
polynomial, rational, absolute value, exponential, and logarithmic functions.

8702CFE7C19244BE9C284F6D4DD538D6.description: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically.

983EDD7A18B341A1AB37D027156D7E51.description:
Solve quadratic equations in one variable by inspection, factoring, completing the
square and derive the quadratic formula from this form. Recognize when the quadratic formula
give complex solutions and write them as a ± bi for real numbers a and b.

8E5732BFD47A425FB72619952B545DD0.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.

2149D8C2332746B8B3D6A7F10266AEF0.description:
Solve rational and radical equations in one variable, and give examples showing how
extraneous solutions may arise.

B6D6A065F1DC4DE9ABC9DD6EF12D3DB6.description: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning.

37896184635C489E92E06DD68D426AC8.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest,
using the same reasoning as in solving equations.

666821B16EB348638DBFDDF2387154B8.description:
Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or
inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or nonviable options in a modeling context.

AEEE49B67E154A9D88C0F2285DC3080C.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately create equations in two or more variables to
represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and
scales.

8509612FCB6C4ED3BF68787A4A4F7E70.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately create equations and inequalities in one variable and
use them to solve problems.

EA7E9F73F2B64F5F9DF78DD8CB44DC07.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.

EC668CDEA5F048BE80DFE84A4D0A993B.description:
Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms; write a(x)/b(x) in the form q(x) +
r(x)/b(x), where a(x), b(x), q(x), and r(x) are polynomials with the degree of r(x) less than the degree
of b(x), using inspection, long division, or, for the more complicated examples, a computer algebra
system.

9AE20A595EB74C7AA3D30C4AB7E61524.description: Prove polynomial identities and use them to describe numerical relationships.

5C4C0C9F7D534F27985492549D5486B5.description: Identify zeros of polynomials when suitable factorizations are available, and use the zeros to construct a rough graph of the function defined by the polynomial.

9CACCE5154EE45E9946D411C973960EE.description:
Know and apply the Remainder Theorem: For a polynomial p(x) and a number a, the
remainder on division by x - a is p(a), so p(a) = 0 if and only if (x - a) is a factor of p(x).

FFE85DF7C27A4B4ABA8790286403F126.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately demonstrate that polynomials form a system similar
to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and
multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials.

E44AE95F543C410C94C9315C72866DA9.description: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions

CD020DDC3D5B4CBFA28B746AFEDFDE27.description:
Derive the formula for the sum of a finite geometric series (when the common ratio is
not 1), and use the formula to solve problems.

62CFDD8FF1784F009032CE0EDACA6D3A.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately create an equivalent form of an expression to reveal and explain
properties of the quantity represented by the expression including factoring quadratic expressions,
completing the square in a quadratic expression to reveal maximums or minimums, and using
properties of exponents to create equivalent forms of exponential expressions to reveal properties
of interest in the function.

5DB4431CDF6D40F48CB413B0788B7DBF.description: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems.

A051A4B876344E8FB3CD9AB64BDF3865.description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it.

5AE5AF5D678C4E3A9A709DB98D639F68.description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

17F24DFD9F824D708883A8BB7B90793D.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

D3A749C4D33047B2B20F4AD654664BD4.description: Look for and make use of structure.

486F67685FB646C39930F455D3F87483.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

E64B79956FB94197BC786C9DC23399C5.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Public Draft WA Learning Standards Math

FA3539B69D8344338C165423723D6040.description: Interpret and communicate results through structured answers with teacher guidance.

02F7C401FCC04E94B1D0FD0C7B35F920.description: Analyze data sets by noticing and describing patterns in data-rich situations.

997B1AD8D68444F3B3FAC8A075F79AA0.description:
Collect or consider data through organizing objects or drawing pictures to represent and
communicate observations.

C6B4BCE573E64CCC9D3BB38A256789A6.description: Generate questions to investigate situations within the classroom.

0394F51F0DD34F399484EABB14886590.description: Use simple shapes to compose a variety of larger shapes.

1B0C12333E1843ABB1164A8D3F2ACF0D.description:
Model shapes in the world by building shapes from components (e.g., sticks
and clay balls) and drawing shapes.

833C03FA2C244E08B706CDFB23973A83.description:
Analyze and compare two- and three-dimensional shapes, in different sizes
and orientations, using informal language to describe their similarities, differences, parts (e.g.,
number of sides and vertices/“corners”) and other attributes (e.g., having sides of equal length).

3873FFBA3EB048E887970D7022AD32DE.description: Analyze, compare, create, and compose shapes.

DF0FC21A6363476EBAE46FF6C4E63381.description: Identify shapes as two-dimensional (lying in a plane, “flat”) or three-dimensional (“solid”).

C0669CEFC5224EF9A533B23BB04BD839.description: Correctly name shapes regardless of their orientations or overall size.

84FAACD79BFA4075934ADB978BA21C70.description:
Describe objects in the environment using names of shapes and describe the relative
positions of these objects using terms such as above, below, beside, in front of, behind, and next
to.

8562E16499A34EC6B4A97D70D107A014.description: Identify and describe shapes (squares, circles, triangles, rectangles, hexagons, cubes, cones, cylinders, and spheres).

CB86ECF605AF45DF823BACEE3C2EE598.description:
Classify objects into given categories; count the numbers of objects in each
category and sort the categories by count.

748BD54C6C514DD59936388CDF9C4F6B.description: Classify objects and count the number of objects in each category.

C8B1BEE786C04E568B076C43AA223590.description:
Directly compare two objects with a measurable attribute in common, to see which
object has “more of”/“less of” the attribute, and describe the difference.

11E489F92F6749AAB1E1E23A084D3B61.description:
Describe measurable attributes of objects, such as length or weight. Describe several
measurable attributes of a single object.

3C4865A84ACB42FAB45768C74E91313A.description:
Compose and decompose numbers from 11 to 19 into ten ones and some further ones, e.g., by
using objects or drawings, and record each composition or decomposition by a drawing or
equation (e.g., 18 = 10 + 8); understand that these numbers are composed of ten ones and one,
two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.

CC065FA4B7BD4F4EA4611043DA27FF39.description: Work with numbers 11–19 to gain foundations for place value.
