Apply the Addition Rule, 𝑃𝑃(𝐴𝐴 𝑜𝑜𝑜𝑜 𝐵𝐵) = 𝑃𝑃(𝐴𝐴) + 𝑃𝑃(𝐵𝐵) − 𝑃𝑃(𝐴𝐴 𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎 𝐵𝐵), and interpret the
answer in terms of the model.

1B33AF0EEC1E42F6B5CDBA507C08D738.description:
Find the conditional probability of A given B as the fraction of B's outcomes that also
belong to A, and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

C74660305B614FC6876D50C68F72FE3E.description: Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events.

4877F65D3C5E412787E3A9DC042A71E6.description:
Recognize and explain the concepts of conditional probability and independence in
everyday language and everyday situations.

016B280E64BC443E9E2BEEC130586603.description:
Construct and interpret two-way frequency tables of data when two categories are
associated with each object being classified. Use the two-way table as a sample space to decide if
events are independent and to approximate conditional probabilities.

F8228364E46344868ECE242303C7F41A.description:
Understand the conditional probability of 𝐴𝐴 given 𝐵𝐵 as
𝑃𝑃(𝐴𝐴 𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎 𝐵𝐵),
𝑃𝑃(𝐵𝐵) and interpret
independence of 𝐴𝐴 and 𝐵𝐵 as saying that the conditional probability of 𝐴𝐴 given 𝐵𝐵 is the same as the
probability of 𝐴𝐴, and the conditional probability of 𝐵𝐵 given 𝐴𝐴 is the same as the probability of 𝐵𝐵.

FE8C80D32F264D77AACA7A645865D2E0.description:
Understand that two events A and B are independent if the probability of A and B
occurring together is the product of their probabilities, and use this characterization to determine if
they are independent.

9645DF1D5B064E68B91CA1D68CE0A232.description:
Describe events as subsets of a sample space (the set of outcomes) using characteristics (or categories) of the outcomes, or as unions, intersections, or complements of other events ("or,"
"and," "not").

0F2D1239568F4993A1D5715CD062D9C9.description: Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data.

8F41B7D06FBB4F9CBD3FA814B279DCF1.description: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability

9A7C3DF905154EF4880D1B9D027787E1.description: Compute (using technology) and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit.

5AB8C4F406124C9892A71F4D64EC38A0.description:
Interpret the slope (rate of change) and the intercept (constant term) of a linear model in the
context of the data.

5B6AB289831240EF8B2067EF807776FC.description:
Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the
variables are related to solve problems in context by fitting functions to the data and explaining
trends and relationships within the data.

4E04915C0BF849C2A3E9E3BA7FEE54F4.description:
Summarize categorical data for two categories in two-way frequency tables. Interpret
relative frequencies in the context of the data (including joint, marginal, and conditional relative
frequencies). Recognize possible associations and trends in the data.

0440ED81D45745E59FDD891B02FC8279.description:
Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative
variables.

292D889EFB6C4BC1B556A405339BA979.description:
Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets,
accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers).

60C904C56A9A4277B7F291EA015B865F.description:
Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (median, mean)
and spread (interquartile range, standard deviation) of two or more different data sets.

A94C37B4768B4B8E81CD18D4BBD4C7C7.description: Represent data with plots on the real number line (dot plots, histograms, and box plots).

EED979C5BAAD464EA8441E81C28B6F35.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable.

676C756E5484458386DE5614DAADBAE3.description:
Apply geometric methods to solve design problems (e.g., designing an object or
structure to satisfy physical constraints or minimize cost; working with typographic grid systems
based on ratios).

EE08E12005024781B4237A8ECF75FDE9.description:
Apply concepts of density based on area and volume in modeling situations (e.g.,
persons per square mile, BTUs per cubic foot).

97F75212A0AC434B906611AB7A604803.description:
Use geometric shapes, their measures, and their properties to describe objects (e.g.,
modeling a tree trunk or a human torso as a cylinder).

02CF8665BD044F49BA8A2CF19FDA52F1.description: Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations.

5980A0B2AFF241B79E8C858DDBBD2FF9.description:
Identify the shapes of two-dimensional cross-sections of three-dimensional objects,
and identify three-dimensional objects generated by rotations of two-dimensional objects.

D753F5D147794F1B9B400494C62121A5.description:
Visualize relationships between two-dimensional and three-dimensional
objects.

12CE889247EB4AACA5417CB0291A4468.description: Use volume formulas for cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres to solve problems.

89D8E717AC8C49C89669A0E03A12BA78.description:
Give an informal argument for the formulas for the circumference of a circle, area of a
circle, volume of a cylinder, pyramid, and cone.

FBA5B0C828BC4868AC0F0F3718142D0D.description: Explain volume formulas and use them to solve problems.

7E98FE44227A4CF8978DBE89EA4F5C02.description:
Use coordinates to compute perimeters of polygons and areas of triangles and
rectangles, e.g., using the distance formula.

F3616302C4C14D889FE675C53E3223F1.description:
Find the point on a directed line segment between two given points that partitions the
segment in a given ratio.

3166BC0368F94EAFA58620F72FE803DD.description:
Prove the slope criteria for parallel and perpendicular lines and use them to solve
geometric problems (e.g., find the equation of a line parallel or perpendicular to a given line that
passes through a given point).

E47C48F4D5D94B7C96469BF67E382A8D.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.

1F2255649A9C48E8A0B7A58563323081.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.

8D815AE2ECF747A3A30FDF2ACB992770.description:
Derive the equation of a circle of given center and radius using the Pythagorean
Theorem.

7634BFE3671741B88C4B941275FA2A9E.description: Translate between the geometric description and the equation for a conic section.

66C3BE90B98E4D2593F963F01AA08F72.description:
Derive using similarity the fact that the length of the arc intercepted by an angle is
proportional to the radius, and define the radian measure of the angle as the constant of proportionality; derive the formula for the area of a sector.

E6EA959FB68044C7B50356AC2988BED1.description: Find arc lengths and areas of sectors of circles.

CBBBAA591CFA42A991FEF42F9AB8B4D6.description:
Construct the inscribed and circumscribed circles of a triangle and flexibly, efficiently, and
accurately prove properties of angles for a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle.

28F8F43FCE2044C9B391F01BED96848D.description:
Identify and describe relationships among inscribed angles, radii, and chords, including
how angles formed inside the circle, the circle's radius, and line segments within the circle are
related. Understand special cases including angles formed by diameters and how the circle's edge
interacts with its radius.

D08344467246407BA937BAF93BFE3E2D.description: Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately prove that all circles are similar.

B73C4B781CB34D06852638CBE96480E3.description: Understand and apply theorems about circles.

CA77DD3568CB47D3AE5FA2AE1052DCB2.description: Use trigonometric ratios and the Pythagorean Theorem to solve right triangles in applied problems.

6280F41F84A34EB196AE2DDB5D25E342.description: Explain and use the relationship between the sine and cosine of complementary angles.

830D643891CF4F43AF743035C9EC5337.description:
Understand that by similarity, side ratios in right triangles are properties of the angles in the
triangle, leading to definitions of trigonometric ratios for acute angles.

0CA6A11287D3444ABCB8FD66B4521655.description: Define trigonometric ratios and solve problems involving right triangles.

AD08E57C2EC0471DAEEC8DFF1A4E4E47.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately use congruence and similarity criteria for triangles to solve
problems and to prove relationships in geometric figures.

32CAE548567E495B95A7CAE7F32E2CD2.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately prove theorems about triangles: proportionality, triangle
similarity, and the Pythagorean Theorem.

EB8988C6BB5C401BBE5D3EB2EEC2E2A7.description:
Use the properties of similarity transformations to establish the AA criterion for two
triangles to be similar.

00907ED0A7AA4D9882CF9975E42B3524.description:
Given two figures, use the definition of similarity in terms of similarity transformations to decide if they are similar; explain using similarity transformations the meaning of similarity for
triangles as the equality of all corresponding pairs of angles and the proportionality of all
corresponding pairs of sides.

69EC08E674174B04964179A4B6382DE7.description:
Verify experimentally the properties of dilations given by a center and a scale factor
by seeing what happens to lines affected by a center of dilation and how scale factor affects line
segments.

6275BC61D0E14438A256132CC692BCE5.description: Understand similarity in terms of similarity transformations.

78982C097C1A401CA3C9F33AB81115BA.description: Construct an equilateral triangle, a square, and a regular hexagon inscribed in a circle.

9B8619212CF84569BFDDCEFE4D80A013.description: Make formal geometric constructions with a variety of tools and methods.

51DF93E7530241EEB3B475645F23D3DB.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately prove theorems about parallelograms: congruence of
opposite sides and opposite angles, properties of diagonals.

3F16CA71C1734C9B9553D01A28EA4383.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately prove theorems about triangles: interior angles, base angles,
segments joining midpoint of two sides, and medians of a triangle.

134D69AF3FE44A77812571A611C7410A.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately prove theorems about lines and angles: vertical, transversals,
alternate interior and exterior, perpendicular bisectors, etc.

10E8702A8DB94515B97F657D335A6563.description:
Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, surface area, and
volume.

7EA75DFB0A8A4A7B826BBA4600602636.description:
Explain how the criteria for triangle congruence (ASA, SAS, and SSS) follow from the definition of
congruence in terms of rigid motions.

71CD6942CD2A4001876539A5033F3996.description:
Use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to show that two triangles are
congruent if and only if corresponding pairs of sides and corresponding pairs of angles are
congruent.

8CC23D78F72E48BBBEFC3618F907D810.description:
Use geometric descriptions of rigid motions to transform figures and to predict the effect of a
given rigid motion on a given figure; given two figures, use the definition of congruence in terms of
rigid motions to decide if they are congruent.

ED5A7F9EE6A7427A94BA6AA05E0DC591.description: Understand congruence in terms of rigid motions.

B82F1B4EDD06460AAEFA5B1E813F35DF.description:
Given a geometric figure and a rotation, reflection, or translation, draw the transformed figure
using, e.g., graph paper, tracing paper, or geometry software. Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately specify a sequence of transformations that will carry a given figure onto another.

418D9B054FA844D0897D982259DC8AC3.description:
Develop definitions of rotations, reflections, and translations in terms of angles, circles,
perpendicular lines, parallel lines, and line segments.

3E4AD738E4E94B0EB5EB817C7E2B9CD1.description:
Given a rectangle, parallelogram, trapezoid, or regular polygon, describe the rotations and
reflections that carry it onto itself.

3B7D4DD7E9E04C3388BFE86863471652.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately represent transformations in the plane, e.g., transparencies and
geometry software; describe transformations as functions that take points in the plane as inputs
and give other points as outputs. Compare transformations that preserve distance and angle to
those that do not (e.g., translation versus horizontal stretch).

6E723CFE7A6B4C62B347D8C26CAFF223.description:
Know precise definitions of angle, circle, perpendicular line, parallel line, and line segment, based
on the undefined notions of point, line, distance along a line, and distance around a circular arc.

275BF72B5A664F559514D86B8EDEBA88.description: Experiment with transformations in the plane.

FD448DA6DD1C4727A3559EAB43EDE322.description: Interpret the parameters in a linear or exponential function in terms of a context.

EF1D1C7C5AAD4FF5845F18C0C7B61021.description: Interpret expressions for functions in terms of the situation they model.

E088437475244109B8B77BA0032660B7.description:
Observe using graphs and tables that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually
exceeds a quantity increasing linearly, quadratically.

E9985CE2779948698FC45C95474CF83D.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately construct linear and exponential functions given a
graph, a description of a relationship, or two input-output pairs (include reading these from a
table).

E3A8B94B971F433B8FA34483750E4BBD.description:
Distinguish between situations that can be modeled with linear functions (equal differences over
equal intervals) and with exponential functions (equal factors over equal intervals), recognizing
constant rates per unit interval, and growth or decay by a constant percent rate per unit interval.

28ED318C63A14B3ABE477E62C92AFC79.description:
Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve
problems.

6CA58EA41BC24E47825DA2911DB1EDB8.description:
Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, k f(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for
specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Using a
variety of strategies, experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph
using technology.

C6E6AEDD63B44E1294ABA60A36E2F50B.description: Build new functions from existing functions.

2AE74F1B01A1417891E6463F6F049CE5.description:
Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively and with an explicit formula,
use them to model linear and exponential situations, and translate between two forms.

790DFDF9268C4863A4C14D865E9ED938.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately write a function that describes a relationship between two
quantities, including linear and exponential arithmetic and geometric sequences in context.

43A1563C249D4BEDACE3D58B6F500167.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.

3D57C44A11974B3485CAC2E913389760.description:
Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically,
numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions). Functions could be linear, exponential, or
quadratic.

8E83B71852484FAAA8078D11494FC0CC.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately write a function defined by an expression in different but
equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties of the function including zeros and
symmetry, using factoring for quadratic functions and integer constants for time with exponential
growth and decay.

2986DA35228A470BB2D301BC95C95F05.description:
Graph linear, exponential, and quadratic functions expressed symbolically and show key features of
the graph, including intercepts, maximum, minimum, and interpreting end behavior for exponential
functions by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.

D8FCFD68F35A4A0E840C92C8CFCEC92B.description:
Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (represented symbolically or as a
table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.

8C12C3E570234AE5A80F722D126A6578.description:
Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship
it describes in linear, exponential, or quadratic contexts.

3C1CBA4874CC44AF8A1EC15D7D0A11A6.description:
For a function that models a relationship between two quantities in context, interpret key features
of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a
verbal description of the relationship. Key features include intercepts; intervals where the function
is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries for
functions including linear, exponential, and quadratic.

4B0E85F51B4E4594B581F335EEE483BD.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context.

6367790D68D1432CA8C334BE19B963DE.description:
Recognize that sequences are functions, sometimes defined recursively, whose domain is a subset
of the integers.

CF900803CDEF4617A638085BE4F68993.description:
Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret statements that
use function notation in terms of a context.

DD66FC7416054B66A17BFFA298437F8D.description:
Understand that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range)
assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range. If 𝑓𝑓 is a function and x is
an element of its domain, then 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) denotes the output of f corresponding to the input 𝑥𝑥. The
graph of f is the graph of the equation 𝑦𝑦 = 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥).

053AA9E187D242D5B23A52832DEB1585.description: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation.

AA23A5CC877C4E0EBCAF53B8D324948F.description:
Graph the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half-plane (excluding the boundary
in the case of a strict inequality), and graph the solution set to a system of linear inequalities in two
variables as the intersection of the corresponding half-planes.

303DB4BF5F4D471CB38D1B31647C73D3.description:
Using a variety of strategies explain the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the
equations 𝑦𝑦 = 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) and 𝑦𝑦 = 𝑔𝑔(𝑥𝑥) intersect are the solutions of the equation 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) = 𝑔𝑔(𝑥𝑥); find
the solutions approximately, e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make tables of values,
or find successive approximations. Include cases where 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) and/or 𝑔𝑔(𝑥𝑥) are linear, exponential,
and quadratic.

DF4719DA78AB447CA21F3749F89F474B.description:
Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in
the coordinate plane, often forming a curve (which could be a line).

654BE737963E4C38B085EB14B9465FE4.description: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically.

4EBA5834C5C641BDA6ED4D8DFFBC51FD.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately solve a simple system consisting of a linear equation
and a quadratic equation in two variables algebraically and graphically.

B3CC104268D34597902AE29D55D314AB.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately solve systems of linear equations exactly and
approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.

7290B24C7F2D463AAE71E267213740BE.description:
Demonstrate using a variety of strategies that, given a system of two equations in two
variables, replacing one equation by the sum of that equation and a multiple of the other produces
a system with the same solutions.

74C719803E274F45A013B99A2CFB2643.description:
Solve quadratic equations in one variable by inspection, taking square roots, and
factoring as appropriate to the initial form of the equation.

56FFFD2C7C9F4E20BCB99B48249F56E9.description:
Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients
represented by letters.

40DDB6643A194762BBE5CA31B64EA6F8.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.

CC2763903A934434B6C942E92DA01A35.description:
Explain each step in solving an equation as following from the equality of numbers asserted at the
previous step flexibly, efficiently, and accurately selecting and demonstrating use of strategies to
solve equations, starting from the assumption that the original equation has a solution. Construct a
viable argument to justify a solution method.

10E9BBD0F1FA4870BCBCBC2BA15213F6.description: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning.

E671DD5B8FCF4418A7BD298C0CF75740.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the
same reasoning as in solving equations within linear, quadratic, and exponential equations.

BA54C811E6A64163AD66240B88B09B68.description:
Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities,
and interpret solutions as viable or nonviable options in a modeling context within linear,
quadratic, and exponential equations.

7747EE6645F148258A2F85FF57E896C8.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately create linear, quadratic, exponential equations to represent
relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.

9A0C9D9F125B44EDAB8638F2005475F9.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them
to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear, quadratic, and exponential functions.

9AF2D8CDE0DD490681B3CBCA30B69745.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.

D6FEDEBCD0FC47D187C82EC1D46B43F1.description:
Flexibly, efficiently, and accurately demonstrate that polynomials form a system similar
to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and
multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials.

89E27F48B6D9484D962B545742DC70FE.description: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions

7D1FD2E786D34CAC9FE0C38D85E45D57.description:

properties of the quantity represented by the expression including factoring quadratic expressions
and using properties of exponents to create equivalent forms of exponential expressions to reveal
properties of interest in the function.

functions.

quadratic functions.

choose and interpret units consistently in formulas; choose and interpret the scale and the origin in graphs and data displays.

rational number and an irrational number is irrational; and that the product of a nonzero rational
number and an irrational number is irrational.

Rewrite expressions involving radicals and rational exponents using the properties of exponents.

follows from extending the properties of integer exponents to those values using a variety of
strategies, allowing for a notation for radicals in terms of rational exponents.

C1BDFBA634334E019EF88205382122DB.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

63E741A275FE487083A57B4811EDDFC2.description: Look for and make use of structure.

F9CC7083EE4649998F9ED71E3926C9CF.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

ED207CCF88BB417C89773A4F8A80693C.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

asking new questions as understanding of the topic evolves.

4640BC3AB00B4C0F9CC1FC536BA1973C.description: Describe how language use changes over time.

illuminate the content and engage the audience and lead them through the speaker’s thinking.

reading, and/or researching the topic.

FB2006411E4C4335AF234C8FDC3315BF.description: Analyze changes in opinion and understanding.

9A65D59B1A86413B8DEA9CF0B4B6BF0E.description: Challenge ideas and conclusions based on contradictory evidence or experience.

FFAC9868602F427B9E9D6AD0678A77D0.description: Summarize points of agreement and/or disagreement.

public speaking in a variety of genres in the context of grade-level content, in person and/or digital
forums.

FB51E95658EA47669F02506C1CEE8365.description: Determine whether to share compositions given the potential permanence of published environments and the impact it may have on intended and unintended audiences and/or on the writer.

Students organize content, using, adapting, and/or breaking
the genre’s structure, to lead readers through the student’s thinking.

56221DDB6CCA4A999843F764EA38BA68.description:
Students craft introductions and conclusions within genre,
purpose, and discipline to engage the audience, establish voice, and support content in the body of
the text.

54C3BA9C9AF44590B2FE293FFA05818C.description: Attribute sources in ways consistent with the genre and discipline, using technology appropriately.

4C3D1F2CC4AA4DFB913ADABB1AB18912.description: Draft claims and support them with relevant and credible evidence connected by sound and valid reasoning.

5646F2E8EB3C4B1092410A1F14EA1B92.description: Develop analysis of experience, events, information, ideas, and/or texts.

15A2D4E7183141AE8ED01F90024B69C4.description: Develop descriptions to activate and build on the audience´s prior learning and opinions, and to help the audience to imagine and empathize with the content.

FC42F9705A2B491185AC2BBFC2756F1D.description: Students draft content within the genre, purpose, and discipline to develop ideas, engage the audience, and express voice.

8DDA96903C524B2797B62FFDF85F52C6.description: Curate ideas and material, including findings from their research (see RML11th–12th.4) and media, determining when and how it’s fair and legal to use media created by others.

CAE814972F224C8FB1651EBDDD07E91A.description: Generate topics and material from experience, imagination, reading, research (see RML11th–12th.4), media, conversations, the communicative situation, products from W11th–12th.1, and/or desire to communicate a particular message to an audience.

D19E6269532748009EB7987177AE6AAD.description: Adjust to feedback and shifts in focus and timeline when needed.

F8ED40DF19E045FA899CFC9630EF55C0.description: Students manage and complete writing projects.

9FF473B28FCB41749684D2C48D6011F7.description: Students compose multimodal texts within a variety of genres across content areas to affect an audience’s ideas, understanding, perspectives, and/or actions.

04D33CE7B68A4939B3E3F4995F98E9E2.description:
Students compose to process and reflect, respond to reading
and learning, explore and develop ideas, record observations, experiment with language and genre,

must be taken through W11–12.2 – W11–12.10.]

in the context of grade-level content, in which the development, organization, and language use
are appropriate to genre, task, purpose, and audience.

relevant textual evidence to support their analysis, evaluation, or use of texts in discussions, writing,
or presentations.

085313437AF641E1AA5E6734A4731F8E.description: Develop their own ideas, perspectives, arguments, projects, and/or plans for action in conversation with the text/s they are reading and the people with whom they are reading.

52F6EFB15DC84F4CAD36FBDE0D79DAA2.description: Students use texts they have read for purposes relevant to them.

C1804427FBC3404D8448A3DEB909EF38.description: Evaluate how well a text fulfills its stated purpose.

0489E21F84594DA7A5810ACCBDCF42AC.description: Evaluate how well a text engages the reader or provokes thought, understanding, or action.

339458D5B841483AAA8E8F3BF88C5C72.description: Evaluate how well a text effectively supports the reader to visualize and/or empathize with concepts new to them.

4F290C0E2CE54ACC87EB4ACD6FB6617D.description: Analyze how different genres, mediums, and platforms represent similar content and affect the reader differently.

D444671BD7154F84B77FAF5CF1FB2F8D.description: Analyze how two authors who write in the same genre make different choices about structure, language use, or literary techniques and explain their effects.

501D6B8D24E443C091228B512B602784.description: Analyze how figurative language and rhetorical devices affect the reader.

3CB09582DC1A4436A8A7029AE6994C53.description: Analyze how an author presents and organizes content to create effects such as mystery, tension, or surprise.

2061661D401D4C0EA0AA6F3DBAC29716.description: Analyze the particular viewpoint presented in a theme or main idea and how it develops across the whole of a text.

565C8D885269491BA2223139D8AD9B35.description: Describe what they understand from the topic or story, including how information or ideas unfold, relate, and develop.

FCD6F8BA4E0E45A08E486EB3B6F7C27B.description: Students read a wide range of self-selected texts.

7D6E15FA35C6439FA501FE05845A5471.description:
Students read, comprehend, interpret, analyze, evaluate, use, and appreciate fiction, poetry, drama,
and nonfiction texts, including those of historical and literary significance, from a broad range of
genres, cultures, and media in the context of grade-level content to understand themselves, others,
and the world.

Use a model to describe how variation in the flow of energy into and out of Earth’s systems result
in changes in climate. [Climate] [ESE]

063DF2B844C34745B5A7C2590785D745.description:
Develop a model based on evidence of Earth’s interior to describe the cycling of matter by thermal
convection.

2B243A438F9C4690ABBD279AADA1C78C.description:
Analyze geoscience data to make the claim that one change to Earth’s surface can create feedbacks
that cause changes to other Earth systems. [ESE]

058F8BC1592348C6AA08EF755A5F6DB5.description:
Develop a model to illustrate how Earth’s internal and surface processes operate at different spatial
and temporal scales to form continental and ocean-floor features.

D2EB80E5F5A845B89A4DF132AD6F16E2.description:
Develop and use models based on data and evidence to describe how changes in Earth’s internal
and surface processes, especially climate, are caused by variations in energy flow into and out of
Earth's systems at different size and time scales.

CD03B3F47CC940B2916AB23AD3EDC1B7.description:
How do the materials in and on Earth’s crust change over time? How does the
movement of tectonic plates impact the surface of Earth? How does water
influence weather, circulate in the oceans, and shape Earth’s surface? What
factors interact and influence weather? How have living organisms changed the
Earth and how have Earth’s changing conditions impacted living organisms?

76813ACDEC774C2FA4CB0729224EC806.description:
Apply scientific reasoning and evidence from ancient Earth materials, meteorites, and other
planetary surfaces to construct an account of Earth’s formation and early history.

7B309124EC4A49778E8FAA5EBBBF9C56.description:
Evaluate evidence of the past and current movements of continental and oceanic crust and the
theory of plate tectonics to explain the ages of crustal rocks.

9BED7EC2E2C44F4188B2D751600DEC17.description:
Use mathematical or computational representations to predict the motion of orbiting objects in the
solar system.

3D62033D6F244319B583FA408524C55E.description: Communicate scientific ideas about the way stars, over their life cycle, produce elements.

21EC117D58A84FB1A102AB80C0299F5F.description:
Construct an explanation of the Big Bang theory based on astronomical evidence of light spectra,
motion of distant galaxies, and composition of matter in the universe.

A744C77423B14EA486F40F5C8DCC4FF1.description:
Develop a model based on evidence to illustrate the life span of the sun and the role of nuclear
fusion in the sun’s core to release energy in the form of radiation.

C1C34085169E440D96498A07580B4499.description:
Use mathematical and computational thinking to qualitatively predict the motion of objects in the
solar system, describe that the processes and elements produced within stars depend on the mass
and age of the star, and apply evidence to construct an account of Earth’s formation and early
history.

1E0E3A238B85455381773D6C14B86440.description:
What is Earth’s place in the Universe? What makes up our solar system and
how can the motion of Earth explain seasons and eclipses? How do people
figure out that the Earth and life on Earth have changed through time?

EBEB3CC9ADB74E4D918232A9D0C8B741.description:
Use a computer simulation to model the impact of proposed solutions to a complex real-world
problem with numerous criteria and constraints on interactions within and between systems
relevant to the problem. [Climate] [ESE]

938B89E6F38041D19215347951E89D65.description:
Evaluate a solution to a complex real-world problem based on prioritized criteria and trade-offs
that account for a range of constraints, including cost, safety, reliability, and aesthetics as well as
possible social, cultural, and environmental impacts. [Climate] [ESE]

1701F8D72D434D66A13F3213DFDA1176.description:
Design a solution to a complex real-world problem by breaking it down into smaller, more
manageable problems that can be solved through engineering. [Climate] [ESE]

0A9D2BF96052472BA6643EC75941B599.description:
Analyze a major global challenge to specify qualitative and quantitative criteria and constraints for
solutions that account for societal needs and wants. [Climate] [ESE]

FEA9E9A8DB3047D898EEC0CDD39217D3.description:
Use modeling, investigation, and data to design, evaluate, and refine solutions to complex
problems that can be solved through engineering; consider real-world criteria such as social,
cultural, and environmental impacts in addition to constraints such as safety and reliability.

document.title: Public Draft WA Learning Standards Science

91A89307C6584F41812378B2203E4EA0.description:
Conduct a project that specifies a local influence on a global environmental problem, identifies
solution paths, takes steps to solve the problem, and reports results to demonstrate the
knowledge, attitudes, and understanding of personal and civic responsibility required to ensure
environmental justice and sustainable communities.

E8175F614460454694721CF520CF65AF.description:
Engage in place-based inquiry to gather, analyze, and evaluate information, modeling connections
that explain one or more ways that humans can support natural and human-built environments for
environmental sustainability or climate change resiliency.

41E1B09C0341411F86B0D877671CFCE8.description:
Apply understanding of ecological, social, and economic systems to develop and communicate
solutions for environmental issues at local, regional, national, tribal, and global scales.

4B9A011048A9440293F7707898B6EE42.description:
Engage in place-based learning to understand how the natural world, urban systems, and the
economy interact, and through project-based learning, identify and address environmental
problems to support equitable and sustainable systems in scales from local to global.

4C64790B72A548838BA189A9ECDC552C.description:
How can humans work with nature to design sustainable systems that benefit
the environment, economy, and society for factors like public health, access to
nature, and future access to natural resources?
